    re-reading each of the 4 current sites individually (not assumed from stale line numbers) found
    only 3 are genuine duplicates of `RANGE_GATED_STRATEGIES` — the range-model confidence override,
    the neutral-only filter that must agree with it, and the first-hour confidence gate. The 4th
    (`orchestrator.py:1137`, `("iron_condor", "short_strangle", "long_straddle")`) is a DIFFERENT,
    correctly-scoped concept: a direction-inference exemption for drift tracking (long_straddle
    belongs there because it buys both a call and a put, not because it is range-gated — folding it
    into `RANGE_GATED_STRATEGIES` would have been semantically wrong, not a fix). That site is also
    the flagship offender in the getsource census (`test_r17_dormant_strategy_fixes.py:97`, whose
    own docstring says "ties the test to the actual source, not a re-derived literal") — left for
    that track, not touched here.
    The 3 real sites now reference `RANGE_GATED_STRATEGIES`. TESTING NOTE: this is a zero-logic-
    change substitution — the literal and the named constant were already identical in membership,
    so there is no CURRENT behavior to observe; the entire risk is FUTURE drift. Proportionate
    coverage is a STRUCTURAL AST guard (same category as W38's SQL-function guard and W28's
    `.today()` guard — a legitimate structural check, not the source-string-as-behavior-proxy
    pattern the house rules forbid), not a forced behavioral drive of `_scan_symbol`/`_try_execute`
    for a change with no behavior to differ. Run against the untouched pre-fix file: the guard
    finds bare duplicates at exactly the 3 lines fixed, nothing else.

[3] `fail-direction-10` — RE-PROBED, SCOPE NARROWED DELIBERATELY. The residual named in the
    2026-09-21 roadmap entry was real: `circuit_breaker.py`'s READ-side fail-closed behavior
    (W14's `_state_unreadable`, W32's `_maybe_reload` re-read) is intact, but the WRITE-side
    failure path — `_persist()`'s own `except` around `state.set_state(...)` — was untouched by
    either wave. It logged a warning and moved on; nothing anywhere could observe that a write had
    failed, so a crash before the next successful persist could still lose an active trip exactly
    like `regress-live-04` did before W14, just from the opposite direction (a failing write
    instead of a failing read).
    Reproduced pre-fix: a `CircuitBreaker` whose store's `set_state` raises records a loss, and
    `get_status()` afterward carries no trace at all — the field this wave adds did not exist.
    Fixed: severity bumped `log.warning` -> `log.error`, and a `store_write_healthy` field added to
    `CircuitBreakerStatus`, cleared on the next successful persist (mirroring how `_state_unreadable`
    clears on the next successful read) rather than needing a separate retry queue — `_persist()`
    already runs again on its own the next time any state-changing method calls it.
    DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: full paging. `CircuitBreaker` has no `_notify_cb`, unlike
    `PortfolioManager`/`AccountManager` (wired in `TradingOrchestrator.__init__`), and `_persist()`
    is sync, so an async notify call cannot be added to it without a larger design (async wiring
    through a sync method, or a new consumer that polls `get_status()`). Building that now would
    have been real scope creep past this wave's budget for one narrow, now-visible-not-invisible
    gap. Registered as the residual, not claimed as closed.

[4] `money-flow-01` — RE-PROBED AND RETIRED. NOT a fix; a full trace of the real call graph shows
    the finding's own claim ("the reconciler books real P&L via `state.close_trade` only — zero
    `update_daily_stats`/`record_trade_result`/PDT/commission true-up") is false at HEAD, and has
    been false since W1: `close_trade()` (`state.py:462-472`) enqueues into `exit_outbox` in the
    SAME transaction as the close, for every caller including the reconciler — the code comment
    there names exactly this ("no matter which path — executor callback, reconciler, sweep,
    crash-recovery drain — discovers it"). `_drain_exit_outbox()` (`orchestrator.py:800+`) claims
    the row, filters non-real closes, trues up commission, buckets by session (W37), books stats
    and the breaker in one transaction (`_book_exit_core`, W32's exactly-once), records PDT when
    the entry was also same-day, and records Thompson.
    Every piece the finding names as missing is present, wired, and — this is the load-bearing
    fact — ALREADY TESTED: `tests/test_w1_booking_integrity.py::TestDrainBooksOrphanCloses::
    test_reconciler_style_close_reaches_breaker_and_stats` seeds a trade, calls `close_trade()`

## 2026-09-21 - W44: fail-direction-03 + concurrency-4 — earnings fail-open gates, one root cause

Planned in full via EnterPlanMode before any code (Context / Approach / Files / Tests /
Verification / PLAN.md sections), approved, then implemented exactly as planned with one
mid-implementation correction (finding 3 below). Re-verified against HEAD before writing anything,
per the discipline every wave since W41 has needed — the pre-scoping note above held up, plus one
new discovery that changed the fix design (finding 3).

**1. `fail-direction-03`** — `EarningsCalendar` (`src/ait/data/earnings.py`) built the IDENTICAL
`EarningsInfo(next_earnings_date=None)` shape whether a symbol genuinely has no upcoming earnings
(every ETF in the live universe) or the Yahoo fetch broke, and cached either one for the full
6-hour TTL. Both gates (`is_near_earnings`, `would_hold_through_earnings`) then read "no date" as
"allow" — a fetch outage silently removed earnings protection for up to 6h, and the outage was
invisible (the `_bg` failure log was `log.debug`, and nothing paged).

**2. `concurrency-4`** — `TTLCache` (`src/ait/data/cache.py`) had no lock, while `earnings.py` is
the one `src/ait/data/` consumer that writes into a cache instance from a background thread
(`get_next_earnings`'s cold-miss-inside-a-running-loop path) concurrently with the main thread's
own reads/writes of the SAME instance. `concurrency-4` is the mechanism that makes
`fail-direction-03`'s fail-open reachable — not a separately-sequenced finding.

**3. Design correction found during planning, not sketched in the original roadmap**: the live
universe is ETF-only (`config.yaml:19`, `[SPY, QQQ, IWM]`, per the operator's 2026-07-22 decision
at `config.yaml:15-18` taken specifically to avoid single-name earnings gaps) — a blunt "unknown ⇒
refuse" would have refused 100% of entries forever, since ETFs have no earnings. Checked live
against yfinance before choosing a fix: `SPY`/`QQQ`/`IWM` return an **empty dict** from
`ticker.calendar` (yfinance swallows Yahoo's 404 internally, does not raise); `AAPL` returns a
populated dict with a real `Earnings Date` key. So confirmed-absence and fetch-failure are already
distinguishable today — the code just built the same shape for both. Operator decision (this
session, via AskUserQuestion): **last-known-good-aware fail-closed** — an unknown answer refuses
new entries UNLESS the most recent successful fetch is still fresh, in which case that answer
(which for every ETF today says "no earnings") is reused. This closes the finding for real
(single-name protection) at zero cost to the current universe, unlike a VIX-style blunt
fail-closed, which would halt all entries during a Yahoo-wide outage regardless of whether the
traded symbols have any earnings risk at all.

PROOF (pre-fix reproductions, run against HEAD before any change):
- `EarningsInfo` had no way to distinguish the two cases — confirmed by reading `_fetch_earnings`
  (`earnings.py:189-194` pre-fix): both the "no data found" return and the `except Exception`
  return built `EarningsInfo(symbol=symbol, next_earnings_date=None)`, byte-identical.
- `TTLCache` race: a 6-thread stress test (`set()`/`get()` in a tight loop against a shared
  instance, `max_size=8` to force every `set()` through the eviction path, `sys.setswitchinterval
  (1e-6)` to maximize GIL handoff frequency) reliably reproduced `RuntimeError: dictionary changed
  size during iteration` / `RuntimeError: dictionary keys changed during iteration` plus
  consequential `KeyError`s, in 3/3 runs against the unlocked cache. A single precisely-timed
  interleaving (spawn one interloper thread, sleep, evict) was tried FIRST and did NOT reproduce
  reliably — the unlocked interloper thread simply raced to completion inside the pause window
  rather than landing mid-iteration; replaced with the stress design before it went in the suite.
- Third earnings-gate consumer confirmed (not previously cited before this session):
  `execution/portfolio.py:769`, the exit-side "IV crush pre-close" check, wrapped in a bare
  `except Exception: pass` (`:780-781` pre-fix) — a persistent failure there was completely silent.

Fix (`src/ait/data/cache.py`, `src/ait/data/earnings.py`, `src/ait/config/settings.py`,
`config.yaml`, `src/ait/bot/orchestrator.py`, `src/ait/execution/portfolio.py` — 232
insertions/39 deletions across the 6 files):
- `TTLCache` gained a `threading.RLock` (reentrant: `set()` calls `_evict_expired()` while already
  holding it). `get()` reads under the lock, does the pandas `.copy()` after releasing (unchanged
  hold-time discipline for the `options_chain`/`market_data` consumers). Eviction/expiry semantics
  unchanged — `tests/test_cache.py` untouched and still green.
- `EarningsInfo` gained `data_available: bool = True`. False only from the `_fetch_earnings`
  exception path and the async cold-miss placeholder; the "no data found" path keeps the default
  True — a confirmed absence is a real answer.
- `EarningsCalendar` gained `self._last_good: dict[symbol -> (EarningsInfo, fetched_at)]`,
  independent of the TTL cache so a later failure can fall back to it. `_remember()` only ever
  caches a `data_available=True` result — a failure can no longer poison the 6h cache. `_unavail
  able()` serves the LKG if within `lkg_max_age_hours`, else returns the unknown sentinel. Applied
  uniformly to BOTH the async and sync call branches (an implementation gap found while writing
  tests: the sync branch originally returned the raw failed fetch directly, bypassing LKG entirely
  — fixed before it shipped, so "sync callers fetch inline" no longer means "sync callers skip the
  LKG policy").
- New `EarningsConfig` (`settings.py`, house pattern: `Field(...)` + `description=` recording why)
  and `config.yaml` `earnings:` section: `refuse_entries_when_data_unavailable: true` (the
  operator's escape hatch — flip to restore pre-W44 always-allow with no deploy),
  `lkg_max_age_hours: 168`, plus `buffer_days_before`/`buffer_days_after` relocated from
  `EarningsCalendar`'s bare constructor defaults (pure move, semantics pinned by existing +
  new tests). `orchestrator.py`'s `EarningsCalendar()` construction now threads all four through.
- Both entry gates (`orchestrator.py` — `is_near_earnings` call in `_scan_symbol`,

## 2026-09-21 - W45: bot-day-05 + bot-day-08 — reconciler/exit-path crash safety

Planned in full via EnterPlanMode before any code, approved, then re-derived mid-implementation
where the research (two parallel Explore agents plus direct reads of every touched function) turned
up a materially better fix shape than the original 2026-08-25 audit's own suggested fix for
bot-day-05, and a simpler, more test-compatible shape than this session's own first plan for
bot-day-08. Both findings from `reports/blindspot_composition_hunt_20260825.md`, re-confirmed
still-open in the 2026-09-06 R24 audit; neither had been re-verified against HEAD before this
session.

**1. `bot-day-05`** — `_execute_exit` (`src/ait/bot/orchestrator.py`) placed the closing broker
order BEFORE CASing the trade to `CLOSING` and before `register_exit_order`. A hard kill in that
window left a live, working exit order with the DB row still reading `FILLED` — every recovery
layer missed it (reconciler's working-order fetch gated on the trade already being `CLOSING`; the
fast monitor's `_pending_exit_orders` skip-set in-memory-only, empty after restart) — so
`portfolio.check_positions` re-demanded the exit and `_execute_exit` fired again: a second reverse
combo, either a reversed book or an untracked inverse position. The single most dangerous item in
the current roadmap batch — a reversal, not a reporting bug.

**2. `bot-day-08`** — the stale-PENDING sweep's entry-order cancel check
(`_cancel_working_entry_order`, `src/ait/execution/reconciler.py`) was supposed to see a pre-crash
entry order still working at the broker under a different (pre-restart) clientId, so it wouldn't
wrongly book a $0 "never filled" close while the order could still fill. Its own docstring claimed
this worked because `ib.openTrades()` is "same-clientId orders only" — false: verified directly
against the actually-installed `ib_insync==0.9.86` that `Wrapper.openOrder` caches every clientId
unconditionally and `openTrades()` applies no clientId filter at all. The protection was real but
only as an undocumented side effect of a third-party library cache — and this session's research
found it isn't even reliably true: a disconnect wipes that cache entirely, and on a **same**-clientId
reconnect (not just a fallback) the stash re-fetch never re-fires, so the accidental protection
evaporates on an ordinary reconnect, not just the fallback-clientId scenario the finding named.

PROOF (pre-fix reproductions and mutation checks, both via `git stash push -- <file>` / pop, not a
hand-revert):
- bot-day-05: with the fix stashed out, 4 of 6 targeted tests correctly failed —
  `AttributeError: 'TradingOrchestrator' object has no attribute '_cas_to_closing'` on the tests
  calling it directly, and the two CAS-observed-before-place tests failing because the CAS had
  reverted to happening after placement. The 2 that stayed green
  (`test_no_order_paths_never_cas_and_never_place`,
  `test_buy_to_close_no_quote_defers_without_touching_status`) are legitimate controls: a path that
  never places an order never reached the CAS either way, old or new ordering.
- bot-day-08: with the fix stashed out, 3 of 5 targeted tests correctly failed — Pass 3 didn't
  exist, so the foreign-stash-aware defer and the periodic-prune tests both failed. The 2 that
  stayed green (empty-stash-books-$0, failed-snapshot-leaves-stash-untouched) are legitimate
  controls for the same reason.

Fix (`src/ait/bot/orchestrator.py`, `src/ait/execution/reconciler.py`, `src/ait/broker/ibkr_client.py`
comment-only, `pyproject.toml` — 174 insertions/36 deletions across the 4 source files, plus 4 test
files updated for fixture gaps the fix exposed):

- **bot-day-05.** The original audit's suggested fix (move the CAS earlier in `_execute_exit`,
  before calling the builders) was read directly and rejected: `_close_multi_leg` polls for a quote
  with `for _ in range(5): await asyncio.sleep(0.5)` — up to 2.5s of real waiting, on every
  multi-leg exit attempt, successful or not, before it ever reaches `place_order`. CASing that early
  would make a perfectly healthy position invisible to `portfolio.check_positions` (FILLED/PARTIAL
  only) for up to 2.5s on every routine exit, not just at crash time. Instead: new
  `_cas_to_closing(trade)` helper, called on the line immediately before each of the 3 real
  `place_order` call sites (two in `_close_single_leg`, one in `_close_multi_leg`) — every
  defer/no-quote/qualification-failure path in both functions already `return`s `None` *before*
  reaching its function's placement line, so **no revert-on-failure logic was needed anywhere**: a
  path that never CASes never needs to un-CAS. The old post-placement CAS block in `_execute_exit`
  (including its "race window only... cancel it" cleanup, which only existed because the order used
  to be placed *before* that point) was deleted as dead code, not relocated. No new persisted
  "pending-exit intent" record either — the `CLOSING` write itself is the persisted intent, already
  exactly the signal `reconciler.py`'s existing working-order-promotion recovery (`:1128-1170` in
  session line numbers, unchanged) keys off; that net just never observed a crash in this window
  before because the write didn't exist there yet.
- **bot-day-08.** `sweep_stale_pending()` (the async wrapper) now also fetches
  `IBKRClient.get_all_open_order_ids()` (authoritative, all-clientId, already existed for the
  CLOSING-recovery path, just never wired here) and feeds it to `prune_foreign_open_orders()`
  (already existed too) before the sweep runs, keeping `foreign_open_order_ids` accurate over time.
  `_cancel_working_entry_order` gained a new Pass 3: if Pass 1/2 find nothing in the local
  `openTrades()` cache, defer (don't book $0) whenever `foreign_open_order_ids` is non-empty.
  **Design correction made mid-implementation**: the original plan threaded a `broker_open_ids`
  parameter through `_cancel_working_entry_order` explicitly — found, before writing any tests, that
  this would break two existing test monkeypatches (`lambda tr: False`, single-arg) in
  `tests/test_r19_state_ml_fixes.py` and `tests/test_w26_budget_and_cluster_cooldown.py`. Redesigned
  to have Pass 3 read `self._ibkr.foreign_open_order_ids` directly instead — simpler, doesn't touch
  the function's call signature at all, and the periodic prune keeps the stash accurate whether or
  not a given call happened to run with a fresh snapshot (the 30s hot path, which cannot afford a
  `reqAllOpenOrdersAsync` round-trip every tick, just checks whatever the last successful prune
  left — slightly stale at worst, never fabricated). Deliberately pass-wide, not per-trade-precise:
  `get_all_open_order_ids()` returns bare order ids with no symbol/orderRef, and `TradeRecord` has no
  persisted entry-order-id column to match against (the `executions.order_id` column only populates
  on an actual fill) — a coarser "defer every stale-PENDING candidate this pass" gate needs no schema
  change and is strictly safer.
- Corrected the false "same-clientId orders only" / "invisible to ib.trades()/openTrades()"
  docstring claims in both files (comment-only, zero behavior change).
- Addendum found during research, not part of either original finding: `pyproject.toml` pinned
  `ib_insync` to `==0.9.86` (was `>=0.9.86`) — matches what `constraints.txt` already pins for the
  trading box; an unpinned bound let a bare `pip install -e ".[dev]"` silently pull a newer
  `ib_insync` whose cache behavior differs, re-opening bot-day-08's blind spot from a different
  angle.

Four existing test fixtures needed small, targeted updates — each a genuine gap in a lightweight
orchestrator/reconciler stand-in that predated this wave's new code paths, not a problem with the
fix itself, confirmed by running before changing:
- `tests/test_r19_state_ml_fixes.py`'s shared `_reconciler()` helper built `_ibkr = MagicMock()`
  with no `foreign_open_order_ids` — an unconfigured MagicMock attribute is truthy by default (even
  though it iterates as empty), so Pass 3 spuriously deferred on every call. Added
  `rec._ibkr.foreign_open_order_ids = set()`, matching the real `IBKRClient`'s own always-initialized
  shape.
- `tests/test_exit_order_safety.py`'s `_orchestrator()` and `tests/test_r14_batch2.py`'s
  `_single_leg_orch()` built a bare `TradingOrchestrator.__new__(...)` with no `_state` at all (never
  needed before, since the CAS used to live in `_execute_exit`, not the builders these helpers
  exercise directly) — added `orch._state = MagicMock()` to both.
- `tests/test_w33_exit_pricing_corrective.py`'s `_Store` stand-in (deliberately minimal, "the three
  state calls exit pricing makes") gained a fourth: `update_trade_status`, returning `True`.
- `tests/test_exit_order_safety.py::TestExecuteExitLivenessGate::test_unknown_liveness_proceeds` —
  a genuine test-semantics update, not a workaround: it asserted `state.update_trade_status.
  assert_called_once()`, which was a correct proxy for "the exit proceeded" when `_execute_exit`
  itself called it, but that responsibility moved into the (here, mocked-out) builder. Removed the
  now-stale assertion; `close.assert_called_once()` alone is already the complete proof, matching how
  the sibling `test_live_at_broker_proceeds` was already asserting.

VERIFICATION:
- `python -m compileall -q src` / `python scripts/typecheck.py` clean throughout (re-run after every
  edit round, not just once at the end).
- New file `tests/test_w45_exit_cas_and_sweep_safety.py`, 11 tests: multi-leg and both single-leg

## 2026-09-21 - W34b EXECUTED (Windows box) — W34's Gateway recovery FAILED its first live use; one launcher now, and its output is kept

NUMBERING: W41-W51 are Ahmed's roadmap, so this corrective to W34 is labelled W34b rather than
taking a number from his range.

WHAT HAPPENED (2026-09-20, Sunday; market closed; QQQ condor open). Windows System log first, then
`logs/orchestrator.log`:
  19:05:09  System 1074  power off requested from the Start menu (user `prith`)
  19:06:15  System 1073  "The attempt by user prith to restart/shutdown computer failed" — the
                         power-off was ABORTED, but it had already closed the Gateway's window
  19:08:49  gateway_down_while_bot_running port=4002 down_seconds=0        <- W34's new check, live
  19:20:49  gateway_recovery_attempt attempt=1 down_minutes=12 wedged_process=False jvm_pids=[]
  19:52:49  gateway_recovery_attempt attempt=2 down_minutes=44 wedged_process=False jvm_pids=[]
  20:22:49  gateway_recovery_attempt attempt=3 down_minutes=74 wedged_process=False jvm_pids=[]
  ...       gateway_down_while_bot_running every 2 min (94 lines) until 22:14:49 down_seconds=11160
  22:16:09  System 6006  the box shut down for the night
So the OUTAGE has a known cause — an aborted Windows power-off took the Gateway with it while the
python processes survived, the same shape as the 09-17 closed-window incident. The aborted
shutdown ended at 19:06, fourteen minutes BEFORE the first relaunch, so it does not by itself
explain why the relaunches failed.
DETECTION, COOLDOWN AND BUDGET ALL BEHAVED AS DESIGNED. THE RELAUNCH DID NOT: three launches, and
30 minutes after each one there was no Gateway JVM at all and the port was still closed. Had this
been a weekday the bot would have been blind for the rest of the session.

WHY IT FAILED IS NOT KNOWN — and that is the second defect. The launcher ran with
`stdout=DEVNULL`, and IBC overwrites `C:\IBC\Logs\IBC-3.19.0_GATEWAY-1044_.txt` on every start
(its weekday-suffixed names stopped after the Windows 11 upgrade changed the `%DATE%` format), so
Monday's 08:33 boot erased the only evidence. I will not guess at a cause.

WHAT IS KNOWN: there were TWO launch shapes (R26
`gateway-start-script-has-two-env-authorities-and-two-launch-shapes`). BOOT —
`gateway.start_gateway_ibc`: `[script, "/INLINE"]`, cwd=IBC_DIR, CREATE_NO_WINDOW — has worked at
every bot start, including 08:33 the next morning on the same install. RECOVERY —
`Popen([script], shell=True, stdout=DEVNULL)` — takes `StartGateway.bat`'s OTHER branch
(`start "<title>" ... DisplayBannerAndLaunch.bat`, a new console window) and is 0 for 3. W35
unified the script PATH and I left the SHAPE alone on purpose, writing that it "has a successful
production run (09-11)". One good run against three bad ones: that call was wrong.

THE FIX: `gateway.launch_ibc_gateway(script, log_dir)` is the one launcher. Boot and recovery both
call it, so they cannot drift again; it uses the boot shape; and it writes the launcher's output to
`logs/gateway_launch_<timestamp>.log` (with `/INLINE` the script runs IBC inside that child, so its
banner and any login failure land in the file). `master.start()` passes the same log dir to the
boot path. `tests/conftest.py` now also fences `master.LOGS_DIR` to tmp_path — older supervisor
tests drive the recovery with a mocked Popen and the REAL log dir, and would each have left a
launcher log in the live box's `logs/`.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE: that recovery will now succeed. It proves recovery uses the shape that
boots, and that the next failure will say why. If Sunday's cause was not the launch shape (an IBKR
weekend login window, a dialog IBC could not answer), the next outage will show it in
`gateway_launch_*.log` instead of leaving nothing.

ALSO VALIDATED HERE, per the "whoever ships runs it on the Windows box" rule: Ahmed's ten weekend
commits (W31, W38-W44, `d7350a3..dcb86a7`) — full fast lane on this box **2201 passed / 46 skipped /
0 failed**, typecheck OK, before anything of mine was applied on top.

PROOF. `tests/test_w34b_gateway_recovery_launch.py`, 5 executing tests. Pre-fix: **3 failed / 2
passed** (the two greens are the boot-path controls). One of the three is a real `.bat` run with no
mocks: a launcher that prints "IBC: login failed - existing session detected" and exits 1 now leaves
that text, and `arg1=/INLINE`, in `logs/gateway_launch_*.log`. One older test stubbed
`ensure_gateway` as `lambda port:` and was widened to accept the new `log_dir` keyword.

VERIFICATION: full fast lane in the dev worktree **2206 passed / 46 skipped / 0 failed** (384s),
typecheck OK, zero launcher logs leaked into `logs/`.

STATE AT HANDOFF: committed, fast-forwarded into the live tree (together with Ahmed's ten commits)
and pushed. NOT running: the supervisor started at 08:33 ET holds the old launch shape, and with the
QQQ condor in an active touch-stop exit this morning nothing is being restarted. It loads at the
next start.

## 2026-09-21 - W33b EXECUTED (Windows box) — the first live exit on W33: what worked, what did not, and the fix. Trade closed -$503.32

THE TRADE. QQQ iron condor T-20260917-095601-aa4fa8 (645P/691P/734C/775C, exp 10-02, credit 4.99,
1 lot) closed on its touch stop. QQQ gapped from 721.33 (Fri close) to 728 at the open and ran
through the 734 short call. Closed 9.94 -> gross -$495.00, real commission $8.32 over 10 fills,
**realized -$503.32**. First close on W32-W37, and first live exercise of W33's exit pricing.

THE FUNDAMENTAL CONSTRAINT, STATED FIRST: **this account prices everything off DELAYED data** —
`market_data_type_set type=4`, and IBKR warning 10167 ("Displaying delayed market data") on QQQ
stock AND on the exit BAG itself. Quotes are ~15 minutes old (U6: the live account is still
unfunded, so there is no real-time entitlement). The touch stop itself fired ~15 minutes after the
real touch, and every exit limit below was built from a 15-minute-old combo quote in a rising tape.

THE EXIT, FROM THE LOGS AND A READ-ONLY BROKER CLIENT (clientId 83, placed and cancelled nothing):
  10:25:02  short_strike_touch (spot 734.55 >= call 734.00)
  10:25:04  combo_exit_quote_poll bag=8.46/8.57 -> BUY LMT 8.67
            broker: order 1897552 Submitted, filled=0 — worked ELEVEN minutes unfilled
  10:36:08  exit_order_stale_working_cancel_requested age_seconds=664 (the rule is 300s; scan
            cycles held the event loop, heartbeat stale 6.5 min — the R9 "monitor blind while
            scanning" finding, live)
  10:37:10  bag=9.50/9.66 -> BUY LMT 9.76; broker: Submitted, filled=0 — twelve more minutes
  10:49:04  cancel requested age_seconds=714
  10:50:06  bag=10.09/10.19 -> BUY LMT 10.29 -> **FILLED 9.94** at 10:50:08 (QQQ had eased to
            734.96, so the real market was BELOW the stale quote — a limit fills at the offer, not
            at our number)
25 minutes from trigger to fill. Marked at the first attempt's quote the loss was ~-$360; it
closed at -$503. About $140 of that is the cost of chasing a trending market with stale prices.

WHAT WORKED (each live for the first time): W33's `combo_exit_quote_poll` answered "what did the
BAG show?" on every attempt without a probe; `ibkr_order_error_captured` recorded each of our own
cancels (code 202, empty reason — no band reject occurred, so no `exit_band_*` key was written,
correctly); W32 booked the close EXACTLY once (daily_stats -503.32 / 0W 1L; breaker
consecutive_losses=1, daily_pnl=-503.32; outbox empty); W37's remembered estimate was used by the
true-up and its key deleted (`realized_pnl_commission_trueup`, ledger complete at 10 executions);
the broker is flat — no open orders, no QQQ option positions.

WHAT DID NOT, AND IS MINE. W33 taught the NO-QUOTE exit to step its price each attempt and left the
QUOTED path at `ask + cross`, reasoning that a limit through a live ask fills. On delayed data that
reasoning does not hold, and the quoted path had no memory: attempt two started from the next stale
quote as if attempt one had never failed. FIX: every consecutive unfilled QUOTED placement for the
same trade raises the next limit by `exit.exit_unfilled_escalation_pct` (0.05) of the marketable
price — n-th retry: x(1 + pct*n). Credit buybacks only (a price we PAY; a debit close is never
pushed upward — tested); the wing-width cap, the mark-anchored ceiling and the broker band all still
bind (tested); the counter clears when the exit completes or after an hour. Replayed on this
morning's numbers the second attempt is 10.25, not 9.76.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX: (1) the 15-minute delay itself — only funding the live account does. How
the $140 splits between the delay and the missing escalation cannot be measured from delayed
data, so it is not claimed here; (2) the 300s rest before a re-price, which scan
cycles stretched to 11-12 minutes. A shorter window for STOP exits and moving scans off the event
loop are both real and both bigger than a same-day corrective; registered, not done.

PROOF. `tests/test_w33b_quoted_exit_escalation.py`, 7 executing tests through the real

## 2026-09-21 - W46: bot-day-03 + bot-day-04 — startup hang/protection-arming, one root cause

Planned in full via EnterPlanMode before any code, approved. Two research passes plus direct reads
of every touched function turned up two things neither the original 2026-08-25 audit nor the
2026-09-06 R24 re-confirmation anticipated, both of which materially shrank this wave's actual
diff versus the roadmap's own sketch. Also closes `ops-substrate-03` (R24 meta-finding: W6 was
declared complete without fixing either of these two — the ledger-visibility half was already
fixed by the 2026-09-21 REGISTER CORRECTION entry; this closes the underlying code half).

**1. `bot-day-04`** — `run()` (`src/ait/bot/orchestrator.py:590`) awaited
`self._trainer.ensure_models_ready(...)` synchronously (up to ~110s-7.5min per `trainer.py`'s own
R9 comment, whenever the 7-day retrain interval lapsed / an artifact was missing / spec mismatch /
drift) BEFORE the startup reconcile, exit-order re-adoption, and the trading loop — leaving the
book with zero working loss exits for the whole training window (`AIT_CREDIT_LOSS_LIMIT` defaults
to `0` → `effective_stop=-999`, confirmed unchanged, so the touch stop is the only credit loss
exit and it only runs inside the trading loop). `_pre_market()` had an independent second call to
the same blocking method.

**2. `bot-day-03`** — `master.py`'s `health_check()` hang branch (`:995-1006` at the time of
research) kills+relaunches the bot whenever the market is open and `data/bot_heartbeat` is >15 min
stale, with zero startup grace (`self._last_restart`, set only in `start()`, was never read here)
and zero restart-budget interaction (its own `return` skipped past all of `_restarts`/
`_max_restarts`). So a boot slower than 15 minutes — which `bot-day-04` alone could cause — got
killed on the very tick that would have written the first fresh heartbeat, and the retry repeated
the same slow boot: killed again next tick, forever, un-escalated, with the "BOT HUNG... restarting"
page firing unthrottled on every cycle.

**Two things found only by reading the current code, not by trusting either audit's suggested
fix:**
- `bot-day-04`'s entry-gating half needed no new code. `DirectionPredictor.predict`
  (`src/ait/ml/ensemble.py:141-147`) and `RangePredictor.predict` already return `None` when
  untrained, and `_scan_symbol` (`orchestrator.py`) already treats a `None` prediction as
  skip-this-symbol — the identical shape to the existing `fail-direction-02` gate for the range
  predictor. Exits don't consult these predictors at all. Proven by execution (this wave's test 3
  drives a real scan against an untrained predictor and confirms no order reaches the executor),
  not asserted from reading.
- `bot-day-03`'s exact grace/cooldown/budget/escalate shape already existed in `master.py`, for a
  different purpose: `_maybe_recover_gateway` (`:658-783`), including its own W34-documented
  ordering lesson — the budget counter must move *after* a real attempt, not before, so a
  kill/launch that raises doesn't still spend budget. The hang-branch fix mirrors that lesson
  directly: `self._restarts += 1` sits after `self.stop(); self.start()` with no wrapping
  try/except, so a raise propagates to the branch's own existing outer handler and the increment
  is simply never reached.

PROOF (pre-fix reproductions via `git stash push -- <file>` / pop, mutation-checking every
behavioral claim, not a hand-revert):
- `bot-day-04`: with the fix stashed out, 2 of 3 non-hanging targeted tests correctly failed
  (`AttributeError: no attribute '_launch_background_training'`); the 3rd (the untrained-predictor
  control) correctly stayed green, since it exercises pre-existing, unchanged behavior. The 4th
  test — driving the real `run()` with a mocked, gate-blocked `ensure_models_ready` — didn't fail
  cleanly against the reverted code, it **hung**: pre-fix, `run()` genuinely awaits training
  directly, so with the gate never set until after `await orch.run()` returns, it never returns.
  Arguably stronger evidence than a clean red — a live catastrophic version of exactly the
  "unmanaged for the whole training window" consequence the finding describes. Stopped the stuck
  run rather than wait it out; restored the fix, all 4 green again.
- `bot-day-03`: with the fix stashed out, all 5 targeted tests correctly failed — 3 with
  `AttributeError: no attribute 'BOT_RESTART_GRACE_S'`, 1 on the grace-skip assertion, and 1
  (`test_never_restarted_by_this_supervisor_gets_no_grace`) on its `_restarts == 1` half
  specifically — its `calls == ["stop", "start"]` half correctly stayed green (matching the
  pre-existing, still-unconditional kill for `_last_restart is None`), confirming that test
  exercises one old invariant and one new one, precisely as designed.

Fix (`src/ait/bot/orchestrator.py`, `src/ait/orchestration/master.py`, plus two existing test
fixtures — 210 insertions/8 deletions across the 4 changed files):
- `orchestrator.py`: new `_launch_background_training()`, guarded against double-launch (both
  `run()`'s startup call and `_pre_market()`'s call reach it in one boot) and against relaunching
  once `self._models_ready` is already `True`. Wraps `ensure_models_ready` in a fire-and-forget
  `asyncio.create_task`, never lets an exception escape the task (logged, not raised — must never
  kill the startup sequence). Both former blocking call sites replaced.
  **Explicit scope boundary, recorded so a future session doesn't misread this as more than it
  is**: this decouples training from the startup *sequence* — reconcile, exit re-adoption, and
  reaching the trading loop no longer wait on it in series. It does not thread-pool-offload the
  synchronous XGBoost/LightGBM fitting itself (`train_all_symbols` has zero
  `run_in_executor`/`to_thread`); a fit call can still hold the event loop for its own duration
  once the background task gets a turn. True thread offload is a materially bigger, separate change
  (numpy/xgboost thread-safety, GIL-release behavior) neither finding asked for.
  Side effect, not a separate fix: `_started_at` (feeds the existing 5-minute post-restart settling
  guard) was already stamped before training — today a 7.5-minute training run silently consumed
  the entire settling window before the first scan was even possible. This fix doesn't touch
  `_started_at`; once training no longer blocks the loop from starting, that guard becomes live
  again for the first time in this scenario, for free.
- `master.py`: new `BOT_RESTART_GRACE_S = 1200.0` (20 min, the original audit's own number)
  constant. Hang branch: grace-skip when `_last_restart` is set and recent (`_last_restart is None`
  gets no grace, falling straight through to today's behavior — verified this keeps
  `test_w20_host_clock_and_calendar_faults.py`'s existing hang test green unmodified, not assumed);
  the existing page gated with `_alert_gate("bot_hung_heartbeat_stale", 1800.0)` (was unthrottled);
  a real hang now spends `self._restarts` and, once exhausted, gives up with the same
  `bot_max_restarts_reached` wording the bot-DOWN branch already uses, instead of looping every
  2 minutes forever.
- `tests/test_audit_fixes.py`: its `bot_manager` fixture patched `LOGS_DIR`/`ROOT` but not
  `DATA_DIR` — found in passing, its two hang-adjacent tests were already running against this
  box's real `data/bot_heartbeat`, surviving only because their bare proc made `self.stop()` raise
  into the (until now, silent) outer handler. This wave changes control flow in exactly that
  branch; fixed rather than continuing to rely on the accident.

VERIFICATION:
- `python -m compileall -q src` / `python scripts/typecheck.py` clean throughout.
- New file `tests/test_w46_startup_protection_and_hang_grace.py` (4 tests) plus a new
  `TestHangDetectorGraceAndBudget` class extending `tests/test_w34_ops_substrate.py`'s existing
  real-`health_check()`-driving harness (5 tests) — 9 new tests total, not duplicating either
  file's existing fixtures.
- Full combined run of every file this wave touches or the research flagged as adjacent
  (`test_w46_*`, `test_w34_ops_substrate`, `test_w20_host_clock_and_calendar_faults`,
  `test_audit_fixes`, `test_w13_gateway_recovery`, `test_w18_gateway_port_and_throttle`,

- Full fast lane, count taken by **running** it (the standing rule since W40): **2219 passed / 45

## 2026-09-21 - W47 EXECUTED — the cadence authority, the MTM baseline, and a real 30s protection guarantee

All four findings re-verified against HEAD before scoping (same discipline every wave since W41),
landed in the roadmap's load-bearing order: `numeric-pairs-07` first (it creates the authority the
last part is measured against), `bot-day-09` + `money-flow-02` together (same `mtm_sod_*` key,
cannot land apart), `bot-day-10` last.

**1. `numeric-pairs-07`.** Four coupled numbers, four bare literals, zero enforcement:
`monitor_interval = 30` (orchestrator.py), `ttl=15` (market_data.py), `MARKS_MISSING_ALERT_TICKS = 10`
(portfolio.py), `max_quote_staleness_seconds=180.0` (settings.py). New `ait/utils/cadence.py` — a
pure stdlib leaf, no internal imports, so `config/settings.py` can import it with no cycle — is now
the one authority (`FAST_MONITOR_CADENCE_SECONDS`, `QUOTE_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`,
`MARKS_MISSING_ALERT_SECONDS`, `QUOTE_STALENESS_BUDGET_SECONDS`); all four sites import it, values
unchanged. `tests/test_w47_cadence_invariants.py` asserts the relationships against the real
imported constants (ttl < cadence; staleness budget ≥ 6× cadence; ticks × cadence == 300s;
touch-confirm window fits inside the staleness budget) plus per-site import identity (`is`, not
`==` — proves each site imports the authority rather than retyping an equal-today literal), plus an
end-to-end `MarketDataService.get_quote()` cache-expiry drive with a patched clock.

**2. `bot-day-09` + `money-flow-02`**, one block in `_monitor_positions_fast`. `PositionStatus`
gained `marks_missing: bool = False`, set from the local `_evaluate_position` already computed
(portfolio.py) but never surfaced — a marks-missing position returned `unrealized_pnl=0.0`,
indistinguishable from a real zero, and the MTM daily-loss brake summed those zeros as a phantom
gain equal to the book's actual carry, structurally unable to trip during an outage
(`money-flow-02`). A marks-missing tick now skips the MTM evaluation AND the lazy SOD-key stamp
entirely (logged `mtm_check_skipped_marks_missing`) rather than evaluate on fabricated data; the
next clean tick re-evaluates for free since `check_daily_loss_mtm` is a pure per-tick
evaluate-and-maybe-trip. New `TradingOrchestrator._capture_mtm_baseline` replaces the old silent
lazy stamp (`bot-day-09`): it reconstructs the SOD baseline from each open position's last
PERSISTED real mark (`StateManager.get_position_mark` — the same numbers `master.py`'s digest
already trusts) when every position has one, and falls back to the current tick's number with a
logged + paged `mtm_baseline_degraded_post_open` when it can't (a genuinely new position with no
prior mark). Deliberately out of scope, not half-built: stamping the baseline opportunistically at
bot shutdown — `orchestrator.stop()` is bare `self._running = False` with no portfolio snapshot,
and wiring one touches supervisor shutdown ordering, a different and riskier surface for a case the
persisted-marks reconstruction already covers well. **Registered, not fixed.**

**3. `bot-day-10`.** `_trading_loop` was one sequential task: an if/else made `_trading_cycle` (the
entry scan) and `_monitor_positions_fast` (protection) mutually exclusive per iteration.
`_trading_cycle`'s entry-scan tail (per-symbol chain fetches, NBBO waits, partial-fill waits —
unbounded, no `asyncio.wait_for` anywhere in it) ran to completion before the next position check,
so the real inter-check gap was `30s + scan duration`, not 30s. The 2026-09-21 live exit log already
shows the symptom verbatim: `heartbeat stale 6.5 min` while a scan held the loop. `_trading_loop` now
supervises two independent concurrent tasks — `_protection_task_loop` runs `_monitor_positions_fast`
on its own guaranteed `FAST_MONITOR_CADENCE_SECONDS` cadence regardless of scan duration (and now
also owns the supervisor file-heartbeat and the periodic watchdog recovery check, both of which used
to stretch alongside the position-check gap for the identical reason — **a second consequence of the
same root cause, closed here as a side effect, not a separate finding**); `_scan_task_loop` runs the
entry scan on its own `scan_interval_seconds` cadence, cadence-for-cadence identical to the original
single-loop version (verified: first scan after `scan_interval` seconds of accumulated sleep, each
next one `scan_interval` after the PREVIOUS one *completes*, matching the original's
reset-in-`finally` semantics exactly).

**Found only by reading the code, not in either original finding — the companion piece the fix
needed:** taken literally ("run `_monitor_positions_fast` as its own independent task"), this
reintroduces **R19**. `PortfolioManager._pass_quote_verdicts` is per-pass instance state (set at the
top of `check_positions`, nulled in its `finally`); two overlapping passes would null each other's
memo mid-flight, and `_spot_quote`'s per-symbol verdict is exactly the mechanism R19 added to stop a
healthy feed being misclassified "frozen" — which downgrades the touch stop to a 2-tick confirmation,
the same +30-60s cost the R16/R19 incident record already prices as a live loss. New
`_get_position_lock` (a lazily-created `asyncio.Lock`) serializes `_monitor_positions_fast` against
`_trading_cycle`'s own position-check block (steps 3/3b/5/5b only — deliberately **not** held across
steps 1/1b/2 above it or the entry-scan tail at step 6+, which touch no position state and are the
whole point of running concurrently). Nothing else needs guarding, verified rather than assumed: a
duplicated `_execute_exit` cannot double-place — W45's `_cas_to_closing` is an atomic
`FILLED|PARTIAL → CLOSING` transition and all three builder sites `return None` on refusal *before*
`place_order`; `check_fills_safe` already carries its own R11 reentrancy guard built for exactly this
("the event-driven path and the 30s monitor can both want check_fills").

**Design correction made mid-implementation:** the plan called for the lock to live in `__init__`,
but many existing tests construct `TradingOrchestrator` via `__new__` (bypassing `__init__`) and
drive `_trading_cycle`/`_monitor_positions_fast` directly — a plain `self._position_pass_lock` would
raise `AttributeError` in all of them. `_get_position_lock` instead uses this class's existing
lazy-getattr-or-create pattern (`PortfolioManager._quality_validator` is the precedent) — same
guarantee, zero test fallout, no test file touched to accommodate a new attribute.

PROOF, every part mutation-tested via `git stash push -- <file>` (never a hand-revert), reruns
until stable:
- Part 1: reverting the TTL to equal the cadence fails `test_quote_ttl_is_strictly_below_the_
  monitor_cadence` (`assert 30 < 30.0`).
- Part 2: with `PositionStatus.marks_missing` and `_capture_mtm_baseline` stashed out, all 7 of
  `tests/test_w47_mtm_baseline_integrity.py` fail — first `PositionStatus.__init__() got an
  unexpected keyword argument 'marks_missing'`, then (once that's back) real assertion failures on
  the reconstruction/skip logic itself.
- Part 3: with the loop restructure and the lock stashed out, the central test
  (`test_position_checks_keep_ticking_during_a_slow_trading_cycle`) fails consistently — **0**
  position checks during the fake slow scan, 3/3 reruns — against the reverted sequential loop,
  before passing clean (6/6, 3/3 reruns) against the fix.

VERIFICATION:
- `python -m compileall -q src` / `python scripts/typecheck.py` clean throughout, every edit round.
- New files: `tests/test_w47_cadence_invariants.py` (10), `tests/test_w47_mtm_baseline_integrity.py`

Both findings re-verified against HEAD before scoping (the standing discipline every wave since
W41), landed as two commits per the roadmap (PLAN.md:6696): `trade-life-commission-trueup-gate-
measures-wrong-quantity` Path A (plus its Path B sibling, found still open at HEAD — see below),

**1. `trade-life-commission-trueup-gate-measures-wrong-quantity`.** `_true_up_commission`
([orchestrator.py](src/ait/bot/orchestrator.py)) gated the inline true-up on
`count_executions(trade_id) >= 2*legs_n` — raw row PRESENCE. `_sweep_executions`
([executor.py](src/ait/execution/executor.py)) wrote `commission=0.0` the instant any fill was
seen, real or not, and a combo order's BAG summary row inflated the row count on top of that (a
4-leg condor's 10 total rows satisfied `>= 8` while real leg commissions were still outstanding) —
permanently overstating realized P&L by whatever exit-side commissions hadn't landed yet.

**Found only by reading `tests/test_r16_broker_fixes.py`'s own production fixture (a real
2026-08-04 SPY condor), not stated in the original finding's text:** the BAG summary row gets its
own `commissionReport` too — reported as a genuine `0.0`, not a missing one. This meant
"`commission IS NOT NULL`" alone would have been an incomplete fix: a couple of quickly-reported
BAG rows could substitute for still-pending LEG rows and reproduce the exact same defect from a
different angle. The completeness check (`count_executions_with_commission`, new) excludes the BAG
row explicitly (`con_id != BAG_CON_ID`) — a genuinely load-bearing detail, not decoration; the first
version of the fix, before this was noticed, would not have closed the finding.

`commission` now defaults to `NULL` ("not yet reported") rather than `0.0` — no schema migration,
since the column already permitted `NULL` and only ever received a literal `0.0`. The upsert also
gained the same "never regress a known value" protection `signal_price`/`live_mid`/`nbbo_spread`
already had, which `commission` alone was missing. `count_executions` itself is untouched — it has
a second, legitimate, different caller (a reconnect fill-reconstruction liveness check that
genuinely wants raw row presence) and must keep meaning that.

**Path B, `_settle_deferred_trueups` (the post-market path), was still open at HEAD** — the
original finding's own second half, which W37 (per this wave's roadmap entry) fixed only the
day-attribution half of, not the completeness half. It had **zero** completeness check at all
(`_real > 0` only) and deleted its `trueup_pending_*` marker **unconditionally**, win or lose — a
trade caught mid-ledger at post-market time got trued up against a partial ledger anyway, and never
got a second chance regardless of outcome. Now shares the exact same completeness gate as the
inline path, keeps the marker set (retries the next post-market run) when still incomplete, and —
per the original finding's own suggested fix, previously undone — now stamps `trades.commission`
with broker truth once it does settle, matching what the inline path already did.

**2. `trade-life-credit-econ-floors-signal-time-only` (restate half).** `_position_capital_at_risk`
stamps `trade_maxloss_<id>` (bot_state) and `trades.capital_at_risk` once, right after
`execute_signal` returns — order **placement** time, before the real fill price is known (a credit
order can ladder for 45s+). Neither was ever restated once the fill landed, even though
`_update_trade_filled`/`_update_trade_partial` already correct `trades.entry_price` to the real
fill. The go-live DD denominator and the aggregate-risk-cap input both read the signal's pre-fill
guess for the position's whole life.

New `restated_capital_at_risk` (`strategies/base.py`, alongside `CREDIT_STRATEGIES`/
`UNDEFINED_RISK_STRATEGIES` — the existing single-source-of-truth home for this classification)
restates from the algebraic identity every defined-risk credit strategy's signal already encodes
(`max_loss = (max_width - total_credit) * 100`, confirmed against `iron_condor.py:362-365`; wing
width is fixed between signal and fill, only credit can move):
`true_max_loss = signal_max_loss + (signal_entry_price - actual_fill_price) * 100`, no new field
needed. Scoped **deliberately** to defined-risk credit strategies only (`iron_condor` today,
matching "the live selector is IC-only," CLAUDE.md) — `short_strangle`/`covered_call`/
`cash_secured_put`/`short_straddle`/`jade_lizard` price `max_loss` as a stress **estimate**
(straddles.py), not a width-minus-credit figure, and this identity would be flatly wrong for them;
the guard is written against the existing named sets, not a hardcoded string, so a future
defined-risk credit spread is covered for free. Lives in `strategies/base.py` rather than reusing
`TradingOrchestrator._position_capital_at_risk` directly, to avoid the executor→orchestrator
circular import (orchestrator already imports executor) — `_position_capital_at_risk` itself is
untouched, still owning the signal-time stamp.

Wired into **both** `_update_trade_filled` and `_update_trade_partial` (a shared
`_restate_capital_at_risk_from_fill` helper) — the partial-fill site included deliberately: the
placement-time stamp assumed the full requested size, so a partial fill's actual (smaller, possibly
differently priced) quantity is exactly the case the signal-time number cannot have accounted for,
and skipping it would have left a known gap. Confirmed **no further wiring needed**, not assumed:
`_sync_risk_manager_positions` re-reads the `trade_maxloss_*` KV fresh every cycle (verified by
driving it for real through the smoke rig), so the aggregate-risk-cap consumer (`risk/manager.py`)
picks up the restated number automatically; `reporting/go_live.py`'s `max_concurrent_car` reads
`trades.capital_at_risk` directly by SQL, so the DD-denominator consumer does too.

## 2026-09-22 - W49 EXECUTED — the meta-labeler's close-count floor is a real config field now, and the keeper's relaunch loop has a real pause switch

`policy-vs-impl-7` and `docs-policy-04` were the one wave the roadmap itself flagged as needing an
**operator decision before scoping** (PLAN.md:6697), and `docs-policy-04` had already been queued
and deferred seven times. Both decisions were made this session, in a planning conversation before
any code:

- **`policy-vs-impl-7`**: three documents disagreed on the meta-labeler's minimum real-close floor
  before it should be trusted for live entries — `config.yaml`'s comment said 50, PLAN.md's own
  tracking table said 100+, and the code enforced neither at arm time
  (`orchestrator.py` armed the gate on `settings.meta_label.enabled` alone). Operator instinct,
  confirmed by reading the code first: rather than picking one of the three numbers, expose it as a
  real config field the operator can change without a code deploy. Confirmed there was nothing to
  leverage in config.yaml yet — the "50+" was a bare comment, `MetaLabelConfig` had no close-count
  field at all.
- **`docs-policy-04`**: build `KEEPER_PAUSE` enforcement, not the doc-only alternative — matching
  this project's general bias toward enforced-not-remembered kill switches.

**1. `policy-vs-impl-7`.** New `MetaLabelConfig.min_closes_to_enable` (default 100, matching what
the audit calls "the current-policy document"; bounds `30-500`, the floor matching the separate,
unchanged `MIN_TRADES_FOR_TRAINING` statistical minimum). New
`reporting.go_live.real_close_count(db_path, strategies=GO_LIVE_VERDICT_STRATEGIES)` — the
count-only sibling of `compute_go_live_verdict`, same population (real closes,
`not_real_close_sql`-filtered, IC-only), so the meta-label gate and the go-live scorecard agree on
"how long is our track record" instead of a third counting convention. New
`TradingOrchestrator._meta_label_arm_sufficient()` wired as a fourth `and` clause into the existing
live entry-consumption gate inside `_scan_symbol` — the only place live entries are actually
influenced; `__init__`-time construction and training already have their own separate,
unrelated gates, left untouched. Re-checked every scan (not cached at startup), so crossing the
threshold mid-day takes effect on the very next scan. Fails CLOSED on any error, which for this
specific gate means falling back to today's baseline of no meta-label opinion at all — the
meta-labeler can only make entries MORE conservative, so skipping it on an unreadable count reverts
to the already-proven primary-model-only behaviour rather than blocking anything.

**2. `docs-policy-04`.** `keeper_ait.bat` (the Windows box's outer supervisor, relaunching
`run_orchestrator.py` within ~90s of no matching process existing) now checks for
`data\KEEPER_PAUSE` immediately after its existing log-rotation block: if present, logs the pause
and skips BOTH the alive-check/relaunch AND the deadman ping for that tick, via a new `:sleep` label
placed right before the existing three-fallback delay chain. Bare marker file, same convention as
`data/HALT` (create = engage, delete = resume). `docs/RUNBOOK.md`'s kill-switch table gained the
`data/KEEPER_PAUSE` row pair and the "Full stop" row now creates it first; the manual-intervention
procedure's step 2 creates it before stopping bot processes, step 5 deletes it.

**Cannot be executed from this Mac dev box** — `keeper_ait.bat` is Windows batch syntax. Verified
instead by a careful dry-run trace of both branches against the script's own already-proven idioms:
confirmed byte-identical behaviour in the no-pause case (the new `if exist` block is a no-op when
the file is absent; the new `:sleep` label is a no-op when reached by normal fall-through, since a
label alone does not alter control flow) and the intended skip-to-sleep behaviour when paused,
traced line by line against the actual current file. **This needs a human with hands on the
Windows box to confirm the branch behaves as read, the first time it actually fires** — registered
here, not silently assumed.

**`CLAUDE.md` was also edited to list `data/KEEPER_PAUSE`, but this is LOCAL TO THIS MAC CHECKOUT
ONLY, not shipped anywhere.** Found mid-implementation, not anticipated when this was planned:
`CLAUDE.md` is gitignored in this repo (`.gitignore:35` — the operator's own pre-existing comment,

## 2026-09-22 - W50 EXECUTED — partial-exit P&L now survives the close, and reconciler promotion adopts broker quantity

Third and final wave of the "qty>1 ledger fork" (R26 register Group F), following the roadmap
(PLAN.md:6698) and W41's GOV-6 guard-rail. All three source findings are in
`reports/blindspot_composition_hunt_20260825.md`: `money-flow-05` (line 532),
`trade-life-partial-slice-pnl-erased` (line 540), `trade-life-promotion-ignores-broker-quantity`
(line 548).

**Three decisions made this session, in a planning conversation before any code** (the roadmap
flagged none of these as *requiring* an operator decision, unlike W49's pair, but they were
genuine judgment calls a plan alone shouldn't make silently):

1. When a partial slice closes, `daily_stats`/the breaker see it **immediately** (both partial-exit
   paths feed them in real time; final close contributes the remainder only) rather than deferring
   to final close as the register's own suggested fix reads — the deferred version would regress
   BC-H3's real-time breaker visibility on a locked-in partial loss.
2. GOV-6 (W41's startup refusal) **comes down** once Parts 1-2 are proven, rather than staying as
   permanent defense-in-depth or being left for a later session to decide. `config.yaml`'s
   `max_contracts_per_trade: 1` pin is untouched.
3. Reconciler promotion **adopts** broker quantity when every leg agrees, and **freezes** new
   entries (not the promotion itself) when legs disagree — chosen over always-adopt (silently
   normalizes a genuinely broken structure) and always-refuse (leaves a live position unmonitored).

**Re-verification against HEAD (this session), before any of the above was decided:** all three
findings' mechanisms confirmed intact, but the register's own line numbers are stale everywhere
(the report is dated 2026-08-25; every file it cites has moved substantially since — W37, W41, W48
all touched this territory), and dormancy is TWO independent gates, not the one the register
describes: `position_sizer.py`'s hard cap (`contracts = min(max_contracts, account_scale_cap,
hard_cap)`, keyed to `config.yaml`'s `max_contracts_per_trade`) bounds the position sizer's own
arithmetic; `paper_trading_mode: true` separately pins the learning multiplier at 1.0
(`orchestrator.py` `apply_adaptations=not settings.learning.paper_trading_mode` ->
`StrategyAdaptor(active=False)` -> `get_strategy_multiplier` returns 1.0 unconditionally). GOV-6
only ever guarded the first gate — see the newly-registered finding below.

**1. `money-flow-05` + `trade-life-partial-slice-pnl-erased`.** `state.py` `close_trade` DELETEd
`open_positions.partial_exits` before anyone folded it into `realized_pnl` — a scaled-out trade's
go-live PF input (`reporting/go_live.py` reads `trades.realized_pnl` directly) silently dropped
every closed slice's P&L, permanently, the instant the DELETE ran. The executor's own true-partial
branch (`_book_partial_exit`, the path a multi-leg fill like a condor scaling out actually takes —
money-flow-05's own correction: the orchestrator's single-leg ladder path can never take a
multi-leg partial) reached NO ledger at all, not even `daily_stats`, until the eventual final close.

Fixed: `close_trade` now reads `open_positions.partial_exits`, sums the slices' `pnl`, and folds it
into `realized_pnl` — atomically with the DELETE, via `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (same idiom `book_exit_core`
already uses), so a concurrent `record_partial_exit` for the same trade_id cannot land in the gap
and be silently lost. The JSON is archived onto a new `trades.partial_exits` column (also added to
`TradeRecord`) rather than just discarded — the erasure this closes. The `exit_outbox` row (read by
the crash-recovery drain) carries the same folded total, not the bare remainder that used to be
written there.

The executor's true-partial branch now feeds `daily_stats`/the breaker in real time via
`record_partial_pnl`, mirroring the orchestrator's own ladder path (`_execute_partial_exit`, which
has done this since BC-H3) instead of reaching no ledger. This creates a new problem the register's
own suggested fix doesn't address: with BOTH partial paths now feeding stats/breaker in real time,
booking the FULL folded total again at final close would double-count every slice. Resolved by
splitting "the money delta" from "the win/loss verdict" at the booking layer:
`book_exit_core`/`record_trade_result` both gain an `outcome_pnl` parameter (defaults to `pnl`,
so every existing call site is behaviourally unchanged); the orchestrator computes
`money_delta = realized_pnl - _archived_partial_pnl(trade)` (the new helper reads
`trades.partial_exits`, so the live callback path and the `_drain_exit_outbox` crash-recovery path
derive the identical number from the identical source, not from anything threaded through
`completed_exits`/`exit_outbox`) and passes `outcome_pnl=realized_pnl` — so `daily_stats.total_pnl`
gets each dollar exactly once, while Thompson, drift, the human-facing notification, and the
consecutive-loss counter all read the trade's FULL round trip (a trade that nets positive overall
via an earlier partial gain resets the loss streak even if its remainder slice alone was a loss).

**A bug in my own first pass, caught by writing the tests before declaring done, not by review:**
the executor's two `completed_exits.append(...)` call sites (the main fill-handling path and
`_book_partial_exit`'s "covered the whole remaining position" branch) built their dict from the
PRE-`close_trade` local `realized_pnl` variable — never reassigned after `close_trade` folded the
real number into the DB. For any trade with partial history this would have fed the in-process
booking path the bare remainder while the crash-recovery drain (reading `exit_outbox` directly)
got the correct folded total — the two paths disagreeing on "this trade's P&L" depending on which
one happened to book it. Invisible for every trade with no partial history (folded == remainder),
which is every trade tested until `tests/test_w50_qty_ledger_fork.py`'s
`TestFinalBookingDoesNotDoubleCountRealTimeFedSlices` was written against the real code path rather
than a hand-built `completed_exits` dict. Fixed: both sites now re-read `trades.realized_pnl` from
the DB after a successful close instead of reusing the pre-close local.

The commission true-up's remembered estimate (`commission_est_{trade_id}`, W37) used to be
OVERWRITTEN by each `_calculate_realized_pnl` call — a trade with partial history calls it once per
slice plus once for the remainder, and the true-up diffs whatever is remembered against
`total_commission()`, which sums EVERY execution row (entry + every partial + final leg). Now
accumulates (read-add-write) instead of overwriting, so the remembered figure is the total estimate
across every slice — the right basis for the diff.

**2. `trade-life-promotion-ignores-broker-quantity`** (separate commit, the more dangerous of the
two per the roadmap). Reconciler promotion (`reconcile()`'s PENDING->FILLED and CLOSING->FILLED
branches, and `_sweep_stale_pending`'s own PENDING rescue) adopted the LOCAL trade quantity
unconditionally — `grep update_trade_quantity src/ait/execution/reconciler.py` returned zero hits
before this wave, at any of the three sites. The later exit then reverses `trade.quantity` blind
(`orchestrator.py`'s `combo_limit(quantity=trade.quantity)` calls), so a restart that missed a
partial fill or exit could close what exists at the broker and open the difference inverted — the
R12 F4.3 reversal incident class, resurrected on the restart path.

Fixed two ways. New `_adopt_or_flag_quantity`, called at all three promotion sites right before the
`open_positions` row is written: when every leg of the trade agrees with the broker at some OTHER
quantity, adopt it (`update_trade_quantity`) and use the adopted trade for the row; when legs
disagree, do not guess which number is real — append to `frozen_keys` so `HALT_UNTRACKED` freezes
new entries, the exact path the untracked-position branches already use, and leave `trade.quantity`
untouched. `matching_trades` is kept in sync (index-based iteration, not a fresh loop variable) so
the pre-existing report-only quantity-mismatch diagnostic a few lines later reads the adopted
figure, not a now-stale one.

Separately, and this is the change that actually closes the reversal risk regardless of whether a
given promotion adopted or froze: `position_liveness` — the gate the exit path already consults
before every reverse combo, refusing on `"partial"` (`orchestrator.py`, `if liveness == "partial":
... needs a human`) — was a pure KEY-SET comparison. Every leg present, at ANY quantity, read as
`"live"`; a leg present but at HALF `trade.quantity` was indistinguishable from a fully intact
position. Now quantity-aware: `_live_ibkr_leg_keys` returns a key -> quantity dict instead of a bare
key set (its one other caller, the sweep's `isdisjoint` check, is unaffected — a dict iterates as
its keys), and `position_liveness` returns `"partial"` when every leg is present but short of
`trade.quantity`. This is the actual safety net: even a mismatch nothing adopted (or one from any
other cause) is caught before the reversal, not just at promotion time.

**3. GOV-6 retired.** W41's startup refusal on `max_contracts_per_trade > 1` existed "until the
qty>1 booking path is fixed (PLAN.md W50)". Removed in its own commit, once Parts 1-2 were proven —
a guard-rail that outlives its bug is a false statement about the system.
`tests/test_w41_live_money_floors.py`'s test asserting the refusal retires with it; its
`=1`-constructs-cleanly control stays, since that remains true. `config.yaml`'s pin is unchanged;
raising it is a separate trading decision (Phase-2 learning volume), not a consequence of this fix.

**Newly registered, not fixed — the multiplier bypass (`orchestrator.py:3501-3523`).** Found while
tracing exactly how `adjusted_size` could exceed 1 despite the sizer's hard cap, to confirm GOV-6
only ever guarded ONE of the two dormancy gates (see re-verification above). The post-validation
learning-multiplier scale-up re-validates at the larger size
(`self._risk_manager.validate_trade(TradeRequest(..., contracts=adjusted_size, ...))`) specifically
BECAUSE a naive scale-up would bypass every dollar-gate the smaller size passed (the GATE-BYPASS FIX
comment at this same site, from 2026-07-07). But the revalidation's OWN result is only consulted for
its `approved` boolean: `if not revalidation.approved: adjusted_size = max(1,
validation.position_size)`. An APPROVED-BUT-SMALLER revalidation (the sizer's own hard cap
independently clamps `size.contracts` regardless of what was requested, so `final_contracts =
min(request.contracts, size.contracts)` can legitimately approve fewer than asked) leaves
`adjusted_size` at the larger, NEVER-VALIDATED-AT-THAT-SIZE value — which is what
`execute_signal(signal, adjusted_size)` then receives. Inert today: reaching `adjusted_size > 1`
requires `strategy_mult != 1.0`, and `paper_trading_mode: true` pins the multiplier's own source
(`StrategyAdaptor.get_strategy_multiplier`) at exactly 1.0 (verified — `apply_adaptations =
not settings.learning.paper_trading_mode`, `active=False` short-circuits to `return 1.0`
unconditionally). This is the one route to qty>1 that GOV-6 never covered (it only asserted the
config knob), and the one Part 3 removes the guard on without touching. Worth its own wave: the fix
is not "clamp to `revalidation.contracts`" alone — `revalidation.max_loss` and every other dollar
figure computed off the ORIGINAL `adjusted_size` (the aggregate-risk key at
`self._position_capital_at_risk(signal, adjusted_size)`, the Telegram message) would also need to
shrink consistently, and that needs its own careful pass, not a one-line patch under this wave's
findings.

**Newly registered, not fixed — a wall-clock-boundary test flake, same bug class as the
`test_r17_live_fixes.py` CEST/ET finding W49 registered, different file.**
`tests/test_w41_live_money_floors.py::TestPDTHistorySurvivesATransientLock` (both tests) started
failing partway through this session — NOT caused by this wave, confirmed by reproducing the

`get_recent_trading_days(WINDOW_DAYS=5)`'s cutoff, computed from `now_et().date()` AT CALL TIME
(`utils/time.py:178`, `today = now_et().date()`) — not pinned to any fixture. The test hardcodes
three entries at 2026-09-15/16/17 and asserts all three survive. With "today" (ET) at 2026-09-21,
the 5 most recent NYSE trading days are exactly {09-15, 16, 17, 18, 21} — 09-15 survives. With
"today" at 2026-09-22 (this session crossed that boundary — confirmed, this Mac's CEST clock runs
ET+6 per W49's own finding, so ET's midnight rollover into 09-22 lands at 06:00 CEST, and this
session's wall-clock runtime crossed it), the window becomes {09-16, 17, 18, 21, 22} — 09-15 is
purged, and the test's "three survive" premise fails by exactly one entry, exactly matching the
observed failure (`deque([('2026-09-16', 'SYM1'), ('2026-09-17', 'SYM2')])`, SYM0/09-15 missing).
Not fixed here (out of scope — this wave doesn't touch `pdt_guard.py` or this test file for any

idiom W41 itself used elsewhere in this same file for a different clock hazard) rather than hardcode

## 2026-09-22 - W51 EXECUTED — the broker-protocol deep halves: reject-reason capture, pre-ex-div close, entry block

Closes the "deep half" of the last two `ENFORCEMENT_GAP | live_money` findings from the R23 sibling
audit, following W41's shallow-half fixes. `model-vs-reality-margin-model-unimplemented`
(`reports/blindspot_composition_hunt_20260825.md:170`) and `model-vs-reality-ex-div-assignment-void`
(same file, line 162). The roadmap (PLAN.md:6699) flagged this explicitly as **not a normal
implementation wave** — "R24's critic notes zero of 16 prior audit angles ever examined the
broker-protocol layer" — so this session ran a probe pass (two parallel Explore agents, one over
`ibkr_client.py`/`orders.py`/`contracts.py`/`account.py`, one over the earnings-gate pattern and
dividend-data availability) before designing anything, then verified every claim directly against
HEAD and, for the external yfinance surface, against live data.

**Two scope decisions made this session, with the operator, backed by evidence the probe pass
turned up:**

1. **Skip `whatIfOrder`; finish `errorEvent`/reject-reason capture only.** The probe surfaced a
   contradiction in this project's own audit history that nobody had reconciled: `GAP_AUDIT_R7.md:330`
   calls broker whatIf consultation "rightly skipped at this scale... for a defined-risk IC book,
   spread margin = width - credit = max_loss, so the existing max_loss check is already exact" —
   while `GAP_AUDIT_R7.md:510`, in a different section of the SAME document, calls it "must exist
   before funding." Given the live selector is IC-only (defined-risk, per CLAUDE.md) and `can_afford`
   already compares against `min(buying_power, available_funds)` (W41), the `:330` reasoning holds
   for the account's actual current shape — and building `whatIfOrder` properly would mean solving a
   real hazard (`AIT_SIMULATED_CAPITAL` scales the account snapshot but not `whatIfOrder`'s real
   broker margin numbers; confirmed no `OrderState.excessLiquidity` field exists, so the check would
   need synthesizing from `maintMarginChange`) with zero existing test precedent. `errorEvent`, by
   contrast, was ~80% built already (W33) and is unambiguously useful regardless of margin-model
   sophistication. Registered as deferred: re-open if the IC-only decision changes, or launch-size
   caps are raised toward go-live (the scenario `GAP_AUDIT_R7.md:343` itself names as when the
   "rightly skipped" reasoning stops holding).
2. **Close only, no roll, for an at-risk short call.** No roll/replace-order machinery exists
   anywhere in this codebase (`grep` for "roll" returns nothing relevant) — building one is
   greenfield and larger than the rest of this wave combined. Closing fully removes the assignment
   risk the finding is about and matches the shape of the one existing exit rule that does something
   similar (`portfolio.py`'s `assignment_risk`, dte<=1, close-only, never roll).

**1. `model-vs-reality-margin-model-unimplemented` deep half — reject-reason capture.** Re-verified
at HEAD before any code, not assumed from the finding text: `ibkr_client.py:73` already did
`self._ib.errorEvent += self._on_error` (W33); `_on_error`/`_order_errors`/`_ORDER_ERROR_CODES`
already existed and already tracked 201 (margin reject); the only accessor,
`order_error_messages(order_id)`, already existed too — it just threw the numeric code away and had
exactly ONE caller, on the exit-side price-band parser (`executor.py`, the W33 branch). The
entry-cancelled path consulted nothing at all: a real IBKR 201 and a routine timeout both collapsed
into the identical `trade_cancelled` log line.

Fixed: `321` (read-only account) and `200` (no security definition) added to `_ORDER_ERROR_CODES`
alongside the already-tracked `110/201/202/10318`. New `order_error_codes(order_id) ->
list[tuple[int, str]]` accessor alongside (not replacing) the existing text-only one — the W33 exit
path is byte-unaffected. `_update_trade_cancelled` now takes the `order_id` that was already in
scope at its one call site, consults the new accessor (`getattr`+`callable` guarded, mirroring the
exact defensive style the W33 exit-path call site already uses, since `FakeIBKRClient` implements
neither accessor), and stamps the result before the CAS. New `trades.reject_code`/`reject_text`
columns (+ `TradeRecord` fields), via the same migration-list idiom W50's `partial_exits` used.
`TradeStatus.REJECTED` (confirmed dead — zero transitions to it anywhere) deliberately left unused:
repurposing it touches more surface (`go_live.py`'s terminal-status filter, anything else keyed on
status) than this finding needs; the new columns supply the distinct reason without a status-taxonomy
change. Confirmed not a reconnect hazard: `IBKRClient._ib` is built once in `__init__` and never
rebuilt; ib_insync's own `disconnect()` doesn't clear listeners, so `errorEvent` survives reconnect
for free, same as the pre-existing `disconnectedEvent`/`orderStatusEvent` wiring.

**2. `model-vs-reality-ex-div-assignment-void` deep half — pre-ex-div close + entry block.** W41's
piece 1 (the reconciler STK branch freezes new entries on an untracked stock position — the
signature of an assignment) reconfirmed still in place at `reconciler.py:1503`. Its own comment
explicitly named two follow-ups as "a real design question left to W51's deeper pass," both resolved
this wave: **no debounce** for STK (kept from W41's own reasoning — the OPT branch's two-sighting
rule exists for an empirically observed position-STREAM flicker, R5 2026-07-09; assignment is a
discrete overnight broker event, not a stream artifact, and nothing suggests a stock-position sighting
flickers the same way); **does now route through** the same Telegram declare-yes/no flow the OPT
branch uses — `manual_positions.prompt_if_needed` gained a `kind="stock"` parameter (default
`"option"`, so the existing OPT call site needed zero changes) so the prompt text is accurate instead
of calling an assignment's 100 shares of stock an "option position", and a declared-manual stock
position now stops re-freezing every single reconcile pass.

No ex-dividend date or amount existed anywhere in this codebase before this wave — checked directly
against LIVE yfinance output, not assumed: `ticker.calendar` (`earnings.py`'s own primary source) is
**empty** for SPY/TLT (a 404, "No fundamentals data found" — ETFs have no fundamentals calendar).
New `src/ait/data/dividends.py`, `DividendCalendar`, structurally `EarningsCalendar`'s twin (same
6h-TTL-cache / last-known-good / fail-open-on-exit / fail-closed-on-entry shape) sourcing
`ticker.dividends` instead — real historical per-payment dates and amounts — and projecting the next
payment forward from the average interval between the last 4. Verified against real output for the
whole universe plus TLT: SPY/QQQ/IWM project ~91 days out (quarterly, amounts $0.75-$1.89), TLT ~30
days out (monthly, ~$0.315-$0.345) — confirming the generic interval-averaging approach handles both
cadences without hardcoding either.

**A design correction found during implementation, not just planning.** The finding's suggested fix
calls this "a daily pre-ex-div check," which reads as a job for the out-of-process APScheduler or the
in-bot `_pre_market()` phase hook (which only fires on a phase *transition* — a mid-session restart
skips it, a documented gap class). Direct inspection of `portfolio.py`'s `check_positions` found a
closer, better-fitting precedent already living there: rule 3c, `pre_earnings_iv_crush`, runs on the
fast monitor's own ~30s cadence — same as every sibling exit rule — and already includes
`iron_condor`. The "daily" framing is about the dividend *lookup* being cheap to cache (the same 6h
TTL earnings already uses), not the comparison needing to run once a day; landing it on the 30s
cadence instead is more responsive, needs no new restart-safety latch, and reuses live spot/mark data
the function already fetches every cycle. New rule 3e, `pre_ex_div_assignment_risk`, immediately
after 3d: finds the short call leg (same `trade.legs`-parsing idiom as rule 1b's touch-stop),
computes extrinsic (`mark - max(0, spot - strike)`, from the same `option_marks` dict every sibling
rule already receives), and closes when extrinsic is below the expected dividend exactly one day
before ex-div — bypassing rule 3's existing `dte<=1` restriction (which is also keyed off
`trade.strike` directly, meaningless for a multi-leg iron condor's real short-call strike). Fails
OPEN on any exception, matching rule 3c's own documented rationale for the exit side. Entry block
mirrors the existing `would_hold_through_earnings` call site exactly (`orchestrator.py`, inside
`_try_execute`), gated on a new `_signal_sells_a_call` static helper — genuinely new detection logic
(the earnings gate blocks unconditionally; this one only matters for a signal that sells a call),
extracted and independently tested rather than left inline, matching `_legs_count`/
`_archived_partial_pnl`'s existing pattern.

**A bug in my own first pass, caught by the regression sweep, not by review.** Rule 3e's guard
originally read `self._dividends` directly in the `elif` condition — outside its own `try/except`,
which only wraps the branch body. `PortfolioManager` gained no `__init__` change that would set this
on every instance automatically; dozens of existing tests construct it via `PortfolioManager.__new__`
and hand-set only the attributes their own scenario needs (a well-established pattern in this test
suite, e.g. `test_r17_live_fixes.py`'s rule-3c rig). Every one of those hit `AttributeError:
'PortfolioManager' object has no attribute '_dividends'` the instant `check_positions` reached the
new `elif` — **27 pre-existing tests failed** on the first full regression sweep. Fixed with
`getattr(self, "_dividends", None)`, the exact defensive style this file already uses throughout for
the identical reason (`_marks_missing_streak`, `_notify_cb`, etc.). Re-swept clean afterward — see
VERIFICATION.
