## 2026-09-22 - ROADMAP: assignment-response policy (close/roll/close-or-roll) scoped as W52-W54, and a rule-3 multi-leg diagnosis gap found while scoping it

No code in this entry. Operator asked to assess — not implement — the effort for a config-driven
close/roll/close-or-roll policy on at-risk short option legs, prompted by reviewing W51's "close
only, no roll" scope cut, and to register the result as the next wave(s), ahead of the still-
pending test-honesty/`inspect.getsource` track (operator's explicit sequencing instruction this
session — same live-work-first precedent as the 2026-09-21 REGISTER CORRECTION + ROADMAP entry).

[1] CORRECTION TO W51's OWN FRAMING: "close or roll" is not call-specific; the ex-div finding is.
    W51's entry above says "close only, no roll, for an at-risk short call" in a way that reads as
    if the close/roll choice itself is about calls. It isn't — two different things were
    compressed into one sentence and shouldn't have been:
    - The GENERAL pattern — how to handle any at-risk short leg, call or put, for any reason — is
      symmetric by nature, and this codebase's own design already treats it that way in source:
      `portfolio.py`'s pre-existing rule 3 (`:711-737`, "Assignment risk — ITM shorts on expiry
      day") has an explicit branch for each side — `trade.contract_type == "put"` and
      `== "call"` — with its own comment pairing "short puts ITM -> stock gets put to you" against
      "short calls ITM -> shares called away." The design intent has never been call-only. (Whether
      that code path actually *executes* for the live strategy is a separate question — see [2].)
    - W51's NEW rule (3e, `pre_ex_div_assignment_risk`, `:836`+) is deliberately call-only, and
      that scoping is economically correct, not an oversight or asymmetric treatment of puts:
      early assignment ahead of a dividend is the textbook "dividend capture" trade — a long CALL
      holder can profit from exercising early, forfeiting remaining extrinsic value, specifically
      to become the stock's owner of record before the ex-div date and collect the dividend. A
      long PUT holder has no analogous incentive — exercising early forfeits extrinsic value for
      no offsetting gain, and the ex-div date's mechanical price drop makes a put MORE valuable
      held, not less. 3e stays call-only permanently; a future wave should not "fix" it by adding
      a put branch.

[2] A REAL FINDING, SURFACED WHILE ANSWERING [1] — and corrected once mid-check, the way this
    register expects: rule 3's per-side ITM diagnosis is unreachable for the only live strategy.
    It is NOT that the rule never fires (first pass assumed `trade.strike` was `None` for a
    multi-leg trade and was about to say so — checked before writing it down, and that's wrong).
    What's actually true, verified at HEAD: `iron_condor.py:410` sets `contract=short_put` as the
    signal's "primary reference leg," so `executor.py:400`'s
    `strike=signal.contract.strike if signal.contract else None` DOES store a real value (the
    short put's strike) on every iron condor trade — rule 3's outer gate (`portfolio.py:715`,
    `dte<=1 and is_credit and trade.strike`) fires as expected. But `executor.py:3145-3153`'s
    `_get_contract_type` returns `"iron_condor"` for any 4-leg signal (`"spread"` for a 2-leg one,
    e.g. `short_strangle`) — never `"put"`/`"call"` for a multi-leg trade — and rule 3's ITM check
    (`:723-726`) branches on exactly `trade.contract_type == "put"` / `"call"`. Neither matches
    `"iron_condor"`, so `itm` stays `False` unconditionally, and the `if not should_exit:` fallback
    two lines later (`:735-737`) fires instead every time, labeling the close
    `"expiry_approaching (DTE: {dte})"` — the same generic label whether the position is genuinely
    ITM-and-at-risk or not.
    Net effect, precisely stated: a live iron condor at dte<=1 still closes either way (the
    fallback guarantees it) — **this is not a live protection hole**. What's lost is the
    diagnosis: rule 3 can never tell a future policy which side is ITM, or that assignment risk
    (as opposed to routine time-decay) is why it's closing. A close/roll policy needs exactly that
    per-leg answer — which leg, is it really ITM — to decide whether there's anything to react to,
    and which leg to roll if rolling. Rule 3e already solved this correctly for its own (call-only)
    case by reading `trade.legs` JSON instead of `trade.contract_type`/`trade.strike` — the same
    idiom rule 1b (`:578`+, short-strike touch stop) uses. Rule 3 needs the identical treatment,
    extended to both sides, to become the general per-leg ITM detector a roll-capable policy would
    dispatch from. The same gap applies to `short_strangle` (2-leg, also credit, also gets
    `contract_type="spread"`) if that strategy is ever re-enabled — not just `iron_condor`.
    Folded into W52 below rather than filed as its own standalone finding: it's the same fix shape
    3e already used, on the same underlying pattern.

[3] WHAT A ROLL ACTUALLY NEEDS — researched against this codebase's real primitives, not estimated
    from first principles. Reused, proven machinery (not new cost): `ContractBuilder.combo()`
    (`contracts.py:68-98`) is a generic conId/action/ratio Bag builder with no concept of "closing"
    vs. "opening" — it already underlies both entry (`executor.py:668`) and exit
    (`orchestrator.py:4712`, which builds its closing combo by re-qualifying each `trade.legs`
    entry and reversing its action). `qualify_contract(s_batch)`, the NBBO-based marketable-limit
    combo pricing/reprice ladder (the R16-fixed raw-`Bag` `reqMktData` path), and the legs-JSON
    "find the short call/put strike" idiom (rule 1b, rule 3e) all transfer directly — none of this
    needs to be built.
    Genuinely new, roughly in the order each blocks the next:
    a. Roll-target contract selection. Nothing today picks an option contract outside of a
       from-scratch entry (the iron-condor strategy's own strike picker assumes it's building a
       fresh 4-leg condor, not replacing one leg of an open position). Needs a small, new selector:
       given an at-risk leg plus a live chain, pick a defensive replacement (later expiry, same
       strike; or a delta-matched strike, same expiry; or both).
    b. `_validate_combo_legs`/`_EXPECTED_LEG_SHAPE` (`executor.py:68-99`) is keyed by
       `strategy_name`, with a fixed expected (SELL, BUY) count per known strategy; a roll's leg
       shape (e.g. one BUY-to-close plus one SELL-to-open) matches no existing key. Needs either a
       new pseudo-strategy entry or its own validator — small, but a real gap in a gate the R5
       audit put there on purpose ("a single reversed leg turns defined-risk into undefined-risk").
    c. Atomicity is an open, unproven question, not a design detail to wave through: one BAG combo
       mixing a to-be-closed existing conId with a to-be-opened new conId (what a TWS "roll"
       ticket does under the hood), vs. two sequential orders (`_close_multi_leg` then
       `_execute_multi_leg`, reused almost as-is). Atomic removes the gap-risk window between legs
       but needs to be proven against paper, not assumed from `Bag`/`ComboLeg` being generic.
       Sequential is safer to build first but creates a new partial-failure state this codebase has
       never had to handle (old position closed, new one's placement then fails or reprices away).
    d. `close_or_roll`'s comparison model is a real modeling task, not a config toggle — "the bot
       considers both and picks the better" means comparing crystallizing the close now against
       the roll's net credit/debit, new max-loss profile, new DTE, and whether the new position
       still carries near-term assignment risk. Should start as an explicit, auditable heuristic
       (e.g. roll only on a net credit that doesn't increase max-loss vs. closing), not a full
       pricing-model EV calculation — but that sophistication call belongs to whoever scopes that
       wave, not decided here.
    e. DB/reporting linkage. A roll is naturally "close trade A, open trade B"; needs a link field
       (e.g. `rolled_from_trade_id`) so the two rows read as one continuous position, and
       `go_live.py`'s real-close/verdict logic (CLAUDE.md-flagged single-source-of-truth file)
       needs to know a roll's close isn't a normal win/loss close, or the 50-close paper-verdict
       sample gets contaminated by rolls counting as extra closes.
    f. Both rule 3 (general, once fixed per [2]) and rule 3e (ex-div, calls only, per [1]) need to
       stop unconditionally setting `should_exit=True` the moment they detect risk, and instead
       consult the new policy — a control-flow change to `check_positions`'s exit-decision shape
       (every rule today just flips a boolean), not an additive elif.

[4] CONFIG SHAPE — a sketch to size against, not a final schema; field names will move once
    [3]b-f are actually designed. A new `AssignmentResponseConfig(_StrictModel)` in `settings.py`,
    mirroring `DividendConfig`'s shape (`:499-518`): a `policy` field typed
    `Literal["close_only", "roll_only", "close_or_roll"]` (`Literal` is already the house idiom for
    this exact kind of field — `trading.mode`, `logging.level`), defaulting to `close_only` (so
    shipping the config plumbing changes no live behavior until an operator opts in), plus whatever
    [3]a/d need (a roll-target DTE floor, a minimum roll credit, etc. — TBD at implementation). A
    matching `assignment_response:` block in `config.yaml`, next to `dividends:`/`earnings:`.

[5] THE ROADMAP. Next three wave numbers, sequenced ahead of the test-honesty/`inspect.getsource`
    track per the operator's explicit instruction this session — that track carries no live-money
    urgency and keeps interleaving freely once this lands. (Disambiguation: this is unrelated to
    the *other* "roll" idea already registered at `GAP_AUDIT_R7.md:252-253` — rolling the
    untested side of a still-healthy condor toward the money for extra credit, a POST-VERDICT/M
    tactical-defense idea. This entry is about an at-risk/assigned short leg, not a healthy one.)

    | Wave | Contents | Size | Notes |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | **W52** | Fix rule 3's multi-leg ITM diagnosis ([2]): rewrite its per-leg check to use the legs-JSON idiom (rule 1b/3e's pattern) instead of `trade.contract_type`/`trade.strike`, so it can name which side of a multi-leg trade is genuinely ITM instead of always falling through to the generic `expiry_approaching` label | ~half day | Standalone, no operator decision. Worth landing even if W53/54 slip — it's the per-leg diagnosis a roll policy needs, independent of whether roll ever ships |
    | **W53** | Roll mechanics: contract selection ([3]a), combo construction + `_validate_combo_legs` extension ([3]b), the atomicity decision proven against paper ([3]c), DB linkage ([3]e first half). Ships `close_only`/`roll_only` as real, testable, config-selected behaviors | ~2-2.5 days | The atomicity probe ([3]c) may re-scope this wave once run — same "probe before designing" discipline W51 used for the broker-protocol layer |
    | **W54** | `close_or_roll`'s comparison model ([3]d) + wiring rule 3 (post-W52) and rule 3e through the new policy dispatch ([3]f) + `go_live.py` roll-accounting interaction ([3]e second half) | ~1.5-2 days | Comparison-model sophistication (heuristic vs. fuller EV) is an operator decision to make when this wave is actually scoped, not here |

    Total ~4.5-5 days across three waves — larger than any single wave run to date (W47 at ~2.5
    days was the prior largest), consistent with the "greenfield, larger than the rest of W51"
    read that prompted this assessment. W52 is sequenced first and deliberately decoupled from
    W53/54's fate: it's cheap, touches disjoint code from the rest, and closes a real (if narrow,
    per [2]) diagnosis gap on its own regardless of whether or when rolling ships.

STATE AT HANDOFF: this entry only, register-only — no code, no config, no tests touched. Nothing
to deploy or restart.

NEXT: **W52** — rule 3's multi-leg ITM-diagnosis fix, detailed above, no operator decision

## 2026-09-22 - ROADMAP EXTENSION: tastytrade-style tested/untested-side condor defense scoped as W55-W57, plus a soundness review of the operator's playbook document

No code in this entry — same register-only discipline as the entry above. Operator supplied a
document describing the standard (tastytrade-school) iron condor adjustment playbook — roll the
untested side toward the tested side for a credit, vs. roll the tested side itself for a debit,
choosing between them on a short strike's delta and DTE — and asked for (a) a soundness check,
(b) this scoped as new wave(s), (c) a `tested_only` / `untested_only` / `both` config choice, gated
on rolling being available at all, and (d) the document's own decision-framework thresholds exposed
as configured defaults. Two design forks were real enough to put to the operator rather than decide
unilaterally; both are resolved below before sizing anything.

[1] SOUNDNESS REVIEW: the playbook is accurate tastytrade-school doctrine, correctly reasoned on
    its own mechanics (rolling the untested spread closer for a credit does widen the aggregate
    breakeven and does converge the shape toward an iron butterfly; rolling the tested side for a
    debit does trade cost for distance). Two caveats, neither disqualifying:
    - It is one dominant retail/education-sourced philosophy, not a law of options math — its own
      hedging ("both approaches exist... more advanced playbooks combine both") is appropriate.
      The specific decision-table numbers (0.25/0.30/0.40 delta, 14/21 DTE) come from retail
      options-education sources cited in the document, not first-party research. Treating them as
      **configured defaults**, not hardcoded constants, is the right call — see [4].
    - The document is delta-native throughout and cannot know this codebase's own state: **there is
      no live delta/greeks feed on the exit/monitor path today.** Re-verified at HEAD (not assumed
      from the existing rule 3b comment): `portfolio.py:1073`'s `_get_position_delta` docstring
      (R16, already audited) confirms `ib.ticker(contract).modelGreeks` requires an open
      market-data subscription the exit loop never holds (every `reqMktData` elsewhere is
      snapshot-style, opened and cancelled in a `finally`), and ib_insync 0.9.86's `PortfolioItem`
      carries zero greeks fields — verified by its full field list in the same docstring. This is
      why rule 3b (delta_breach) is already documented dead. Separately re-verified:
      `_get_option_marks()` (`:312-324`), the ONE live per-leg data source the monitor loop
      actually has, returns only `item.marketPrice` keyed by `(symbol, expiry, strike, right)` —
      no IV, no greeks, price only. A framework keyed on delta thresholds cannot run against this
      bot's real data without new machinery. This is the first fork put to the operator (below).

[2] SECOND FORK: "roll a side" is ambiguous at the leg level. The document says "close the untested
    spread... and reopen it closer to the current price" — for an iron condor's short+long pair,
    "spread" is naturally the 2-leg vertical (short and its paired long together), not the short
    strike alone. Rolling only the short would leave the original long wing behind at its old
    strike, silently changing that side's width and max-loss — a real risk-shape question, not a
    style choice, and one the document doesn't itself address since it's written for single-vertical
    defenses generically rather than this codebase's defined-risk-IC-only posture (CLAUDE.md flags
    the undefined-risk boundary as a standing, sensitive concern).

[3] OPERATOR DECISIONS (both taken as given, not re-litigated below):
    - **Delta source: synthetic, from the live price the monitor loop already has — not a new
      broker subscription.** `options_chain.py:936-1030`'s `_calculate_greeks` already runs a real,
      well-audited (R16, W19, W35, w17-07) two-pass py_vollib pipeline — solve IV from an observed
      price via `implied_volatility()`, then `delta()`/`gamma()`/`theta()`/`vega()` from the solved
      IV — today only at entry-time chain scanning, fed by a chain snapshot's bid/ask mid. The new
      work is adapting this proven pattern to the monitor loop, fed by `_get_option_marks()`'s
      already-live `marketPrice` instead of a chain snapshot, and validating the solve behaves on
      real monitor-loop prices before trusting it (this codebase's standing discipline for any
      external-data-adjacent calculation — verify against real output, don't assume a working
      pattern transfers unchanged to a new calling context). This does NOT, by itself, revive rule
      3b (that needs the real-subscription path, explicitly not chosen) — but the same new synthetic
      helper COULD be substituted into `_get_position_delta` later at near-zero extra cost, if
      wanted; noted as available, not committed to any wave below.
    - **Roll scope: the full 2-leg vertical, short + long together.** Preserves the defined-risk
      wing structure and matches the document's literal description, at the cost of a 4-leg combo
      (2 closing legs + 2 opening legs) rather than the 2-leg combo (1 closing + 1 opening) W53
      above was scoped around for a single at-risk leg. `_validate_combo_legs`/
      `_EXPECTED_LEG_SHAPE` (`executor.py:68-99`) needs a second new leg-shape accommodation beyond
      W53's, for this different combo shape — the two rolls (single-leg assignment-driven, per
      W52-54; two-leg vertical, tactical, per this entry) are not the same order shape and
      shouldn't be forced through one validator case.

[4] CONFIG SHAPE (sketch, sized against, not final): a new `CondorDefenseConfig(_StrictModel)` in
    `settings.py`, structurally distinct from W52-54's `AssignmentResponseConfig` (different
    trigger — delta/DTE bands on a still-healthy position, not near-expiry/ex-div assignment risk
    on an already-at-risk one) but consuming the same underlying roll-order machinery once W53
    exists.
    ```
    enabled: bool = False            # see the POST-VERDICT note in [5] for why the default is off
    side: Literal["tested_only", "untested_only", "both"] = "untested_only"
    monitor_delta_max: float = 0.25          # below this, do nothing
    roll_untested_delta_min: float = 0.25    # document's table, row 2
    roll_untested_delta_max: float = 0.30
    roll_untested_dte_min: int = 14
    roll_untested_dte_max: int = 21
    untested_roll_target_delta: float = 0.20 # roll the untested short toward this delta
    roll_tested_delta_min: float = 0.30      # document's table, row 3 (low-gamma / >21 DTE)
    close_delta_threshold: float = 0.40      # document's table, row 4 (high-gamma / near-expiry)
    ```
    Field names and the exact threshold set will move once the wave below is actually designed —
    this sizes the surface, following `DividendConfig`'s established shape (`settings.py:499-518`)
    and the house `Literal[...]` idiom (`trading.mode`, `logging.level`) for the policy field, same
    as W52-54's entry used for `assignment_response.policy`. A matching `condor_defense:` block in
    `config.yaml`, next to the `assignment_response:` block W53/54 will add.

[5] SEQUENCING AND THE POST-VERDICT QUESTION, MADE EXPLICIT. This exact idea — rolling the untested
    side for credit and/or rolling out in time near 21 DTE — is not new to this register:
    `GAP_AUDIT_R7.md:252-253` already evaluated it and called it POST-VERDICT/M: *"at 1 contract
    each roll costs 2 legs (~$2.60 + crossing) for maybe $10-25 extra credit — thin, and changing
    exit mechanics mid-sample corrupts the 50-close measurement. The flat 1.25x loss close is a
    defensible defense until the verdict."* That reasoning is not overridden here — the register
    is append-only and that entry stands. What changes is that the operator has now asked for this
    to be scoped and built with a config surface, which this entry does. The two are reconciled the
    same way W52-54's own roll capability was: **`enabled` defaults to `False`** ([4]), so shipping
    the code changes no live behavior — the corruption risk GAP_AUDIT_R7 named only materializes on
    an explicit opt-in, which stays the operator's call, ideally after the 50-close paper verdict
    per that prior reasoning, not assumed here either way.

    | Wave | Contents | Size | Notes |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | **W55** | Synthetic per-leg delta for the monitor loop ([3] first bullet): adapt `options_chain.py`'s py_vollib IV-solve-then-Greeks pattern to `_get_option_marks()`'s live price; validate the solve against real monitor-loop prices before anything depends on it | ~1-1.5 days | No dependency on W52-54 or on anything else in this entry — could run any time, including before W52. Sequenced here only for register locality |
    | **W56** | Tested/untested decision logic: per-tick, per open iron condor, compute both short legs' synthetic delta (W55) and evaluate against [4]'s configurable delta+DTE bands to decide do-nothing / roll-untested / roll-tested / close | ~1-1.5 days | Needs a non-boolean decision output from `check_positions` — the same structural extension W54 above already needs for its own close-vs-roll choice. Design once, use for both, rather than two independent bolt-ons |
    | **W57** | The roll-a-vertical action: 4-leg combo construction reusing W53's contract-selection/qualify/NBBO-pricing primitives, the second `_validate_combo_legs` accommodation ([3] second bullet), the `CondorDefenseConfig` policy wiring ([4]), DB linkage for a (potentially two-sided) roll event | ~2-2.5 days | Depends on W53 (shared roll mechanics) and W56 (the decision to act on). The largest of the three |

    Total ~4.5-5.5 days across three more waves, on top of W52-54's ~4.5-5 days — call it ~9-10.5
    days for the complete at-risk-plus-tactical roll capability across six waves (W52-W57). Worth
    the operator seeing that sum in one place before committing to all of it; nothing here forces
    building all six before any one is useful; W52 and W55 in particular are already independently
    useful on their own.

STATE AT HANDOFF: this entry only, register-only — no code, no config, no tests touched. Nothing
to deploy or restart.

NEXT: unchanged from the entry above — **W52** first (no operator decision required). W55 has no

## 2026-09-22 - STUDY: post-FOMC entry blackout (walk-forward) — verdict NO BUFFER; and a research-harness hazard found on the way

QUESTION (operator, after the 09-21 -$503 stop). Should condor entries be blocked for N days AFTER
a macro event, as they are 1 day before? The trade was entered the morning after the 09-16 FOMC.
In the live record it is the only day-after-event entry in 13 closes, so live evidence is one trade.

HOW. `scripts/post_event_study.py`, same harness as the take-profit study (SPY/QQQ/IWM, condor only,
train126/test63/step63/gap5, entry DTE 18, ungated entries, W5 cost model), one new research-only
engine gate (`Backtester(post_event_blackout_days, post_event_dates)`, threaded through
`WalkForwardConfig`; inert unless set — proven by a within-run sanity variant that passes the dates
with no window and reproduces the baseline to the cent). FOMC only, because the live calendar knows
2026-2027 and the harness needs 2022-2026: 28 historical decision days transcribed from the Fed's
published schedule (in the script, with the source URL — verify before acting on anything here).
Decision rule written before the run (in the script docstring): n >= 30 both; variant n >= 0.85x
baseline (a buffer removes entries and pace is the binding constraint); PF > baseline + 0.10;
net/position-day >= baseline; max DD <= baseline + 1pp. Smallest qualifying N wins.

RESULT (live data store, entry DTE 18, 22 windows, 2023-01..2026-09):
  | variant      | n  | PF    | net $  | DD % | removed (P&L)    | added (P&L)   |
  | no_buffer    | 57 | 0.628 | -3,521 | 4.32 |                  |               |
  | post_fomc_1d | 54 | 0.627 | -3,424 | 4.22 | 3 (-$97)         | 0             |
  | post_fomc_2d | 53 | 0.659 | -2,980 | 3.75 | 6 (-$748)        | 2 (-$208)     |
  | post_fomc_3d |    identical to 2d (FOMC is a Wednesday; day +3 is Saturday)               |
  **NO BUFFER.** Every variant fails `PF > base + 0.10` (0.728 needed; best 0.659). The 2-day
  buffer is the best of them — PF +0.03, DD -0.6pp — for 7% fewer closes; inside noise.
  What the harness actually exercised: the three entries a 1-day buffer removed are all DAY-0
  entries (2024-07-31, 2024-12-18, 2025-06-18: the FOMC day itself), which live ALREADY blocks via
  the pre-event gate (days_to_event = 0 <= 1) — the harness's pre-event gate is inactive before
  2026, so these exist only in the simulation. In four simulated years there was NOT ONE entry on
  the day after an FOMC decision (the 09-17 shape) at 18 DTE with one slot per symbol; the only
  directly-gated day-after-event trade at 2d is 2025-10-31 (day +2, -$214). The question the
  operator asked has a sample of roughly one in the harness as well as live. The rule says no
  buffer; the honest reading is "no evidence for one, and almost none against".

WHAT THE HARNESS CANNOT TEST (registered in the script; not hidden): the live IV-rank floor (the
engine's `iv_rank` is a realized-vol range rank, not the implied-vol percentile live gates on);
the short-strike expected-move band (the engine places shorts by delta, which sits at ~0.84 EM by
construction). Both arms the operator asked about need engine parity work before they can be
tested. And ABSOLUTE LEVEL: this harness puts the live ruleset at PF 0.63 with touch stops on 44%
of trades; the live book is PF 1.79 with 2 stops in 13. Only the RELATIVE effect is read here.

A RESEARCH-HARNESS HAZARD, FOUND THE HARD WAY. The first run of this study (from the dev
worktree) reported baseline n 87 / PF 0.831 — nothing like the take-profit study's n 51 / PF 0.445
on 09-14, with the engine and walk-forward code unchanged and the OHLCV bars byte-identical (2,211
bar-days compared against the bars that run saved). Cause, proven by reproduction: the worktree
held an EMPTY `data/historical.db` — `HistoricalDataStore.__init__` creates the file if absent —
so `load_daily_ohlcv` fell back to Yahoo for everything with NO stored IBKR implied vol, and
`_load_calibrated_spreads` (which opens the store by cwd-relative default path, ignoring the
`db_path` the walk-forward was given) found no calibration. Same code, same dates, pointed at the
live store: n 50 / PF 0.449 — the 09-14 figure. So the engine prices 2024-07-onward windows with
stored implied vol when it has it and with a VIX-scaled realized vol when it does not, and the two
harnesses disagree by a factor of ~2 in PF. Nothing warned. The study now takes `--data-root`,
runs from it, and ABORTS unless every symbol carries stored IV on >= 400 rows; the results record
the store and its coverage. The take-profit study (run in the live tree on 09-14) was on the right
store. OPEN, for whoever owns the engine: thread `db_path` into `_load_calibrated_spreads` and into
the settings load, and make an empty store a loud failure rather than a silent fallback.

PROOF. `tests/test_post_event_study_injection.py`, 14 executing tests (gate inert by default; blocks
exactly days 0..N; only the most recent event counts; ISO dates accepted; applied at the real entry
path — a run gated on every day opens zero positions; pickles across the process-pool boundary;
reaches the OOS and shadow Backtesters; refused with per-window optimisation). All 14 red before the
engine change (unknown keyword). Full fast lane with the change: **2350 passed / 46 skipped / 0
failed**, typecheck OK. No live code path reads the new parameters.

Outputs: `reports/post_event_study/entry_dte_18/` (per-variant json + summaries, `removed_by_*.json`
with the exact trades each buffer took away and added, results.md/json with data provenance,
run.log). Progress directories (timeseries bars, 6 MB) are not committed, as with the take-profit
study.

## 2026-09-23 - W53 (first slice) EXECUTED — roll-mechanics groundwork: config, vertical-roll leg validator, roll-target selection, DB linkage

SCOPE. W53 per the roadmap (`:8639-8779`): roll mechanics for the assignment-response
policy. Before building, two Explore agents re-verified the register's own claims at HEAD
`2dbd7a3`/`12b0354` and found the real shape bigger and different than estimated:

- `_close_multi_leg`/`_execute_multi_leg` do NOT reuse "almost as-is" as `:8720-8724` assumed
  — both manage a WHOLE position's lifecycle (all legs, one trade row); neither can replace
  one leg, or one vertical, of an open position while leaving the rest alone. **No code path
  anywhere in this codebase has ever mutated a trade's legs/expiry/entry_price after entry.**
- Rolling only the at-risk short leg (the framing `:8698-8740` scoped W53 around) breaks the
  defined-risk gate: the paired long is left behind at the old expiry, so the short is naked
  between expiries. The separately-scoped W55-57 (`:8783-8894`) independently hit the same

## 2026-09-27 - SCOPING NOTE: W54's heuristic-vs-fuller-EV fork, worked through with the
operator -- and a hard, currently-unmet prerequisite for backtesting the EV path found while doing it

No code in this entry -- register-only, same discipline as the 2026-09-22 ROADMAP entries
(`:8639`, `:8783`). Operator asked what W54's own "operator decision" (`:8762`, `:8775`)
actually is, and the conversation worked through the heuristic-vs-EV fork in enough depth
that the conclusions -- and one real, load-bearing finding surfaced while checking a claim
against the codebase rather than assuming it -- are worth registering before W54 is ever
formally scoped, so the next session doesn't re-derive them from scratch. **W54 has not
been started or wave-numbered by this entry** -- this is pre-wave scoping, the same status
the 2026-09-22 entries had before W52-57 were assigned.

[1] THE FORK, RESTATED PRECISELY. `[3]d` (`:8725-8731`) already leans toward starting with
    an explicit heuristic ("roll only on a net credit that doesn't increase max-loss vs.
    closing") over a full EV calculation, but leaves the sophistication call open. Worked
    through to: **both should be built as a config-selectable pair**, `Literal["heuristic",
    "ev"]` (naming TBD at implementation), nested so it only takes effect once
    `assignment_response.policy == "close_or_roll"` is itself chosen -- inert otherwise,
    same gating idiom `policy` and `condor_defense.enabled` already use. Defaults to
    `"heuristic"`, for the same reason every other model-risk toggle in this register
    defaults to the cheaper/safer arm.

[2] A REAL CONSEQUENCE OF CHOOSING RISK-NEUTRAL DRIFT, worth recording because it changes
    what "fuller EV" even needs to be built as. Risk-neutral valuation means the discounted
    expected payoff of holding a position to expiry IS, by definition, that position's
    theoretical fair value today -- so "compute the EV of holding the new position to
    expiry" collapses to "price both alternatives accurately," not a Monte-Carlo-style
    simulation over a terminal price distribution. Two consequences: (a) the EV path is a
    smaller, more auditable build than the phrase suggests -- accurate present-value
    pricing of both sides (reusing the existing py_vollib IV-solve pipeline,
    options_chain.py:936-1030), not a new simulation engine; (b) it cannot, by
    construction, find genuine directional edge -- it can only catch cases the heuristic's
    crude credit/max-loss proxy misses (e.g. a "net credit" roll that's actually giving
    away more time value than it collects). Recorded so nobody later expects the EV path to
    systematically outperform the market, only to account for it more carefully than the
    heuristic does.

[3] THREE GAPS THE OPERATOR'S OWN 3-POINT PROPOSAL DIDN'T COVER, worked through to concrete
    recommendations (none built, all for whoever scopes W54 for real):
    a. **Portfolio-level risk gating.** A roll's opening leg should pass through the SAME
       entry gates a fresh signal would (`risk/manager.py` -- concentration, correlation,
       VIX credit tiers), not just its own standalone EV-vs-close comparison -- reusing the
       existing gate rather than a parallel check, per CLAUDE.md's duplication-causes-
       silent-divergence theme. The real wrinkle: a roll REPLACES an existing position, so
       the gate needs to net the new position's risk against what the old one already
       contributed, not treat it as pure incremental exposure on an unchanged book (a naive
       reuse would double-count). Flag as its own labelled sub-item (a `[3]g`, continuing
       the existing lettering) when W54 is actually scoped.
    b. **Fill-price conservatism inside the EV number itself.** Price both sides of the
       comparison using the SAME conservative per-leg synthesis already used elsewhere
       (`orchestrator._synthesize_combo_cost`'s BUY-at-ask/SELL-at-bid idiom,
       `combo_entry_limit`'s natural-vs-mid ladder) rather than a fantasy mid -- otherwise
       the model can systematically overstate its own edge relative to what the reprice
       ladder can actually fill.
    c. **A repeat-roll safeguard.** Nothing today caps how many times one position can
       roll. Recommend two layers: a hard `max_rolls_per_position` count cap (cheap,
       `Field(...)`-bounded, walks the `rolled_from_trade_id` chain W53 already built --
       ship this one, non-negotiable) plus a documented-but-deferred cumulative-roll-cost
       cap (catches "death by a thousand small rolls" a count cap alone would miss) --
       same "ship the simple version, register the sophisticated one" pattern this register
       already used for the heuristic-vs-EV choice itself.

[4] DATA-QUALITY FALLBACK, refined from the operator's own proposal (fall back to
    heuristic + alert on bad IV, naming the expiry in question): reuse the EXISTING
    detection signal (`chain_iv_is_a_guess`, `options_chain.py` -- confirmed live this
    session, see the probe-preflight entries above) rather than inventing a second
    IV-quality detector; make the trigger graduated (a config threshold, same idiom as
    `options.min_open_interest`/`max_bid_ask_spread_pct`) rather than a strict binary, since
    "the whole chain is quoteless" and "one far-OTM strike is missing" are very different
    severities; and use PER-STRIKE IV (already computed by the existing solve) rather than
    a single flattened ATM number, since the roll's own OTM strikes are exactly where skew
    matters most.

[5] LATENCY: A CONFIG-EXPOSED RE-EVAL CADENCE (operator's proposal), refined. `get_chain`'s
    measured 110-209s median cost (W53's own register entry, `:9303`) makes a per-tick EV
    re-evaluation infeasible; agreed on a config-gated interval (only reachable under
    `policy=="close_or_roll"` AND the EV comparison model, `Field(...)`-bounded so it can't
    be set to something that re-introduces the same latency problem or defeats reactivity
    entirely). Two refinements:
    - Skip a cycle rather than fire a new chain fetch while the previous one is still in
      flight -- the same "never act on an unanswered request" discipline the reconciler
      already applies (`get_all_open_order_ids` returning `None` on an unanswered request,
      never read as "nothing working"). Not a new pattern to invent.
    - Per [2] above, the EXPENSIVE part is target SELECTION (a chain scan, to find the
      right delta/strike), not repricing an already-selected target (a few targeted
      quotes). Worth considering two cadences rather than one -- a slow one for
      re-selecting the roll target, a fast one for re-checking its live economics -- though
      this is a refinement to weigh at implementation, not decided here. Note this
      "cache an expensive result, reuse it for a while" shape already exists in this
      codebase (`OptionsChainService`'s 2-min `TTLCache` on `get_chain`,
      options_chain.py:479) -- a slower EV-verdict cache is the same idiom one layer up,
      not a new one.

[6] THE HARD FINDING: BACKTESTING THE EV PATH BEFORE IT COULD EVER GO LIVE (operator's own
    requirement, agreed on early in this conversation) HAS A PREREQUISITE THAT DOESN'T EXIST
    YET, AND CANNOT BE BUILT QUICKLY. Checked directly against the codebase rather than
    assumed, prompted by the operator's own "are we sure we store this" question --
    findings from an Explore agent this session, HEAD `52f818b`:
    - `data/historical.db` (`HistoricalDataStore`, `src/ait/data/historical.py`) has TWO
      structurally different kinds of IV data, not one: a per-strike/per-expiry-shaped
      table (`option_spread_samples`: symbol, sample_date, right, strike, dte, iv, bid,
      ask, mid, half_spread_pct) that is the only table shaped like a real vol surface, and
      a composite-scalar level series (`daily_prices.implied_vol` / `daily_iv`: one number
      per symbol per day).
    - The operator's own recollection of "2 snapshots" is exactly right and not
      approximate: `option_spread_samples` holds precisely 2 sample dates (2026-05-24,
      2026-08-25), QQQ only, 1,963 rows total.
    - **Nothing scheduled writes surface data.** `orchestration/master.py`'s APScheduler job
      list has zero jobs touching `historical.db`. The live bot's only automatic write
      (`orchestrator.py:5549`, `_persist_daily_iv`, once per symbol per day) is the
      composite scalar, not a surface. `scripts/calibrate_option_spreads.py` is the only
      code that ever captures a real surface, and it is manual-only, never wired into any
      scheduled job -- confirmed by grep, zero hits outside `scripts/`/`tests/`/
      `backtesting/`/`diagnostics/`.
    - **This is not merely an un-cadenced job -- the data cannot be backfilled at all.**
      `calibrate_option_spreads.py` can only ever snapshot TODAY's chain (via yfinance or
      an IBKR live snapshot); there is no historical options-chain data source anywhere in
      this codebase. Starting a scheduled surface-snapshot job today only accumulates
      history forward from today -- it cannot reconstruct the past. The only avenue for
      genuine historical per-strike coverage would be integrating a paid historical-options
      provider (Polygon is already a runtime dependency for other data, per
      `constraints.txt` -- whether its endpoints cover historical option chains is
      UNCONFIRMED, not checked this session).
    - **Corroborating evidence this gap is real and already known in a different guise**:
      the composite-level series has genuine depth ONLY for QQQ (daily_prices/daily_iv back
      to 2011-08-26, ~3,780-3,790 rows) and SPY/IWM (since 2024, ~500-510 rows each) -- the
      rest of the live universe has none. And confirmed directly against source: `iv_rank`
      in BOTH the backtest engine (`ml/features.py:_add_iv_features:660-682`) and
      `ml/regime.py:_measure_iv_rank:156-174` is a pure realized-vol range rank computed
      from OHLCV log-returns -- "no stored IV is read at all" (the function's own
      docstring). Only the LIVE bot's `_estimate_iv_rank`
      (`bot/orchestrator.py:5558-5660`) attempts a true IV percentile first, falling back to
      the same realized-vol proxy when the stored series is short (<60 rows) or stale (>5
      days). This is exactly the "parity needs an IV-percentile series in the store first.
      Registered, not built" item W52a's entry already named (`:9187-9189`) -- now traced
      to source and confirmed, not just repeated.
    - **No cross-date interpolation exists anywhere**, confirmed by direct grep
      (`ffill`/`forward_fill`/`gap_fill`/`interpolat` across `data/`, `backtesting/`,
      `ml/`) -- every real consumer treats a gap as something to react to, never to paper
      over: `post_event_study.py`'s 400-row guard (`MIN_STORED_IV_ROWS`, `:105,224-248`)
      hard-aborts on thin data (distinct from and stricter than `_load_calibrated_spreads`'
      `calibrated_spreads_absent` no-op-to-config-default, `engine.py:1553-1583`); `iv_rank`
      falls back to realized vol in both live and backtest, as above. What DOES exist:
      within-day, across-STRIKE interpolation for a LIVE chain snapshot only
      (`options_chain.py:atm_iv():243-294`, linear between the two strikes bracketing
      spot) -- never against stored history; and a tenor-interpolation scheme
      (VIX9D/VIX/VIX3M/VIX6M flat-forward-variance) that exists only on the unmerged branch
      `Interactive-modeling-1` (`scripts/calibrate_term_structure.py`, not on
      `feature/event-straddle`/`main`) plus an untracked notebook in this working tree

## 2026-09-27 - W55 EXECUTED — synthetic per-leg delta for the monitor loop

SCOPE. Per the 2026-09-22 ROADMAP EXTENSION (`:8783-8905`), explicitly independent of
W52-54/W53's atomicity probe: no rule on the exit/monitor path has a live per-leg delta
today. Rule 3b (delta_breach) is dead -- `_get_position_delta` (portfolio.py:1117-1166)
requires `ib.ticker(contract).modelGreeks`, a live market-data subscription the exit loop
never holds, and ib_insync 0.9.86's `PortfolioItem` carries zero greeks fields (its own R16
docstring). The ONE live per-leg data source the monitor loop has is `_get_option_marks()`
(portfolio.py:312-324) -- a single `marketPrice`, no bid/ask, no IV. This wave adapts the
existing, already-audited py_vollib IV-solve-then-Greeks pattern
(`options_chain.py:936-1112`, entry-time chain scanning only) to run off that single live
price instead, and validates it against real prices before anything is wired to depend on
it. **Nothing calls the new code from this wave** -- same "additive, unreachable from any
live path" convention W53's first slice used.

OPERATOR DECISION THIS SESSION: the new monitor-loop solver shares code with the existing
entry-time Greeks pipeline via an extract-function refactor (proven behavior-preserving
below), rather than duplicating the py_vollib calls in a second, parallel implementation --
the single-source-of-truth choice, so a future audit fix to the solve lands in both call
sites automatically.

FIX:
1. **`data/options_chain.py`** -- two new module-level pure functions, both usable
   standalone (no chain, no `self`):
   - `solve_iv_from_price(price, spot, strike, t, r, flag) -> (iv|None, outcome)`:
     extracted VERBATIM from `_calculate_greeks`'s pass-1 solve block (the exact
     `implied_volatility()` call and the W19/w17-07 arbitrage-exception handling that
     tells a genuinely-impossible quote apart from a convergence miss). `outcome` is
     `"solved"` / `"failed_arbitrage"` / `"failed_other"`.
   - `compute_greeks_from_sigma(spot, strike, t, r, sigma, flag) -> (d,g,th,v)|None`: a
     NEW function, deliberately NOT extracted from pass-2's Greeks loop -- pass 2 has a
     subtler contract (only recomputes a Greek IBKR hasn't already delivered; a
     mid-computation exception leaves whatever was already assigned in place, partial
     success survives) that the monitor loop's "always start from nothing, want all four
     fresh, all-or-nothing on any exception" need doesn't share. Sharing it there would
     have changed pass 2's partial-failure behavior -- left untouched, duplicated with
     simpler semantics instead. This distinction (share where the contract genuinely
     matches, don't force-share where it doesn't) is worth a future reader noting before
     assuming "extract everything" was the goal.
   - `_calculate_greeks` refactored to CALL `solve_iv_from_price` in its pass-1 loop
     instead of inlining the same code; its own now-redundant top-level
     `implied_volatility`/arbitrage-exception imports removed (dead after the extraction --
     confirmed unused, `implied_volatility` is no longer called anywhere else in the
     method). Pass 2 is BYTE-IDENTICAL, untouched.
2. **New module `execution/synthetic_delta.py`** (same "nothing calls into this module
   yet" convention as `roll_selector.py`; no import-cycle risk confirmed --
   `roll_selector.py:17` already imports `data/options_chain.py`, direct precedent):
   - `synthetic_leg_greeks(option_marks, symbol, expiry, strike, right, spot) ->
     ContractGreeks | None`: builds the exact `YYYYMMDD` key `_get_option_marks()`/
     `_option_position_unrealized()` use (`str(expiry).replace("-","")[:8]`,
     portfolio.py:322,370), requires `price > 0` (the one guard `_get_option_marks()`
     itself lacks -- it only filters None/NaN), calls `solve_iv_from_price` then
     `compute_greeks_from_sigma`. ANY failure -- missing mark, non-positive price, bad
     expiry, solve failure, arbitrage exception -- returns `None`, never a guessed value:
     matches `_get_position_delta`'s own None-on-failure convention exactly. No
     chain-level median fallback exists for a single leg outside a chain, and none is
     invented here. `t` uses the IDENTICAL whole-calendar-day convention
     `OptionsChain.dte`/`OptionContract.dte` use (`today_et()`-based, floored at 0.001)
     -- consistency with the audited pattern, not a new time-resolution scheme. Calls
     `_risk_free_rate()` directly (imported from `options_chain.py`) rather than taking a
     rate parameter, so a caller can't accidentally pass an inconsistent rate.
   - `synthetic_vertical_deltas(trade, side, option_marks, spot) -> {"short":..., "long":
     ...}`: the trade-level wrapper, same legs-JSON idiom W52's `_short_strikes_from_legs`
     and W53's `_at_risk_vertical` (roll_selector.py:41-61) use. Requires a CLEAN single
     short+long pair on `side` -- same invariant `_at_risk_vertical` enforces -- returning
     `{"short": None, "long": None}` otherwise, not a partial result.
   - `_get_position_delta`'s own separate bug (sums every `ib.portfolio()` item for the
     SYMBOL without matching the trade's own legs, double-counting across two trades on
     the same symbol, portfolio.py:1152-1154) is dead-code-only, out of this wave's scope,

3. **`scripts/validate_w55_synthetic_delta.py`** -- the wave's own explicit "validate
   against real monitor-loop prices before anything depends on it" requirement. Read-only:
   places no orders, calls no whatIfOrder, requests no Greeks subscription. Fetches a real

   monitor-loop mark would look like for the same contracts (that chain's own mid, standing
   in for `_get_option_marks()`'s `marketPrice`), runs the NEW synthetic path against it,
   and reports both side by side plus a sanity verdict (delta in [-1,1], IV positive,
   chain-vs-synthetic delta within 0.10). Also checks `ib.portfolio()` directly against any
   REAL open positions, if any exist by the time it runs -- the actual production data
   shape, not a stand-in. ClientId 98 -- outside the bot's ladder (1, 101-105) and the W53
   probe's 97.

A REAL BUG CAUGHT BY A TEST WRITTEN AFTER THE IMPLEMENTATION, not a design choice:

## 2026-09-27 - CENSUS-4 EXECUTED — the "scattered moderates" rewrite batch of the
test-honesty `inspect.getsource` census, 7 sites, zero production changes

SCOPE. "Batch D — scattered moderates" (`PLAN.md:7076-7081`), the register's own
suggested next step after A (CENSUS-1) and E (CENSUS-5): 7 sites across 6 files, no
shared theme or reusable harness this time — strategy entry gating, backtest engine
meta-label context, ML trainer date recovery, risk manager config reads, orchestrator
exit-step dispatch, reconciler sweep gating. Every rewrite was EMPIRICALLY PROBED in a
throwaway process before being written, AND mutation-checked afterward against the real
source (a targeted, reverted source edit per site, confirming the new assertion actually
fails against the un-fixed behavior) — a step beyond CENSUS-1's own proof discipline,
applied here because this batch has no shared harness to lean on for confidence.

TWO SITES HAD BUGS IN THE ORIGINAL TEST ITSELF, not just the anti-pattern — worth
recording since they're corrections to what the tests actually claimed, not merely style:
- `test_w19_greeks_provenance.py:116/126`: the original assertion checked BYTE-OFFSET
  ORDERING between `iron_condor.py`'s `iv_is_guessed` check and its legacy zero-delta
  check. Mutation-verified directly: swapping the two checks' order produces
  BYTE-IDENTICAL output for every probed chain shape (`iron_condor.py:218-226`, both
  return `[]` with the SAME `"degraded_greeks"` reason) — the ordering the original test
  pinned has no observable behavioral effect at all. The real, worthwhile claim (the
  guessed-IV check firing before strike selection, so a guessed chain with
  technically-nonzero-but-off-target deltas still reports `degraded_greeks` rather than a
  later, unrelated rejection) is what the rewrite actually proves.
- `test_w28_et_date_authority.py` (`:205`, shifted from `:211` by CENSUS-5's own earlier
  edit to this file): `hasattr(tr, "_ModelTrainer")` was always False — `_ModelTrainer`
  has never existed in `trainer.py` (confirmed directly; only `ModelTrainer` does) — so
  the getsource call had always grepped the ENTIRE MODULE, not the intended class. A
  second, related discovery: the seemingly-adjacent sibling test
  (`test_recovered_date_is_an_et_date`) is NOT real coverage — it re-derives the same
  `fromtimestamp(..., tz=ET)` computation inline instead of calling the trainer, itself a
  "re-derived literal" variant of the same anti-pattern this whole census exists to catch.

FIX (test-only; zero `src/ait` changes — every rewrite drives EXISTING, already-correct
`src/ait` behavior):
1. `test_w19_greeks_provenance.py:116/126` — drives the real `IronCondor.generate_
   signals` against three real chain shapes (guessed+on-target-deltas, guessed+off-target-
   0.9-deltas, unguessed+zero-deltas), reading back `last_entry_reason`. Trap avoided:
   always pairs a flagged shape with its unflagged twin, since an unflagged chain can
   still fail a later, unrelated economic gate (`em_gate` on the synthetic chain used

FINDING (independent of the census, worth recording on its own): the two production call
sites this batch's tests are supposed to prove "share one source of truth" read the SAME
`ait.execution.exit_policy` constants ASYMMETRICALLY. `backtesting/engine.py:2597,2609`
reads `exit_policy.EXPIRY_APPROACHING_DTE` / calls `exit_policy.macro_flatten_window_
days(...)` as MODULE-ATTRIBUTE lookups at call time — monkeypatching the module's
attribute genuinely moves the engine. `execution/portfolio.py:24-25` does `from
ait.execution.exit_policy import (EXPIRY_APPROACHING_DTE, ...)` — a VALUE import,
binding a private copy into `portfolio.py`'s own namespace at import time; monkeypatching
`exit_policy.EXPIRY_APPROACHING_DTE` afterward does NOT move what live already bound
(confirmed directly: a live-side probe of the patched constant kept reading the original
value). Consequence: "live and engine agree on `EXPIRY_APPROACHING_DTE`" can only be
proven honestly by a BOUNDARY-VALUE comparison (both close at dte==5, both hold at
dte==6), never by a shared-patch-and-compare. `macro_flatten_window_days` does NOT have
this trap — it reads a mutable dict (`MACRO_FLATTEN_WINDOW_DAYS`), and `setitem`-patching
the dict genuinely moves both call sites, since neither one binds a copy of the dict
itself. Future test-honesty work near an import boundary should check which import form
is in play before assuming a shared monkeypatch proves delegation.

REWRITES (both in `TestSharedExitPolicy`, `tests/test_r20_research_validity.py`):
1. `test_macro_flatten_windows_match_live_source` → renamed

   halves with a sweep over `{short_strangle, jade_lizard, cash_secured_put, covered_call,
   iron_condor} × {0,1,2,5,6}` days-to-event, driving the REAL engine

   helpers, adapted from `test_r15_review_fixes.py:319-363`), asserting both flatten
   exactly when `d2e <= window` and hold otherwise. Plus a delegation case:
   `monkeypatch.setitem(exit_policy.MACRO_FLATTEN_WINDOW_DAYS, "cash_secured_put", 3)` at
   d2e=3 flattens BOTH engines.
2. `test_expiry_close_dte_matches_live_source` → renamed
   `test_expiry_close_dte_matches_across_live_and_engine`. Kept the existing real
   `EXPIRY_APPROACHING_DTE == 5` assertion. Replaced both getsource halves with the
   boundary-value proof described in the finding above (both engines close at dte==5,

   DTE", 7)` moves the engine's own boundary to 7 — live cannot be proven this way, so it

## 2026-09-28 - W58 BUILT — historical options vol-surface backfill tool (QQQ, via
Polygon/Massive), proven end-to-end against real live data

W54's EV-comparison model needs historical per-strike, per-expiry option data to ever be
backtested — the 2026-09-27 scoping-note entry found this data doesn't exist and can't be
backfilled from anything already wired into this repo. This wave builds and proves the
tool that closes that gap. No production trading-path code touched — pure data
infrastructure, `src/ait/bot`/`execution`/`risk`/`strategies` all untouched.

**THE DATA SOURCE, TESTED LIVE BEFORE ANYTHING WAS BUILT.** The operator surfaced a
candidate ("Massive," `massive.com`, Options Basic free tier) mid-session; testing it
directly against the real API (not just reading the pricing page) found it IS Polygon
under a different brand — its own `NOT_AUTHORIZED` errors point at `polygon.io/pricing`
verbatim. Critically, the *existing* `.env` `POLYGON_API_KEY` already carries the
identical entitlement: same rolling 2-year window (tested the exact boundary — a range
straddling it silently truncates, a range fully outside it 403s), same 5-calls/min
throttle (empirically: 4 calls succeed, 5th+ return 429), byte-identical responses on
every comparison test. **No new account was needed.** No bid/ask anywhere on this tier —
confirmed by testing `/v3/quotes/...` and `/v2/last/nbbo/...` directly, both
`NOT_AUTHORIZED`; only trade-based OHLC (`o,h,l,c,v,vw,n,t`) is available.

**SCOPE, SETTLED OVER SEVERAL ROUNDS WITH THE OPERATOR** (each a real trade-off, not a
default): QQQ first (already has a 2-snapshot head start in `option_spread_samples`);
±30% moneyness band checked across each contract's WHOLE trading life, not a single date
(a contract ATM at issuance that drifts 46%+ out of band by expiry must still be
included — the naive expiry-day-only check was mutation-tested and confirmed to miss
exactly this case); full expiry density including 0-2 DTE, not a weekly sample (QQQ
turned out to have DAILY expiry cadence just like SPY — an earlier "9/month" estimate
was a live bug in the *research*, not the design: an unfiltered contracts query
truncated at the API's 1000-row page limit before reaching later dates in the month,
caught and corrected mid-conversation by re-querying with a strike filter); EOD
resolution only, never minute bars; IV/greeks precomputed and stored at ingestion, not
solved lazily; raw prices stored UNFILTERED (no `n`/`v` liquidity floor at ingestion —
that's separate, later, config-gated work reading this table, explicitly out of this
wave's scope); risk-free rate uses today's static `options.risk_free_rate` config
placeholder, stored per-row so a later re-solve pass (once a real historical rate series
exists — FRED's DGS1MO/DGS3MO is the recommended source, registered as a follow-up, not
built here) can update IV/greeks from already-stored raw prices with **no re-fetch**.

**BUILD.**
1. `src/ait/data/historical.py` — new `option_daily_bars` table (`underlying,
   option_ticker, expiry, right, strike, date, dte, open, high, low, close, volume, vwap,
   transactions, underlying_close, iv, iv_outcome, delta, gamma, theta, vega,
   risk_free_rate`, PK `(option_ticker, date)`, 2 indices). Deliberately NOT reusing
   `option_spread_samples`'s schema — its `bid`/`ask`/`mid` are `NOT NULL` and it's built
   for a live-quote source this OHLC/trade-based data doesn't have (the operator's own
   conclusion, confirmed against the DDL directly). `save_option_daily_bars()` mirrors
   `save_spread_samples`'s exact `INSERT OR IGNORE` + `executemany` idiom.
   `option_ticker_has_data()` is the resume-skip check — safe as a coarse per-contract
   test because `executemany` inside `with sqlite3.connect(...)` commits or rolls back as
   one unit, so a crash mid-write can never leave a partial batch for one contract.
2. New `scripts/backfill_option_history.py`. Flow: load the underlying's own daily
   closes (already in `daily_prices`, no separate fetch) → paginate Polygon's contracts
   reference endpoint → filter to the moneyness-over-life band → skip contracts already
   stored → fetch each survivor's full daily history in ONE call (`/v2/aggs/.../range/1/
   day/{from}/{to}`, up to 50k bars) → solve IV via the existing `solve_iv_from_price`/
   `compute_greeks_from_sigma` (`options_chain.py`, W55) → store raw + solved, unfiltered.
   Raw `requests` HTTP, not the `polygon-api-client` SDK's own pagination/retry (neither
   has a throttle hook for 5/min — confirmed by reading the installed SDK's source
   directly) — a uniform `time.sleep(pause_secs)` (default 12.5s) after every single
   outbound call, contracts-page or aggs-call alike, is what actually governs the whole
   job's pace. A `_POLYGON_AUTH_FAILURE_LIMIT`-style breaker (mirroring `MarketDataService
   `'s own idiom) aborts on repeated 401s rather than retrying into a dead key, while a
   per-request `NOT_AUTHORIZED` (e.g. the rolling window shifting mid-run) is logged and
   skipped, not treated as fatal — the two failure modes are genuinely different and were
   deliberately NOT conflated. `--max-contracts` is a smoke-test escape hatch;
   `--dry-run` prints the request plan without fetching or writing.

**PROOF.**
- Unit tests: `TestOptionDailyBarsTable` (6, in `test_backfill_historical_data.py`,
  modeled directly on `TestSpreadSamplesTable`'s own convention) + `test_backfill_
  option_history.py` (8: the moneyness-over-life filter's 3 real cases plus an empty-
  window case, and `process_contract`'s resume-skip / real-IV-solve / missing-underlying-
  close / no-bars-returned cases, against a fake `PolygonClient` at the network boundary

  predicted, reverted.
- **Live smoke tests against the REAL API** (not mocked, matching this session's
  standing "prove it against reality" discipline for W53/W55): first attempt used a
  hardcoded 2024 date that had — since this session began — drifted outside the *now-

  include this timeframe` response live and confirming the script's own default
  (`start_date = end_date - 730 days`, computed at runtime, never hardcoded) is the
  right design, not merely a convenience. Corrected to relative recent dates and re-ran:
  **9 real rows landed in `data/historical.db`'s `option_daily_bars`** across two runs
  (2 `solved`, 7 `failed_arbitrage`) — a genuine, honest mix, not cherry-picked: the

## 2026-09-28 - W58 FOLLOW-UP: operational hardening for the multi-day backfill run —
network-retry resilience, a status file, and the launchd wall re-confirmed

The operator seriously considered launchd (auto-restart across sleep/reboot) for the
real ~20-day backfill run and correctly abandoned it once this repo's own prior finding
was surfaced: launchd-spawned processes cannot access this repo at all (PLAN.md,
2026-09-15 "W16b correction" — `~/Documents` is macOS-TCC-protected, no consent-dialog
path exists for a headless job). Resolved design instead: the operator starts the
script themselves in a normal terminal (inherits Terminal/VS Code's already-granted
Documents access, no TCC wall), optionally `nohup`'d, and manually resumes after any
interruption — safe today (resume-skip via `option_ticker_has_data`, proven live in the
original W58 build) but not yet OBSERVABLE or RESILIENT to what an unattended multi-day
stretch actually hits. This entry closes both gaps.

**FINDING, CONFIRMED BY DIRECT READ:** `PolygonClient._get()` had no retry around the
HTTP call — a `requests.exceptions.RequestException` (connection drop, timeout — exactly
what a post-sleep WiFi reconnection looks like) propagated straight up uncaught.
`get_daily_bars()`'s failures were already survived (the per-contract loop in `main()`
already wraps `process_contract(...)` in `try/except Exception: continue`), but
`list_contracts_pages()` — called once, up front, for the whole multi-page contracts
enumeration — had no such protection: a network blip during that phase crashed the
entire process with a raw traceback. The one real structural gap, not a rewrite of
working code.

**BUILD.**
1. `PolygonClient._get()` — bounded retry loop (backoff `[0, 5, 10, 20, 40, 60]`
   seconds, patient enough for a typical post-wake reconnection), catching
   `requests.exceptions.RequestException` specifically (not a bare `except Exception` —
   a real programming error still surfaces immediately, isn't silently retried).
   Exhausting retries raises a clear `RuntimeError` wrapping the original exception.
2. `main()`'s enumeration call is now wrapped in its own try/except: a persistent
   failure there logs `backfill_enumeration_failed`, writes the status file as
   `status: "crashed"`, and exits 1 — closing the structural gap above.
3. A top-level try/except around the whole run (`main()` now delegates to `_run()`) so
   ANY otherwise-unhandled exception still produces one clear final log line and a
   `status: "crashed"` status-file write before exiting non-zero, regardless of where
   something breaks.
4. New status file, `data/backfill_option_history_status.json` (same "small file in
   `data/`, cheap to `cat`" spirit as the existing `data/bot_heartbeat` convention,
   just with real progress fields a bare timestamp can't carry): written at run start
   (`status: "running"`, `contracts_total`, `started_at`), after every processed
   contract (`contracts_done`, `rows_written`, `current_ticker`, `last_updated`), on
   clean completion (`status: "complete"`), and on any crash path (`status: "crashed"`,
   `last_error`). One `cat` now answers "still running?", "how far along?", and "why did
   it die?" without scrolling a log.
5. Docstring rewritten with the actual recommended operational pattern (see RUN
   COMMANDS below) — including the launchd-wall explanation inline, so the reasoning
   isn't lost outside this register entry.

**A REAL BUG FOUND BY THE NEW TESTS THEMSELVES, before this entry was written**:
`write_status(path: Path = STATUS_FILE, ...)`'s default argument was bound to
`STATUS_FILE`'s value ONCE, at function-definition time (a classic Python mutable/
late-binding-default gotcha) — a test that `monkeypatch.setattr(m, "STATUS_FILE",
tmp_path / "status.json")` to redirect writes away from the real `data/` directory
silently failed to do so; the function kept writing to the original path regardless.
Caught immediately (`FileNotFoundError` at the tmp_path location — the real file went
elsewhere), fixed by resolving `STATUS_FILE` inside the function body at call time
(`path = path or STATUS_FILE`) instead of as a bound default. A leftover fake status
file this bug's own test run left in the real `data/` directory (`status: "complete",
symbol: "QQQ", rows_written: 3` — obviously synthetic test data, not real backfill
progress) was found and deleted before this entry was written, so nobody mistakes it
for real progress later.

**RUN COMMANDS** (per the operator's explicit request — copying the docstring's own
canonical text so it isn't only discoverable by reading the script):

Always run from the repo root (`trade_v2`) — `--db-path`'s default and the status
file's path are both resolved relative to the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY at invocation,
not to the script's own location (unlike `.env` loading, which resolves correctly
regardless of cwd via `apply_runtime_env_defaults()`'s own `REPO_ROOT` computation).
Running from elsewhere would silently create/use a different, empty `data/
historical.db` with no error — the operator explicitly chose documentation over a code
fix for this (`STATUS_FILE`/`--db-path` staying cwd-relative), since always invoking
from the repo root is how they'll actually use it.

```
cd /path/to/trade_v2

# Foreground (blocks the terminal, stops if you close it):
python scripts/backfill_option_history.py

# Background, survives closing the terminal (recommended for the real run):
nohup python scripts/backfill_option_history.py \
    > logs/backfill_option_history.log 2>&1 &
```

Checking on it: `cat data/backfill_option_history_status.json` (structured snapshot —
stale `last_updated` while the process is confirmed alive means something's stuck;
`status: "crashed"` means `last_error` says why); `tail -f logs/backfill_option_
history.log` (live detail); `ps aux | grep backfill_option_history` (is the process
alive). Interrupted for any reason — just re-run the identical command; already-fetched
contracts are skipped, nothing lost, nothing re-downloaded.

**WINDOWS, PER THE OPERATOR'S QUESTION.** Confirmed: `POLYGON_API_KEY` is already set
in the Windows box's own `.env`. Code-level assessment (not live-tested on Windows):
the script is expected to run there unmodified — pure Python, `pathlib` throughout (no
hardcoded `/`-separated strings), no POSIX-only calls (no `os.fork`, no Unix-specific
signal handling), and `.env`/config loading is already proven cross-platform (the live
bot itself runs on the Windows box today). The one piece that IS platform-specific is
the launch command, not the code: `nohup` is bash/POSIX-only. The Windows equivalent
for "survives closing the terminal" is PowerShell's `Start-Process`:

```
Start-Process python -ArgumentList "scripts\backfill_option_history.py" `
    -RedirectStandardOutput logs\backfill_option_history.log `
    -RedirectStandardError logs\backfill_option_history.err -WindowStyle Hidden
```

(also run from the repo root, same reasoning as above). Flagged honestly as untested,
not asserted as proven — the Mac is where this was actually built and smoke-tested.

**PROOF.** 4 new tests in `tests/test_backfill_option_history.py` (now 12 total):
`TestPolygonClientGetRetry` (retries-then-succeeds against a real
`requests.exceptions.ConnectionError`-raising fake session, and exhausts-retries-raises)
and `TestRunEnumerationFailure`/`TestRunStatusFile` (drive the real `main()`/`_run()`
end to end with `enumerate_contracts`/`process_contract` faked at the network boundary,
asserting on the real written status-file JSON). Mutation-checked the retry logic:
temporarily truncated `NETWORK_RETRY_BACKOFFS` to a single attempt, confirmed the
retries-then-succeeds test failed exactly as predicted (`RuntimeError: ... after 1
attempts`), reverted — `git diff --stat scripts/backfill_option_history.py` confirmed
clean before moving on. `python -m compileall -q scripts tests`: OK. Re-ran a small
real dry-run (`--max-contracts 3 --dry-run`) against the live API after all changes —
still works end to end. Full fast lane: **2540 passed / 1 failed / 46 skipped / 153
deselected, 976.80s (16m16s)** — the one failure is the standing `AIT_MARKET_DATA_TYPE`
divergence; zero new failures. Count check against the original W58 build's fast lane
(2536+1=2537 total): this run is 2540+1=2541 — a delta of exactly +4, matching the 4
new tests precisely (no other test file touched).

STATE AT HANDOFF. `scripts/backfill_option_history.py` and `tests/test_backfill_
option_history.py` are the only files changed. Zero production trading-path files
touched. Zero config changes. Nothing to deploy or restart — this tool still runs

## 2026-09-28 - W59 BUILT — historical risk-free-rate series, closes W58's registered
follow-up; real SOFR term structure re-solves the 9 existing option_daily_bars rows

Every row `backfill_option_history.py` writes stores a PLACEHOLDER risk-free rate (the
static `options.risk_free_rate` config value, 5%) — a deliberate decision registered at
build time: use the placeholder now, store it per-row, re-solve later once a real
historical rate series exists. This wave builds that series and does the re-solve. No
production trading-path code touched — `src/ait/bot`/`execution`/`risk`/`strategies` all
untouched; the live bot's own IV solve still uses the static config placeholder
unchanged (this wave only rewrites already-stored historical rows).

**SOFR, NOT TREASURY — REVISED AFTER OPERATOR PUSHBACK.** The first draft of this plan
used Treasury CMT rates (DGS1MO/DGS3MO) with a binary switch at 45 DTE. The operator
rejected it on sight with two questions: are we getting SOFR, and are we getting a real
term structure covering the short end (0-2 DTE) as well as the 14-60 DTE calibration
window? Both were right. Re-researched live before revising: `SOFR`, `SOFR30DAYAVG`,
`SOFR90DAYAVG`, `SOFR180DAYAVG` (NY Fed compounded averages) are all free, keyless, and
confirmed live via curl against FRED's public CSV endpoint, all starting 2018 —
comfortably before any date the options backfill's rolling 2-year window will ever
reach. SOFR is the actual modern industry-standard risk-free reference for derivatives
pricing (the post-LIBOR standard); Treasury CMT's shortest tenor (1-month) has no usable
anchor for 0-2 DTE at all. Final design is a genuine 4-point term structure, not a
threshold.

**DESIGN.** `src/ait/data/historical.py`: new `SOFR_TENOR_DAYS` mapping (column name →
tenor in days: `sofr`→1, `sofr_30d_avg`→30, `sofr_90d_avg`→90, `sofr_180d_avg`→180) and a
pure `interpolate_rate(tenor_points, dte) -> float | None` function — piecewise-linear
across whichever anchors are present, flat-extrapolated beyond the shortest/longest (the
same scheme this codebase's own half-built VIX9D/VIX/VIX3M/VIX6M term-structure idea
already uses elsewhere, per the earlier W54 scoping-note entry, just applied to SOFR).
New `risk_free_rates` table (`date TEXT PRIMARY KEY, sofr, sofr_30d_avg, sofr_90d_avg,
sofr_180d_avg`) with `save_risk_free_rates(df) -> int`, an upsert (`ON CONFLICT DO
UPDATE`) — unlike option-bar ingestion's `INSERT OR IGNORE`, this data SHOULD refresh on
re-fetch since FRED occasionally revises recent prints. `get_risk_free_rate(as_of, dte)
-> float | None` forward-fills to the most recent row with `date <= as_of` (FRED
publishes only on business days), then calls `interpolate_rate`. `update_option_bar_iv(
option_ticker, date, iv, iv_outcome, delta, gamma, theta, vega, risk_free_rate) -> int`
is a plain `UPDATE ... WHERE option_ticker=? AND date=?` — deliberately never touches the
raw price columns, per this file's own DATA-H2 lesson (INSERT OR REPLACE nulls out
untouched columns; a plain UPDATE has no such hazard).

New script `scripts/backfill_risk_free_rate.py`, two phases. Phase A always runs (even
under `--dry-run`, deliberately — an empty `risk_free_rates` table would make
`get_risk_free_rate` always return `None`, making a dry-run report meaningless): fetches
all 4 SOFR series via the existing `MacroDataFetcher.fetch_series()` (`src/ait/data/
macro.py`, reused as-is, zero new HTTP/CSV code) and upserts them. Phase B (gated by
`--dry-run`) reads `option_daily_bars` directly, computes each row's real rate via
`get_risk_free_rate(row.date, row.dte)`, skips if missing or already within 1e-6 of the
stored rate, otherwise re-runs the same W55 `solve_iv_from_price`/`compute_greeks_from_
sigma` pipeline the original backfill used against the row's own already-stored `close`/
`underlying_close` and calls `update_option_bar_iv`. `_update_with_retry` tolerates a
transient `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` with a short `[0,1,2,5]`s
backoff (local disk contention from a concurrently-running `backfill_option_history.py`
— a different failure class from that script's own network-retry backoff, so a much
shorter budget) and re-raises any non-lock `OperationalError` immediately. CLI:
`--symbol` (optional filter), `--db-path`/`--table-prefix`, `--dry-run`.

**A REAL BUG THIS WAVE'S OWN TESTS CAUGHT BEFORE IT REACHED LIVE DATA.** FRED publishes
these series as raw percentages (`4.12` meaning 4.12%), but `solve_iv_from_price`'s `r`
and `options.risk_free_rate`'s own config units are a decimal fraction (`0.0412`).
Feeding the raw percentage straight into Black-Scholes would have been badly wrong (a
~412% "rate"). Caught by `test_resolves_when_the_real_rate_differs_from_stored` asserting
`pytest.approx(0.0412)` and getting `4.12` — fixed with a `series / 100.0` conversion in
`fetch_rate_table()`, applied once at the fetch boundary so everything downstream (the
stored table, `get_risk_free_rate`, `interpolate_rate`) stays unit-consistent with the
rest of the codebase.

**PROOF.** 17 new tests in `tests/test_backfill_historical_data.py` (now 48 total):
`TestInterpolateRate` (exact anchors, interpolation, both flat-extrapolation edges, empty/
unsorted input), `TestRiskFreeRatesTable` (schema, save/round-trip, upsert-overwrites-on-
refresh, empty-df), `TestGetRiskFreeRate` (forward-fill, before-any-data returns `None`,
interpolation from a stored row), `TestUpdateOptionBarIv` (overwrites iv/greeks without
touching raw price columns, no-such-row is a no-op not an error). New `tests/test_
backfill_risk_free_rate.py` (12 tests, no `inspect.getsource`, no real HTTP — `fetch_
rate_table` tested against a fake `MacroDataFetcher`): `TestResolveRows` (real re-solve
against a real temp store — not mocked — including the percent/decimal bug's own
regression test, skip-when-unchanged, skip-when-no-rate-data, dry-run doesn't write,
`--symbol` filter isolation), `TestUpdateWithRetry` (against a fake store that raises a
real `sqlite3.OperationalError("database is locked")`: retries-then-succeeds, exhausts-
and-raises, non-lock-error-not-retried), `TestFetchRateTable` (merge, the percent-to-
decimal conversion, missing-series-tolerance, all-missing-returns-empty). Mutation-
checked 3 mechanisms, each temporarily broken, confirmed the relevant test failed for the
predicted reason, reverted, confirmed `git diff --stat` clean: `interpolate_rate`'s
linear-fraction math; `get_risk_free_rate`'s forward-fill query (`<=` → `=`); the percent-
to-decimal conversion (removed `/100.0`, confirmed the exact `4.12 vs 0.0412` mismatch).
`python -m compileall -q src scripts tests`: OK.

**LIVE SMOKE TEST, against the real `data/historical.db`** (checked `data/backfill_
option_history_status.json` and the process list first — confirmed no operator backfill
run active at the time, safe to proceed without lock contention). `--dry-run`: fetched
and stored 2142 real SOFR rows from FRED via the real `MacroDataFetcher` (not curl, not a
fake — the actual reused code path), reported `9 rows checked, 9 would be re-solved, 0
already match, 0 have no rate data yet` against the 9 pre-existing rows from the original
W58 build's own smoke tests (all of which carried the 0.05 placeholder). Real run (no
`--dry-run`): `resolve_complete checked=9 resolved=9 skipped_no_rate=0
skipped_unchanged=0`. Direct read of the table after confirmed all 9 rows' `risk_free_
rate` changed from the 0.05 placeholder to real SOFR-derived values (0.0364–0.0368 for
these rows' dte=0 — the overnight `sofr` anchor, correctly selected by `interpolate_
rate`), with `iv`/`iv_outcome` genuinely re-solved alongside (unchanged `failed_
arbitrage` outcomes stayed `failed_arbitrage`, `solved` rows kept solving with the new
rate baked in — confirms the re-solve pipeline is deterministic on price, not silently
flipping outcomes).

Full fast lane: `tests/test_backfill_historical_data.py` + `tests/test_backfill_risk_
free_rate.py` together, 60/60 passed standalone. Full suite: **2569 passed / 1 failed /
46 skipped / 153 deselected, 1227.86s (20m27s)** — the one failure is the same standing
`test_r19_config_authority.py::TestContractIsTheSingleAuthority::
test_applier_and_readers_share_one_table` (`AIT_MARKET_DATA_TYPE` local-`.env`
divergence) every entry this session has already named; zero new failures. Count check
against the W58 build's own fast lane (2540+1=2541 non-deselected): this run is
2569+1=2570 — a delta of exactly +29, matching the 17+12=29 new tests precisely (no
other test file touched).

STATE AT HANDOFF. Files touched: `src/ait/data/historical.py`, `tests/test_backfill_
historical_data.py` (both modified), `scripts/backfill_risk_free_rate.py`, `tests/test_
backfill_risk_free_rate.py` (both new). Zero production trading-path files touched. Zero
