## 2026-09-28 - W56 BUILT — tested/untested condor-defense decision logic, a pure
additive module, nothing wired to any live path

SCOPE. Per the 2026-09-22 ROADMAP EXTENSION (`:8783-8905`): W55 (synthetic per-leg delta)
is built; W56 is the decision layer that reads a tested short's delta+DTE and decides
hold / roll-untested / roll-tested / close against the operator's playbook table
(0.25/0.30/0.40 delta, 14/21 DTE — `:8848-8869`; the document itself isn't in the repo).
W55's own NEXT flagged two prerequisites for WIRING this in: its own live TWS/RTH
validation run (still not run) and a shared non-boolean `check_positions` output W54
also needs (`PositionStatus` today is `should_exit: bool` + `exit_reason: str`,
`portfolio.py:41-64`). This wave does not touch either — it builds the decision logic and
config surface as an additive module nothing calls, the same convention W53's
`roll_selector.py` and W55's `synthetic_delta.py` used. No production trading-path
behavior changes; `portfolio.py` is untouched.

THREE OPERATOR DECISIONS THIS SESSION (the [4] sketch's table leaves real gaps and
ambiguities the operator resolved before building):
1. **Scope: pure module only.** No change to `portfolio.py`/`PositionStatus` this wave —
   that structural extension is deferred to when W54 and W56's wiring are designed
   together, per W55's own NEXT.
2. **Table gaps** (tested-short |Δ| 0.30–0.40 at ≤21 DTE; 0.25–0.30 at >21 DTE; 0.25–0.40
   at <14 DTE — cells neither row of the table covers) → **HOLD**, reason
   `no_rule_matched`. Cheapest/safest arm; the existing exits (1.25x stop, touch stop,
   DTE≤5 close) still backstop the position regardless.
3. **A roll the `side` setting disallows** (e.g. the table says roll-tested but
   `side=untested_only`) → **HOLD**, reason names the blocked roll. `side` governs rolls
   only — the close row is never side-filtered, so a genuine 0.40-delta blowout still
   closes under any `side` setting.

DESIGN.
1. **`CondorDefenseConfig`** (`src/ait/config/settings.py`, after `AssignmentResponseConfig`,
   registered on `Settings.condor_defense`) — `enabled: bool = False` (GAP_AUDIT_R7
   POST-VERDICT reasoning, `:8871-8882`: thin edge at 1 contract, changing exit mechanics
   mid-sample corrupts the 50-close measurement — stays off pending that verdict),
   `side: Literal["tested_only","untested_only","both"] = "untested_only"`, and the table's
   6 threshold fields (`monitor_delta_max`, `roll_untested_delta_min/max`,
   `roll_untested_dte_min/max`, `roll_tested_delta_min`, `roll_tested_dte_min`,
   `close_delta_threshold`) at the table's own defaults. A `model_validator(mode="after")`
   refuses inverted/overlapping bands (`monitor_delta_max <= roll_untested_delta_min <
   roll_untested_delta_max <= roll_tested_delta_min < close_delta_threshold`, and the DTE
   windows can't overlap either) — a future retune that breaks the ordering fails fast at
   config load, not silently at decision time. `roll_tested_dte_min` (22) is its own
   explicit field rather than "not in the untested window," specifically so the two bands
   can't silently drift into overlap if either is retuned independently.
   `untested_roll_target_delta` from the [4] sketch is deliberately NOT added — nothing in
   W56 reads it; it ships with its actual consumer, W57. Matching `condor_defense:` block
   added to `config.yaml`, `enabled: false`, same commit as the code (no
   `extra="forbid"` deploy-ordering hazard).
2. **`src/ait/execution/condor_defense.py`** (new, called by nothing):
   `classify_tested_delta(abs_delta, dte, config) -> (DefenseAction, reason)` is the pure
   table lookup — no data access, kept separate from the rest so band edges are testable
   with exact numbers alone (same split this register used for `interpolate_rate` vs. the
   DB-backed `get_risk_free_rate` in W59, immediately above). Order: close threshold first
   (applies at any DTE, never side-filtered) → monitor floor → tested band (needs both the
   delta AND `dte >= roll_tested_dte_min`) → untested band (delta AND DTE window) →
   otherwise `no_rule_matched`.
   `evaluate_condor_defense(trade, option_marks, spot, dte, config) -> DefenseDecision`
   does the data work: `enabled` is checked FIRST, before touching marks or the legs JSON
   at all (`disabled` reason, so an empty `option_marks` dict never even gets read);
   `trade.strategy != "iron_condor"` → `not_an_iron_condor`; reuses `_at_risk_vertical`
   (`roll_selector.py:41`, W53) to require a clean short+long pair on BOTH sides before
   picking a tested side (`no_clean_condor` otherwise) — an ambiguous condor never
   half-decides. Never raises; every failure path returns a HOLD with a named reason,
   matching `select_roll_target`'s and `synthetic_leg_greeks`'s own fail-safe convention.
3. **Tested-side selection is by relative strike distance to spot, not by comparing two
   solved deltas.** `(spot - put_short)/spot` vs. `(call_short - spot)/spot`; the smaller
   wins (an ITM short's distance goes negative, so it's always picked over an OTM one;
   ties — a genuinely centered condor — go to the put, where skew makes the real delta
   larger at the same relative distance). Deliberately not "whichever leg's synthetic delta
   solves larger": the untested side is often far OTM with a near-zero mark, exactly where
   W55's IV solve is most likely to fail (`failed_other` / a sub-floor sigma) — requiring
   BOTH sides to solve successfully would blind the decision precisely when the tested side
   is under real pressure. Only the tested short's own delta (via `synthetic_vertical_
   deltas`, `synthetic_delta.py:100`, W55) is ever solved for; the untested side's marks
   (and even the tested side's own paired long's mark) can be entirely absent without
   blocking a decision — proven by a dedicated test, not assumed.

PROOF. `tests/test_w56_condor_defense.py`, 43 new tests, no `inspect.getsource`, no
MagicMock for `option_marks` (real dict, matching W51/W55's own convention) — driven end

fixture's precondition (the solved |Δ| really lands in its intended band) is asserted, not

band edge (inclusive/exclusive checked explicitly, e.g. exactly 0.30@18-DTE falls through
to `no_rule_matched` since the untested upper bound is exclusive); `evaluate_condor_
defense`'s four live-band decisions; the side filter both directions plus `both`; close
never side-filtered; tested-side selection (call tested near the money, ITM put tested
over an OTM call); every failure path (`disabled` before any solve, non-condor, malformed

## 2026-09-28 - W53's PLACING RUN ATTEMPTED, BLOCKED — a real chain-fetch bug found live,
`open` NOT run, no orders placed

With TWS paper reachable and `is_market_open()` confirmed True (the same live window the
entry immediately above used for W55's validation), attempted `scripts/probe_w53_roll_
atomicity.py preflight` as the documented first step before `open`/`roll`/`flatten`.
`preflight` places no orders by design — safe to attempt regardless of outcome.

RESULT: **preflight did not complete.** Two attempts, 100s and 240s bounded (`timeout`),
both ended the same way — no JSON result, no traceback, no `GUARD REFUSED`/`UNEXPECTED
ERROR` line, process dead, log static, nothing left listening on clientId 97 or lingering
in `ps aux` afterward (confirmed both times). Both logs show the identical pathology: an
unbroken flood of `Error 200: No security definition has been found` and `Unknown
contract` for hundreds of `SPY` strikes (roughly 616–713 and 639–713 across the two
attempts, expiries 20261006/20261012) interleaved with `Error 10091` (real-time top-of-
book not entitled, delayed available) — never converging to a usable quote set in either
window.

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by direct read of `_get_ibkr_chain` (`src/ait/data/
options_chain.py:716-722`), not guessed: `target_strikes` is filtered from `chain_def.
strikes` by `abs(s - price) <= price * 0.20` (a flat ±20% band) with no per-expiry
availability check. `reqSecDefOptParamsAsync` returns ONE combined strike set for the
whole trading class across ALL its expiries, not one set per expiry — near-dated weeklies
routinely list a narrower strike range than the class's LEAPS. At SPY's current spot
(~$765, confirmed via the W55 validation entry immediately above), ±20% is a ~$306 band
in $0.50/$1 increments — several hundred strikes, a large fraction of which belong to
other expiries and don't exist for the specific near-dated expiry `_fetch_ibkr_expiry`
then tries to qualify them against, one `Option()` object per strike per right. This is
the SAME failure class the file's own R16 comment two lines above already documents for a
related symptom (wrong `chain_def` class serving nonexistent strikes) — this is a
different trigger (right class, wrong per-expiry strike scope) landing on the identical
symptom (`Option()` qualification against strikes IBKR doesn't recognize for that
contract).

Why this wasn't seen before in this session: `smoke_deploy.py`'s own SPY scan (this
entry's predecessor, `17:47:22`) logged `scan_symbol_timing chain=0` — a near-zero chain
fetch, meaning it hit either the chain cache or a DTE-range/expiry combination that
doesn't trigger the pathology (the live bot's own `options.dte_range` default differs
from this probe's `OPEN_DTE_MIN=5/OPEN_DTE_MAX=10`). W55's own live validation
(immediately above) used a DIFFERENT, already-cached SPY chain fetched moments earlier in
the session, at a wider/different DTE window, and also completed cleanly. This is the
FIRST time this session exercised `_get_ibkr_chain` fresh against these specific near-
dated 5-10 DTE expiries at today's live SPY price — and it's a live, reproducible bug,
not a fluke: identical symptom on both the 100s and 240s attempts, different expiry
(20261006 then 20261012 — the chain naturally rolled between attempts, ruling out a
one-off transient IBKR-side glitch on a single expiry).

DECISION: **did not proceed to `open`.** `cmd_open` calls the exact same `pick_vertical` ->
`chain_service.get_chain` path that just failed to converge twice: placing a real order
(even a capped, paper, auto-flatten-guarded one) against a chain-fetch pipeline that
cannot currently produce a clean strike list would be placing an order based on
whatever partial/garbage state existed at time of failure, not a validated decision. The
probe's own safety design (paper-only, capped, auto-flatten-on-error) protects against a
BAD fill, not against building the order request on top of a chain that never finished
resolving in the first place — a different risk this session chose not to take.

STATE AT HANDOFF. No code changed. No orders placed (preflight never calls `placeOrder`
by design; confirmed no lingering process/connection either time). No `reports/w53_probe/
2026-09-28/state.json` was ever written (both hangs occurred before `cmd_preflight`
reaches its own `save_state` call) — nothing for a future `flatten`/`status` invocation to

## 2026-09-28 - FIXED — `_get_ibkr_chain`'s all-expiries strike-band bug, proven live:
W53's probe now completes end-to-end with a real preflight result

Closes the bug the entry immediately above found and registered. No W-number assigned —
this is a bug fix to shared, R16-audited data infrastructure, not a new capability wave.

SCOPE. `src/ait/data/options_chain.py`, two methods, no other `src/` files, no config
changes. `_get_ibkr_chain` (`:654-737`) no longer computes a `target_strikes` list from
`chain_def.strikes` (the trading class's ALL-EXPIRIES combined strike set from
`reqSecDefOptParamsAsync`) and reuses it across every target expiry. `_fetch_ibkr_expiry`
(`:747-...`) drops its `strikes` parameter and instead, per expiry, calls
`reqContractDetailsAsync(Option(symbol, exp_str, 0.0, right, "SMART",
tradingClass=symbol))` once per side (confirmed against ib_insync 0.9.86's own source:
`strike=0.0` is `Option`'s own default, `ib.py:932-941`'s docstring confirms it returns
every real, listed match) — each result's `cd.contract` already carries a real `conId`,

per-expiry contracts) — filtering now costs zero extra round trips regardless of band

## 2026-09-28 - BUILT — `check_positions` non-boolean decision-output extension (shared
design, no wave number): the sole remaining blocker for wiring W54 and W56, closed at the
shape level

SCOPE, deliberately narrow. Two registered items both needed the same structural
extension before either could ever be wired into the live exit path: W54's rule 3/rule 3e
need to stop unconditionally closing an at-risk leg and instead consult `assignment_
response.policy` to decide close-vs-roll (finding `[3]f`, `:8737-8740`: "a control-flow
change to `check_positions`'s exit-decision shape ... not an additive elif"); W56
(`condor_defense.py`, built and live-validated earlier this session) needs a caller that
can express hold/roll-untested/roll-tested/close instead of a bare boolean. The
2026-09-22 roadmap entry named this explicitly: "Design once, use for both" (`:8887`).
This wave builds ONLY the shared shape — it does NOT wire rule 3/3e to consult the policy
or call `roll_selector.select_roll_target` (still W54's own job per `[3]f`), and does NOT
wire `condor_defense.py` into `check_positions` (a separate future step). Every existing
exit rule's behavior is byte-identical to before this wave.

**Touches `execution/portfolio.py`** — a CLAUDE.md-flagged critical/sensitive area. The
touch is deliberately minimal and was flagged plainly in this wave's plan before starting,
approved as that plan's own confirmation: two new dataclass fields with defaults
(backward-compatible with every existing keyword construction site) and a small derivation
inserted at the single point `_evaluate_position` already builds its return value.

DESIGN. `PositionAction(str, Enum)`: `HOLD`, `CLOSE`, `PARTIAL_CLOSE`, `ROLL` —
deliberately simpler than `condor_defense.DefenseAction` (`HOLD`/`ROLL_UNTESTED`/
`ROLL_TESTED`/`CLOSE`, a decision TABLE's internal vocabulary); `PositionAction` is
`check_positions`' OUTPUT vocabulary, what a future executor would act on. A future wiring
wave maps `DefenseAction.ROLL_UNTESTED`/`ROLL_TESTED` both onto `PositionAction.ROLL`
(`roll_side` names which physical side, `exit_reason` carries the table-row nuance) —
not decided or built here, just proven sufficient (see Proof). `PositionStatus` (`:42-96`)
gains `action: PositionAction = PositionAction.HOLD` and `roll_side: str | None = None`,
appended after the existing `marks_missing: bool = False` so every existing keyword
construction site stays valid unchanged. `_derive_position_action(should_exit: bool,
partial_exit_quantity: int) -> PositionAction` is a small, pure, module-level function
(same split this register uses repeatedly: `classify_tested_delta` vs `evaluate_condor_
defense`, `interpolate_rate` vs `get_risk_free_rate`) — `should_exit` → `CLOSE`;
else `partial_exit_quantity > 0` → `PARTIAL_CLOSE`; else `HOLD`. Never returns `ROLL` —
nothing produces that value yet; a future rule sets `action=ROLL` directly instead of
calling this. `_evaluate_position`'s existing final `return PositionStatus(...)` gets two
new kwargs (`action=_derive_position_action(should_exit, partial_exit_quantity)`,
`roll_side=None`); nothing above that line changes — every one of the ~10 existing rules
(1, 1b, 2, 3, 3a-3e, 4, 5) keeps setting `should_exit`/`exit_reason`/`partial_exit_quantity`
exactly as before. No caller of `check_positions`/`PositionStatus` (`orchestrator.py`,
dashboards) is touched — the new fields are unused by every existing consumer.

## 2026-09-28 - WIRED — `condor_defense.py` into `check_positions`, decision-only: the
last step of the W55→W56 arc, closed

SCOPE. `condor_defense.py` (W56) and its own live-validated synthetic-delta solve (W55)
existed but were called by nothing. The `check_positions` decision-output extension
(immediately above) exists specifically to give a caller like this something richer than
a boolean to report through. This wave makes `_evaluate_position` actually call `evaluate_
condor_defense` for open iron condors and report its verdict.

**Two operator decisions this session, both toward the conservative arm:**
1. **Decision-only, for both CLOSE and ROLL.** `condor_defense.enabled` stays `False` by
   default, unchanged. Once flipped to `True` in the future, NOTHING about real order
   behavior changes — the verdict is recorded in `PositionStatus.action`/`roll_side`/the
   new `action_reason` field, never in `should_exit`. `should_exit` stays 100% owned by
   the existing ~10 rules exactly as before this wave. This was the wave's own centerpiece
   and its primary proof target (see Proof).
2. This wave does NOT make condor_defense's verdict actionable — a separate, explicitly-
   approved future step would be needed for either CLOSE (could reuse the existing
   should_exit path near-immediately, no new order machinery needed) or ROLL (still has
   no executor at all — that's W57's job).

DESIGN. `src/ait/execution/portfolio.py`: `PositionStatus` gains `action_reason: str |
None = None`, deliberately separate from `exit_reason` (which stays should_exit/partial_
exit_quantity's own narrative) so a condor_defense verdict never collides with an
unrelated partial-exit message in the same tick. `_map_condor_defense_action(DefenseAction)
-> PositionAction` — a small pure function (same split as `_derive_position_action`/
`classify_tested_delta`) collapsing condor_defense's richer table vocabulary (`HOLD`/
`ROLL_UNTESTED`/`ROLL_TESTED`/`CLOSE`) onto `check_positions`' simpler one (`HOLD`/`CLOSE`/
`ROLL`) — `roll_side`/`action_reason` carry which physical side and why.
`PortfolioManager.__init__` gains `condor_defense_config: CondorDefenseConfig | None =
None` (same pattern `exit_config` already uses; defaults to `CondorDefenseConfig()`,
`enabled=False`). In `_evaluate_position`, right after rule 3e and before rule 4 (partial
exit): if `not should_exit` and `getattr(self, "_condor_defense_config", None)` is set
(`getattr`-guarded, matching rule 3e's own `_dividends` convention, so every existing test
constructing `PortfolioManager` via `__new__` — all 324 of them — is unaffected), call the
synchronous `evaluate_condor_defense(trade, option_marks, current_price, dte, self.
_condor_defense_config)`. Gated on `not should_exit` so a position some OTHER rule already
wants to close never gets a redundant/confusing verdict logged alongside it. At the return
site: `action = condor_action if condor_action != HOLD else _derive_position_action(...)`,
`roll_side`/`action_reason` set from the verdict when non-HOLD, else `None` — byte-
identical to before this wave whenever condor_defense wasn't computed or returned `HOLD`.
`src/ait/bot/orchestrator.py`'s `PortfolioManager(...)` construction (`:358-366`) gains
`condor_defense_config=settings.condor_defense` — the actual live wiring.

## 2026-09-28 - MADE ACTIONABLE — condor_defense's CLOSE verdict now sets should_exit; ROLL
stays decision-only, a real PDT-interaction bug found and fixed during design

SCOPE, per the operator's explicit choice: the just-shipped wiring (immediately above) was
fully decision-only for both CLOSE and ROLL. This wave activates ONLY the CLOSE arm — a
tested-short delta ≥ `close_delta_threshold` (0.40 by default) now sets `should_exit=True`
and reuses the existing, already-audited close path, the SAME mechanism every other exit
rule (touch stop, take-profit, assignment risk, ...) already uses for iron condors. No new
executor code anywhere. ROLL is untouched — still fully decision-only, since it has no
executor at all (that remains W57's own, separately-scoped, much larger job from the
original roadmap sizing table; not to be confused with this CLOSE-only change).

**Real consequence, stated plainly**: once an operator flips `condor_defense.enabled` to
`True` in `config.yaml` (still `false` today, unchanged by this wave), a tested short
crossing 0.40 delta will cause a REAL close order on a live/paper iron condor. This wave
changes no default, no config, and no currently-running behavior — only what a future
explicit opt-in would do. The live bot was NOT restarted.

**A REAL DESIGN ISSUE FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING THIS, not from a live bug**: the condor_
defense call site sits between rule 3e and rule 4, but rule 5 (further down) can reset
`should_exit=False`/`exit_reason="exit_blocked_by_pdt"` when a day-trade would occur. The
first draft captured a local `condor_action` before rule 5 ran and used IT (not the final
`should_exit`) at the return site to decide `PositionStatus.action` — meaning a PDT-vetoed
condor_defense close would have reported `action=CLOSE` while `should_exit` was actually
`False`: a false report of a close that never happened. Fixed structurally, not patched:
CLOSE is no longer captured as a pre-veto override at all — it's folded into `should_exit`/
`exit_reason` directly at the call site, exactly like every other rule, so the return
site's normal `should_exit`-based derivation (`_derive_position_action`) automatically
reflects a later PDT veto the same way it already does for every other exit rule. ROLL
(which never touches `should_exit`) is unaffected by this issue and needed no such fix.

DESIGN. `src/ait/execution/portfolio.py`'s condor_defense call site (`:1002-1036`): maps
the verdict via the already-existing `_map_condor_defense_action` (now genuinely
consumed, not orphaned); on `PositionAction.CLOSE`, sets `should_exit = True` and
`exit_reason = f"condor_defense_close (tested_side={verdict.tested_side},
delta={verdict.tested_short_delta:.2f})"` — same shape as every other rule's exit_reason
(a code plus inline data, matching `assignment_risk`'s `(short {side} ITM, ...)` /
`take_profit_short`'s `(P&L: ...)` style). On `PositionAction.ROLL`, behavior is
UNCHANGED from the prior wave — `condor_roll_side`/`condor_action_reason` set,
`should_exit` never touched. At the return site: `action = (PositionAction.ROLL if
condor_roll_side is not None else _derive_position_action(should_exit,
partial_exit_quantity))` — no CLOSE-specific branch at all now, since CLOSE flows through
the normal derivation exactly like a touch stop or take-profit would.
`action_reason` is now reserved exclusively for the decision-only ROLL case — a real
CLOSE (from condor_defense or any other rule) is fully described by `exit_reason`, matching
how every other real exit already works.

PROOF. `tests/test_condor_defense_wiring.py`, 13 tests (12 prior, one rewritten in place +
one new — net +1): `TestCloseIsActionable` (renamed from `TestDecisionOnlyWiring`'s CLOSE
half) — `test_close_verdict_sets_should_exit` now asserts `should_exit is True`,
`exit_reason` contains `"condor_defense_close"` and `"tested_side=P"`, `action == CLOSE`,
`action_reason is None`. **`test_close_verdict_vetoed_by_pdt_reports_hold_not_close`** — the
direct regression guard for the design issue above, not just a description of the fix: a
PDT-blocked condor_defense close asserts `should_exit is False`, `exit_reason ==
"exit_blocked_by_pdt"`, and critically **`action == HOLD`, not CLOSE** — proving the return
site no longer reports a close that didn't happen. `TestDecisionOnlyWiring` (ROLL only
now) and `TestFallsThroughToPlainDerivation`'s 5 tests: unchanged, still pass, confirming
ROLL and every HOLD-producing path are untouched.

Mutation-checked 2 mechanisms (temporarily broken, confirmed the intended test failed for
the predicted reason, reverted; `git diff --stat` confirmed clean after both): reverting
the CLOSE branch to decision-only (not touching `should_exit`) broke `test_close_verdict_
sets_should_exit` exactly as predicted; reintroducing the stale-pre-veto-capture bug (a
`condor_wants_close` flag read at the return site instead of the final `should_exit`)
broke `test_close_verdict_vetoed_by_pdt_reports_hold_not_close` exactly as predicted —
reproducing the EXACT bug this design avoids, not a synthetic stand-in for it.

**Full regression surface — 380/380, zero new failures** (379 prior + net +1): the same
311 `portfolio.py` files, `test_position_action_output.py` (13), `test_w56_condor_
defense.py` (43, unchanged), `test_condor_defense_wiring.py` (13). `python -m compileall

name-defined in `src/ait/{config,bot,execution,risk}`. `python scripts/smoke_deploy.py`:
**SMOKE PASS (13 checks)** — confirms the real `config.yaml` (`condor_defense.enabled:
false`, unchanged) and orchestrator construction still work end to end, no DB writes.

Full fast lane: **2644 passed / 1 failed / 46 skipped / 153 deselected, 1118.31s

## 2026-09-28 - W28 test portability: `test_artifact_mtimes_are_read_in_et` now builds its premise on Windows too

Validating Ahmed's 09-27/28 push (`cce07fe..d2e4f39`, 27 commits: CENSUS-1..6, W53 probe, W55,
W56, W58, W59, the `_get_ibkr_chain` per-expiry strike fix, `condor_defense` wired decision-only)
on the Windows trading box: full fast lane **2643 passed / 46 skipped / 1 failed**, typecheck
not re-run for a test-only change. The one failure was CENSUS-4's rewrite of
`TestTrainerBothSidesShareOneConvention::test_artifact_mtimes_are_read_in_et` tripping its own
setup guard ("host-local and ET dates must actually disagree"): the `host_tz` fixture moves the
process zone with `time.tzset()`, which is POSIX-only and deliberately guarded, so on this box —
whose host zone IS ET — the zone never moves and 23:00 ET reads as the same date either way. It
passes on Ahmed's macOS/CEST box, which is why his fast-lane runs never saw it. Not a live-code
defect: `_artifact_train_date` reads mtimes with `tz=_ET` and is correct on both hosts.

FIX (test-only). The test now stands a Berlin host clock in at `ait.ml.trainer.datetime` (a
`datetime` subclass whose naive `fromtimestamp` reads Europe/Berlin; tz-aware calls pass through),
so the scenario is constructed on every platform instead of depending on `tzset`. PROOF: green
here with the code as shipped; **red** with `tz=_ET` removed from `trainer.py:197` (the exact

## 2026-09-29 - BUILT — roll booking mechanics (`execution/roll_booking.py`), unwired: a
real ordering bug found and fixed while building it

SCOPE. `roll_executor.py` (previous wave) prepares a fully validated, priced 4-leg roll
combo but stops before placement. The next gap, found by directly re-reading the real
booking code rather than trusting the earlier framing: **the booking machinery actually
lives in `executor.py` + `state.py`, not `reconciler.py`** — worth stating plainly since
an earlier register entry this session (the roll-executor wave's own NEXT pointer) assumed
otherwise. `reconciler.py` is a periodic (startup/pre-market/post-market/on-demand, NOT
per-tick) position-diff safety net; the real exactly-once machinery is `state.py`'s status
compare-and-swap (`transition`) plus `close_trade`'s outbox/claim/`core_booked` layers, and
every existing booking path (`_order_trade_map`, `PendingOrder`, `PendingExitOrder`)
assumes ONE order maps to exactly ONE `trade_id`. A roll's single 4-leg fill needs to book
TWO: close the old vertical (trade A), open the new one (trade B). This wave builds that
booking logic as new, additive, fully tested code that **nothing calls** — matching every
prior wave's precedent exactly. `executor.py`'s live `check_fills`/`_pending_orders`/
`_pending_exit_orders` loops are untouched; teaching them to recognize a roll order and
dispatch here is the actual wiring step, deliberately deferred to a further, later wave.

Two risks confirmed directly from source before writing any code (not assumed): `HALT_
UNTRACKED` freezes on a position whose legs aren't in `local_map` (built from open trades,
including PENDING) on a second sighting — writing B's PENDING row (real legs) *before* a
roll order is ever placed, the same ordering CLAUDE.md already documents for entries,
prevents this. `go_live.py` already excludes CLOSING/PENDING rows from the verdict sample
(counted only toward the drawdown base) — an intermediate multi-step booking state does
NOT corrupt the 50-close track record; `go_live.py`'s "fold a roll into one outcome"
accounting is a real, still-open MODELING question, but not a correctness blocker,
registered as NEXT rather than solved here.

DESIGN. New `src/ait/execution/roll_booking.py`: `seed_roll_opening_trade` writes B's
PENDING row, mirroring `execute_signal`'s exact `record_trade`-before-placement ordering
(`executor.py:447-493`). `cas_roll_closing_trade` is a thin, named wrapper around the
SAME CAS primitive `orchestrator._cas_to_closing` already uses (FILLED/PARTIAL→CLOSING).
`split_roll_fill_price` is a pure function splitting a roll combo's per-leg fill rows
(the shape `_sweep_executions` already produces — confirmed per-leg conId/price/shares
data IS available for a BAG combo, not just a combo-level summary) into closing-side and
opening-side net totals, same signed-per-leg-sum convention `leg_net_price`/
`_option_position_unrealized` already use. `book_roll_fill` orchestrates: computes A's
`realized_pnl` from the closing split using `_option_position_unrealized`'s OWN credit/
debit polarity formula (reused via `CREDIT_STRATEGIES` import, not reimplemented), calls
the EXISTING `state.close_trade(..., exit_reason_detailed=f"rolled_to_{opening_trade_id}",
from_statuses=(CLOSING,))` — reusing the real exactly-once machinery verbatim — and
promotes B via `state.transition` plus a narrow `UPDATE` that finally gives `TradeRecord.
rolled_from_trade_id` (already existed, `state.py:99`, unpopulated by any code path until
now) a real writer. `PendingRollOrder` is the agreed data contract a future `executor.py`
wiring wave would key a new `_pending_roll_orders` dict by — defined, not instantiated or
consumed by any live code this wave.

**A REAL DESIGN BUG FOUND AND FIXED WHILE BUILDING THIS, not assumed correct from the
plan**: the first draft closed A (`state.close_trade`) BEFORE promoting B
(`state.transition`). `test_b_already_filled_refuses_and_leaves_a_untouched` caught it
immediately — with B already FILLED by something else, A still got closed (since A's own
CAS had already succeeded before B's promotion was even attempted), leaving A CLOSED with
no live B to show for the closed position; the position would have silently vanished.
Fixed by reordering: promote B FIRST, close A second. A failure promoting B now leaves A
untouched in CLOSING (recoverable, still awaiting its real close). The reverse failure (A's
close failing after B is already promoted) is a real, smaller, more VISIBLE residual risk
this two-phase design does not eliminate (B live, A stuck in CLOSING) — documented in the
function's own docstring and registered as a known limitation for the future wiring wave,
not solved here (a true cross-table atomic transaction would mean bypassing `state.py`'s
own exactly-once primitives, which this module deliberately reuses instead).

PROOF. `tests/test_roll_booking.py`, 13 new tests, no `inspect.getsource`, a REAL temp-DB
`StateManager` throughout (never mocked — proves the actual SQL, same convention `test_
w53_db_migration.py` uses). `TestSplitRollFillPrice` (3), `TestSeedRollOpeningTrade` (2,
including a duplicate-`trade_id` proof that `INSERT OR IGNORE`'s own idempotency holds,
not just assumed), `TestCasRollClosingTrade` (2). `TestBookRollFill` (6): happy path
(A closed with the correct split price/link, B filled with `rolled_from_trade_id` and its
real entry price); credit-strategy and debit-strategy `realized_pnl` sign checks against

promote-B-first ordering proof from both directions (B-already-filled leaves A untouched
— the clean direction; A-not-in-CLOSING still promotes B, the documented residual risk,
proven not silently hidden); a `split_roll_fill_price` failure refuses before any write.

## 2026-09-29 - BUILT — fold rolled trade chains into one `go_live.py` outcome + harden
`roll_booking.py`'s linkage: two real bugs found and fixed during implementation

SCOPE. `roll_booking.py` (previous wave) books a roll correctly at the row level, but
nothing read `rolled_from_trade_id` anywhere in this codebase (confirmed greenfield by
grep), and `go_live.py` — the CLAUDE.md-flagged single-source-of-truth for the 50-close
paper verdict — had no roll awareness at all: `rolled_to_` matches none of `NOT_REAL_
CLOSE_PATTERNS`, so trade A currently counts as a normal, independent real close, and B
(inheriting A's `strategy`) will too once it eventually closes for real — one economic
position silently becoming two IC samples in the gate that decides go-live readiness.

**Operator decision: fold, don't exclude.** A rolled chain (A→B, or longer — the schema
has no roll cap) counts as ONE outcome, credited at the chain's TERMINAL real close:
summed `realized_pnl` across every leg, the chain's ORIGINAL `entry_time`, the terminal
leg's `exit_time`. Naive pattern-exclusion (the existing `%pending%`-style mechanism)
would have silently discarded A's real, already-realized P&L — wrong, not just
incomplete, which is why this needed new logic rather than a new pattern.

**Scope boundary, deliberately held**: only the WIN/LOSS/PF/n sample computation
(`BookStats.from_pnls`) is folded. `max_concurrent_car`'s drawdown computation
deliberately still uses the UNFOLDED rows — A's and B's capital-at-risk exposure windows
were genuinely separate real periods of risk even though economically linked; folding
them would claim continuous exposure across the gap between A's close and B's open, using
a blended `car` that matches neither leg's real exposure at any actual moment. The
existing `NOT_REAL_CLOSE_PATTERNS`/`not_real_close_sql`/`not_real_close_bucket` list is
NOT touched either — it's imported by 7+ other files (dashboard, ML training sets,
`learning/analyzer.py`, `scripts/shadow_referee.py`, ...); touching it would silently
change what THOSE consumers count too, a far broader blast radius than this file's own
verdict. Folding is new, local, additive logic inside `go_live.py` only.

**Also fixes two real gaps in `roll_booking.py`**, per the operator's explicit choice to
bundle them in — directly relevant since they're the reliability of the very field this
wave gives its first real reader: B's row never got `capital_at_risk` set (nothing called
the existing `set_trade_capital_at_risk`) — now defaults to A's own (`roll_selector.
select_roll_target` deliberately rolls to the SAME width, so A's max-loss is a reasonable
estimate), overridable via a new `book_roll_fill(capital_at_risk=...)` parameter. And the
`rolled_from_trade_id` back-link was written in a THIRD, separate step after both B's
promotion and A's close already landed — a crash between steps left A pointing forward to
B with no way back. Fixed with a new `_promote_and_link_opening_trade` primitive: ONE
atomic `UPDATE` combining the status CAS and the linkage write, same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`
idiom `close_trade` already uses (not a duplicate of `state.transition()` — that only ever
sets status, so it genuinely can't carry the extra columns; this is a new primitive for a
new need, not a reimplementation).

DESIGN. `src/ait/reporting/go_live.py`: `fold_roll_chains(rows) -> (folded, removed_count)`
— pure function. Discovers chain membership by walking the FORWARD link (`rolled_to_<id>`
regex-parsed from `reason`) from each row not itself pointed-to, using `rolled_from_
trade_id` only as a cheap pre-filter for which rows to start a walk from, never as the
sole source of truth — a `consumed` set guards against double-counting regardless of link
write ordering. A chain whose next hop isn't in the batch (still open) is excluded
ENTIRELY, no partial credit. `_fetch_closed_rows` is a new shared helper both `compute_
go_live_verdict` and `real_close_count` call for the raw (unfolded) fetch, so the two
functions' notion of "the real close population" can never silently drift apart
(CLAUDE.md's duplication-causes-divergence theme). `compute_go_live_verdict`: `closed`
(folded, feeds the sample) is now separate from `closed_raw`/`ic_raw` (unfolded, feeds
drawdown) — explicit, commented, and deliberate per the scope boundary above. `v.excluded`
gains a `rolled_intermediate` bucket (local-only, not touching the shared pattern
machinery) reporting how many non-terminal roll legs were folded away.

**A REAL BUG CAUGHT BY THE TEST SUITE DURING IMPLEMENTATION**: the first draft of `fold_
roll_chains` assumed every caller selects `realized_pnl`/`entry_time` and unconditionally
summed/read them when merging a chain. `real_close_count` only selects `strategy` (it
doesn't need P&L data to count rows) — its own test raised a bare `KeyError:
'realized_pnl'` the instant a real rolled chain existed in its query result. Fixed by
making both fields OPTIONAL in the merge (folded only when the terminal row actually
carries them), confirmed by the SAME test then passing and `real_close_count`'s own
"agrees with the verdict's `n`" assertion holding.

PROOF. `tests/test_go_live_roll_folding.py` (new, 8 tests): `TestFoldRollChains` — a
non-rolled row passes through unchanged; a simple A→B fold; a 3-hop A→B→C fold (the
schema's "no roll cap" genuinely exercised, not just claimed); an incomplete/still-open
chain excludes entirely; **a chain with a MISSING back-link still folds correctly and
doesn't double-count** — the direct proof this design is robust to the exact roll_
booking.py gap being fixed alongside it, not merely dependent on that fix landing
perfectly; two independent chains in the same batch don't cross-contaminate.
`TestVerdictAndCountAgreeOnFoldedRolls` (real temp-DB `StateManager`, direct SQL seed
matching `test_w3_scorecard_truth.py`'s own convention): a real A→B chain plus a
non-rolled trade — `verdict.book.n` counts the chain once, `realized_pnl` sums correctly,
`real_close_count` agrees with the verdict's own `n` exactly (the single-source-of-truth
proof `real_close_count`'s docstring already promises); an in-flight chain contributes
nothing to either.

`tests/test_roll_booking.py` (5 net-new, 18 total): `capital_at_risk` defaults to A's own
and is independently overridable; `_promote_and_link_opening_trade`'s own class —
promotes-and-links together, a refused CAS (wrong starting status) leaves BOTH fields
untouched (not just status), and **a direct single-atomic-statement proof via a real SQL
spy on `sqlite3.connect`** asserting exactly one `UPDATE` (not two) carries both `status`
and `rolled_from_trade_id` together.

## 2026-09-29 - BUILT — W60: roll foundation fixes (carried vertical, P&L sign, leg
serialization, reconciler roll-awareness) -- still unreachable from any live path

SCOPE. The operator confirmed the next wave as "the full ROLL wiring" (placement +
`check_fills` fill recognition). Before writing that plan, direct research into
`executor.py`'s fill-recognition machinery, `condor_defense`'s config gating, and
`roll_booking.py`'s own already-committed code surfaced that the roll modules built across
the last several waves would book **wrong state** the instant anything called them, and
that `reconciler.py` -- which runs every cycle regardless of what triggered a roll -- would
actively fight a working roll order. Given CLAUDE.md's explicit sensitivity around
`execution/executor.py`/`reconciler.py` and this session's own "build additively, fix the
foundation before wiring" discipline, the operator chose to fix these four bugs FIRST, as
their own separate wave, deferring placement/`check_fills` wiring to the wave after.
**Nothing in this wave is reachable from any live path** -- no order is placed, no config
flag changed, `condor_defense`'s ROLL verdict stays decision-only exactly as every prior
wave left it. `reconciler.py` DOES run live every cycle, but every change here is additive
and keyed only on a roll marker (`ROLL:<A>:<B>` orderRef, `rolled_from_trade_id`) that no
row or order carries today -- confirmed by the regression suite passing byte-identical.

THE FOUR BUGS, each confirmed by direct source read before any code was written:

1. **Orphaned carried vertical.** `roll_executor.legs_for_roll` built legs for only the
   ROLLED side (2 of a 4-leg IC's legs). But `book_roll_fill` closed ALL of A and
   `seed_roll_opening_trade` gave B only the 2 new legs -- the untouched vertical (e.g. the
   call side of a put-side roll) would go live at IBKR attached to NO trade row: HALT_
   UNTRACKED on the second reconcile sighting, no stop/TP managing it, and A booked as if
   its whole 4-leg credit were realized when only half of it actually traded.

2. **Realized-P&L sign inverted for credit strategies.** `book_roll_fill`'s formula used
   `signed_entry = -abs(entry)` then computed `closing_net - signed_entry` -- which is
   `closing_net + abs(entry)`, not `abs(entry) - closing_net`. A $1.50 credit IC bought back
   for a $0.80 net debit is a $70 GAIN; the old formula booked **+$230**. `test_roll_
   booking.py`'s own pre-existing assertions encoded the bug (asserting the wrong number,
   and one test's own name -- "is_a_realized_loss" -- contradicted the positive value it
   asserted). The debit-strategy branch was coincidentally already correct (verified by
   direct derivation, not assumed) -- only credit strategies were wrong.

3. **Unserializable legs.** `qualify_roll_legs` enriches every leg with `_contract` (a live
   ib_insync `Option`, not JSON-serializable). `seed_roll_opening_trade` did
   `json.dumps(opening_legs)` straight on that output -- `TypeError` on the first real call,
   never caught because no test had driven a fixture shaped like qualification's real
   output.

4. **`reconciler.py` fights a working roll order.** Its order matching (`_working_exit_
   order_for` / `_cancel_working_entry_order`) is exact `orderRef == trade_id`, and both
   explicitly refuse to claim an order tagged for a different trade. A roll order's
   orderRef (`ROLL:<A>:<B>`) is neither -- it names TWO trades, matching neither's `trade_id`
   verbatim, yet it isn't empty either (so the untagged-legacy fallback doesn't catch it).
   Concretely, unfixed: (a) a working roll order for A would fail `_working_exit_order_for`,
   fall to "no working order", and CLOSING would be REVERTED to FILLED mid-roll (a position
   REVERSAL risk -- the exit monitor would try to close an already-in-flight position
   again); (b) the every-cycle stale-pending sweep would book a stale roll-child B "never
   filled" after 30 minutes even while its roll order is genuinely still working, and would
   refund an entry-budget slot B never actually consumed.

DESIGN.

`src/ait/execution/roll_executor.py`: `legs_for_roll` now returns a 3-tuple `(closing_legs,
opening_legs, carried_legs)` -- carried_legs are trade's own legs NOT on the rolled side,
actions UNCHANGED (the real, still-open position). `prepare_roll_combo` qualifies and
quotes the carried vertical alongside the BAG's own legs in the SAME `poll_leg_quotes` call
but never adds it to the BAG (only the rolled vertical is placed as a combo; the carried
side stays untouched at IBKR, transferred to B at booking time instead). `carried_value` is
the carried vertical's mark, in `portfolio.py`'s own POSITION-sign convention (BUY+/SELL-,
via the leg's UNCHANGED action) -- reusing `leg_net_price` directly rather than inventing
new math, since that function already implements exactly this sign convention when given
non-reversed actions. `PreparedRollCombo` gains `carried_legs`/`carried_value`.

`src/ait/execution/roll_booking.py`: new `_persistable_legs()` strips `_contract` before
every `json.dumps` of a legs list (bug 3's fix, applied at every write site). New
`roll_order_ref(closing_id, opening_id)` / `parse_roll_order_ref(ref)` -- the single source
for the `"ROLL:<A>:<B>"` marker, imported by `reconciler.py` rather than re-derived.
`seed_roll_opening_trade` now persists B's legs through `_persistable_legs`, seeds ONLY the
new (opening) legs -- not the carried vertical, which would make reconcile/the sweep see
those legs as "live" and promote/count B against them before the roll ever fills -- and
sets `rolled_from_trade_id` via an explicit UPDATE immediately after `record_trade` (that
column isn't in `record_trade`'s own INSERT, same gap `capital_at_risk` has), so a roll's
PENDING row is recognisable as roll-linked from the moment it exists, not deferred to
promotion. `_promote_and_link_opening_trade` gains a `legs` parameter, now writing the
MERGED (carried + opening) legs into the SAME atomic UPDATE as the status/link write -- B's
`legs` column reflects the whole post-roll position only from this one atomic statement,
never a separate follow-up write that could crash half-done. `book_roll_fill` gains
`carried_legs`/`carried_value` parameters; fetches B's seeded opening legs via `state.
get_trade_by_id` and merges with `carried_legs` for the promotion write; computes A's
`exit_price = closing_net - carried_value` (converting `carried_value`'s POSITION-sign
convention to the TRADE-cost "cost to close" convention `_calculate_realized_pnl`
(executor.py:2695-2713) already uses, by negating it) and `realized_pnl` via that SAME
credit/debit branching (bug 2's fix); B's `entry_price = abs(opening_net + carried_value)`,
the whole post-roll position's entry basis in the SAME unsigned-premium convention every
other `trades.entry_price` uses. Verified by hand: $1.50 credit IC, rolled side bought back
for $0.80, carried side marked -$0.30 -> A realizes exactly +$40, B's entry becomes exactly
$1.05 -- proven by a dedicated test against these exact numbers, not just the formula.

`src/ait/execution/reconciler.py` (CLAUDE.md-critical; every change additive, keyed only on
the roll marker, verified via the full regression suite staying byte-identical):
new `_working_roll_order_for(trade, working)` -- checked BEFORE `_working_exit_order_for`
in the CLOSING branch; a match records `trade_id -> order_id` into a NEW, deliberately
SEPARATE `ReconciliationResult.closing_roll_orders` field (never `closing_exit_orders`, so
the orchestrator's existing `adopt_exit_order` re-registration never touches a roll order
and can never double-book its eventual fill against `book_roll_fill`'s own booking) and
`continue`s past the plain-exit/revert branches entirely (fixes bug 4a). `_cancel_working_
entry_order` gains a new Pass 1b recognising a roll order whose OPENING side names the
trade being swept (fixes half of bug 4b, B's side). `_sweep_stale_pending`'s booking branch:
a stale roll-child B (`rolled_from_trade_id` set) skips `_refund_entry_budget` (B's "entry"
was never a fresh signal, so there is no slot to give back) and instead CASes its parent A
from CLOSING back to FILLED (`roll_abandoned_parent_restored`) -- confirmed the roll is
genuinely abandoned (no working order, no live legs -- both already checked above) before
restoring, so `check_positions` (FILLED/PARTIAL only) manages A again instead of leaving it
stuck CLOSING, invisible, until the next post-market reconcile (fixes the other half of bug
4b, A's side).

PROOF. `tests/test_roll_executor.py` (16 -> 21, +5): carried legs are the untouched side's
own 2 legs with actions unchanged; empty for a plain vertical roll; `prepare_roll_combo`
qualifies+marks the carried vertical but the BAG never includes it (con_id-set disjointness
asserted directly, not just count); a missing carried quote refuses the whole combo (the
same fail-safe every other missing-quote path already uses); no-carried-legs case leaves
`carried_value == 0.0` exactly. `tests/test_roll_booking.py` (18 -> 29, +11): `_persistable_
legs` strips `_contract` and the round-tripped output survives a real `json.dumps`;
`roll_order_ref`/`parse_roll_order_ref` round-trip and a plain trade_id is never misread as
a roll ref; `rolled_from_trade_id` is set at SEED time (not deferred to promotion) and
survives a refused promotion untouched; `seed_roll_opening_trade` accepts legs straight out
of `qualify_roll_legs`'s real shape (a live, non-serializable `_contract`) without raising;
`_promote_and_link_opening_trade`'s legs write is in the SAME single atomic UPDATE as
status/link (a real SQL-spy on `sqlite3.connect` asserts exactly one UPDATE statement
contains all three); the corrected credit-strategy P&L assertion (was $230, now $70,
matching the hand-derivation above) with an explicit note on why the debit branch was
already correct; a dedicated `TestBookRollFillWithCarriedVertical` class proves the carried
vertical lands in B's merged legs (4 legs, not 2) and the $40/$1.05 worked example exactly;
`book_roll_fill` with a missing B row refuses cleanly (new: it now reads B's seeded legs
from the DB, so a missing row is a new failure mode needing its own guard).

`tests/test_reconciler_roll_awareness.py` (new, 11 tests): `_working_roll_order_for`
matches only the CLOSING side of a roll ref, never the opening side (that's `_cancel_
working_entry_order`'s job) and never a plain exit's bare-trade_id ref; `_cancel_working_
entry_order` cancels a roll order tagged for the trade being swept as ITS opening side, and
refuses one tagged for a different opening trade; a full `reconcile()` run (real temp-DB
`StateManager`, `tests.fakes.FakeIB`/`FakeIBKRClient`) proves a working roll order keeps A
CLOSING and lands in `closing_roll_orders` (not `closing_exit_orders`), a plain working exit
order is UNAFFECTED by the new roll check (R17 behaviour survives unchanged), and -- the
existing self-heal this fix must never break -- NO working order of any kind still reverts
CLOSING to FILLED exactly as before; `_sweep_stale_pending` on a real backdated stale roll-
child B books it never-filled with the budget counter UNCHANGED (not refunded) and restores
parent A to FILLED, while an ordinary (non-roll) stale PENDING is still refunded exactly as
before (the explicit regression guard that the roll branch doesn't swallow the normal path).

Mutation-checked 4 mechanisms via Edit (not `git checkout`, after an earlier `git checkout
--` in this same wave accidentally discarded the day's roll_booking.py work entirely --
recovered by reconstructing the file from the conversation's own record and re-verifying
all 29+21 tests passed before proceeding; the file is now backed by git-tracked diffs only,

Regression: `test_roll_booking.py` + `test_roll_executor.py` + `test_reconciler_roll_

STATE AT HANDOFF. `src/ait/execution/roll_executor.py`, `src/ait/execution/roll_booking.py`,

## 2026-09-29 - BUILT — W61: wire ROLL end-to-end (placement + fill recognition),
gated off by `CondorDefenseConfig.execute_rolls` (default `False`)

SCOPE. Connects every already-built roll piece — `condor_defense`'s ROLL verdict →
`roll_selector.select_roll_target` → `roll_executor.prepare_roll_combo` → a real placed
order → `executor.py`'s fill recognition → `roll_booking.book_roll_fill` — into one live
path for the first time. Kept inert the same way `condor_defense.enabled` itself is: a new
`CondorDefenseConfig.execute_rolls: bool = False` gate, required IN ADDITION to `enabled`
before anything places an order. Nothing about current running behavior changes until an
operator flips both — confirmed by the full fast lane staying at the expected count delta
with zero new failures.

A genuine simplification found during research, not assumed going in: W60's own reconciler
fix (`_cancel_working_entry_order`'s roll-aware Pass 1b) already cancels a stale (30+ min)
working roll order, and the stale-pending sweep already books an abandoned roll child B as
never-filled and restores parent A to FILLED. This wave needed NO new timeout/staleness/
revert mechanism for a roll that never fills — that backstop already existed and was
already tested by W60.

Two things resolved by direct source verification before writing any code, not assumed:
`f.execution.side` is ib_insync's own `"BOT"`/`"SLD"`, not `"BUY"`/`"SELL"` — confirmed
against `executor.py:2401`'s own existing `"SLD"` == sell check — so the new `check_fills`
roll block translates this explicitly before handing fills to `split_roll_fill_price`, which
expects the latter; a raw pass-through was proven (mutation-checked) to silently invert
every fill's sign. And market-hours/the 8-orders-60s rate backstop, which exits currently
skip by placing directly via `ibkr.place_order()`: a roll's opening leg is economically a
new position the same way an entry is, so `place_roll_combo` checks both explicitly
(undefined-risk is moot by construction — `_validate_roll_legs` already refuses anything but
a clean vertical).

**Also this wave: PLAN.md's own numbering was corrected.** The previous wave (originally
committed as "W57") was renamed to **W60** in a small standalone commit
(`e0c9225`) before this wave's own code changes began — the 2026-09-22 roadmap had reserved
W57 for THIS wave, not the foundation-fix one. This entry is W61, not W57.

DESIGN.

`src/ait/config/settings.py` / `config.yaml`: `CondorDefenseConfig.execute_rolls: bool =
False` — a roll is placed only when BOTH `enabled` and `execute_rolls` are `True`.

`src/ait/execution/executor.py`: new `self._pending_roll_orders: dict[int, PendingRollOrder]`,
fully isolated from `_pending_orders`/`_pending_exit_orders` (confirmed by a dedicated
Explore pass before relying on it: `_cancel_stale_orders` only ever walks `_pending_orders`
itself — no broad broker-order scan exists anywhere in this file — and both `check_fills`
loops iterate their own dict directly, never broker orders broadly, so an orderId never
added to either is never visited by them). New `place_roll_combo(prepared, closing_trade_id,
opening_trade_id, carried_legs, carried_value)`: market-hours + shared-`_order_times`
rate-limit checks (mirroring `execute_signal`'s own gates exactly), places via
`ibkr.place_order`, registers the `PendingRollOrder` and (for `_sweep_executions`'s own
ledger-row attribution only — never read for booking correctness) `_order_trade_map[order_
id] = closing_trade_id`. New roll-recognition block appended to the end of `check_fills`
(return signature unchanged — a booked/failed roll logs a structured event rather than
threading a third value through `check_fills_safe`'s three call sites, since nothing
downstream consumes one): acts ONLY on a clean `"Filled"` verdict — a still-working or
partially-filled combo is left alone (partial-combo-fill handling is explicitly out of
scope, registered in NEXT) — builds `leg_fills` from `trade.fills` excluding the existing
`_is_bag_row` combo-summary check, translates `"BOT"/"SLD"` to `"BUY"/"SELL"`, and calls
`book_roll_fill`, removing the entry whether booking succeeds or fails (never retried — a
retry against an already-consumed fill could double-book). `PreparedRollCombo` is
deliberately never imported into `executor.py` (only `roll_booking`'s `PendingRollOrder`/
`book_roll_fill` are) — `roll_executor.py` already imports `_validate_roll_legs` FROM
`executor.py`, so the reverse import would cycle; `place_roll_combo`'s `prepared` parameter
stays duck-typed.

`src/ait/bot/orchestrator.py`: new `_partition_roll_positions(positions, rolls_enabled)`
(a small pure staticmethod, factored out specifically so the gate logic is unit-testable
without driving the whole `_trading_cycle` method) splits not-already-exiting positions into
(roll_positions, remaining_for_thesis_reeval) — when `rolls_enabled` is `False`, every
ROLL-action position falls through to `remaining` exactly as it always has, byte-identical.
`_trading_cycle` computes `rolls_enabled` by reading `self._portfolio._condor_defense_config`
directly (mirrors exactly how `portfolio.py:1024` itself reads this config — there is no
separate orchestrator-level copy) and dispatches `roll_positions` to new `_execute_roll`
inside the same position lock, before the (now-reduced) thesis-reevaluation loop. `_execute_
roll`, cheapest/most-reversible steps first: `select_roll_target` (reusing `assignment_
response.roll_target_dte_min/max` — not a duplicate window in `CondorDefenseConfig`, since a
condor_defense-triggered roll and a future W54 rule-3/3e-triggered roll share one "where do
we roll to" policy) → `prepare_roll_combo` with `debit_cap=-assignment_response.
roll_min_credit` (the sign flip: `roll_min_credit` is a CREDIT floor in `leg_net_price`'s
BUY+/SELL- convention, where a net credit is NEGATIVE — "require at least $0.20 credit"
means refusing `mid_net > -0.20`) → `cas_roll_closing_trade` → `seed_roll_opening_trade` →
stamp the REAL `roll_order_ref(A, B)` onto `prepared.order` (the earlier `prepare_roll_
combo` call used a placeholder ref, since B's trade_id doesn't exist until seeded) →
`executor.place_roll_combo`. A failure at any step after the first two logs and returns
without reverting anything already written — matches normal exits' own existing convention
(no revert after CAS-to-CLOSING there either), and W60's reconciler fix already cleans up an
abandoned attempt on its own 30-minute cadence, so no new recovery path was invented.

PROOF. `tests/test_roll_wiring.py` (new, 24 tests): `TestPlaceRollComboGates` — market-hours
refusal (both the explicit-override bypass and a raising calendar failing closed);
rate-limit refusal sharing `_order_times` with 8 pre-existing entries (proves shared state,
not a parallel counter); a placement failure registers nothing.
`TestPlaceRollComboHappyPath` — `PendingRollOrder` registered with the exact conId sets/
carried fields; `_order_trade_map` set to A; `_pending_orders`/`_pending_exit_orders`
untouched (the isolation claim, proven not assumed). `TestCheckFillsRollRecognition` (real
`StateManager` + `tests.fakes.FakeIB`/`FakeIBKRClient`, a real `TradeExecutor`, a real
`check_fills()` pass — not a mock call-count) — a filled roll order books both trades
correctly and is removed; the BAG summary row never poisons the leg split; a still-working
order is left completely untouched (both A and B's status unchanged); a booking failure
(unattributed conId) still removes the order without touching A. `TestPartitionRollPositions`
— disabled means every ROLL position falls through to remaining; enabled splits correctly by
action; an already-exiting or already-partial position is excluded either way.
`TestExecuteRoll` — each early-return path (no target, prep failure, CAS refusal) writes
literally nothing beyond what pre-existed (a real row-count assertion, not just the return
value); the debit_cap sign-flip, asserted against the real negated value; a full happy path
seeds B with `rolled_from_trade_id` set and the real (not placeholder) orderRef stamped; a
placement failure leaves both A (CLOSING) and B (PENDING) exactly as seeded, proving no new
revert path was accidentally added. `TestExecuteRollsGate` — `execute_rolls` defaults
`False`; both flags are independently required.

Mutation-checked 3 mechanisms via `Edit` (never `git checkout`, learned the hard way in
W60), each temporarily broken, confirmed the predicted test failure, reverted: the `"BOT"/
"SLD"` translation, replaced with a raw pass-through, produced a materially wrong booked
P&L ($270 instead of $70 — every leg's sign inverted, since `split_roll_fill_price`'s own

## 2026-09-29 - BUILT — W54a: close-or-roll comparison models (heuristic default, EV built
but gated), the missing fair-value pricing primitive, and a roll-count cap — still
unreachable from rule 3/3e (W54b, next)

SCOPE. The operator asked to ship W54's EV-comparison logic now, defaulting to the cheap
heuristic, with a config comment recommending backtesting before ever switching to `"ev"`
(the historical vol-surface backfill this needs is still running). Direct research before
writing any code found the 2026-09-27 scoping note's own premises didn't fully hold, and
that wiring rule 3/3e (the trigger) to actually USE a comparison needs more than a config
flag: rule 3/3e and `condor_defense` currently share ONE decision variable
(`condor_roll_side`) with no arbitration between them, a real conflict risk the moment
either could independently choose ROLL; rule 3's `itm_side` is `"put"`/`"call"`, not the
`"P"`/`"C"` `select_roll_target` expects; and portfolio.py has no broker access, so the
comparison can't run where rule 3/3e's decision is made (the same reason `condor_defense`'s
own roll stays decision-only there). Given that, **split into two waves, per the operator's
explicit choice**, mirroring this register's own `W52a` lettering precedent:
- **W54a (this entry)**: the comparison models, the fair-value pricing primitive they need,
  the config selector, and the roll-count cap — built, tested, callable, genuinely
  unreachable from any live path. Also wires the roll-count cap into the ALREADY-shipped
  `_execute_roll` (W61), since that function is live-reachable today (once `condor_defense.
  execute_rolls` is flipped) and benefits from the cap regardless of trigger.
- **W54b (next, separately scoped)**: the arbitration fix, the side-encoding fix, and the
  actual rule 3/3e → orchestrator dispatch.

THREE RESEARCH FINDINGS, each confirmed by direct source read before writing any code:
1. **No theoretical fair-value function exists anywhere on the live path.**
   `options_chain.py` only solves IV FROM a price (`solve_iv_from_price`); nothing prices
   FROM an IV. The scoping note's premise ("risk-neutral valuation collapses to pricing
   both sides accurately, reusing the existing pipeline") was correct in spirit, but the
   pricing half didn't exist — it had to be built.
2. **`leg_net_price`/`poll_leg_quotes` (the roll path's own pricer, W60/W61) had a latent
   gap the exit path's separate, divergent pricer (`_synthesize_combo_cost`) already
   handles**: IBKR's `-1` "no bid" sentinel read `b >= 0` as false, so a worthless wing's
   bid was treated as MISSING — refusing the whole roll — instead of $0. A real bug in
   already-shipped code, fixed here regardless of W54b.
3. **`go_live.py`'s `fold_roll_chains` cannot be reused for a live roll-count cap.** It only
   walks CLOSED rows FORWARD for historical accounting and explicitly drops any chain that
   ends at a still-open trade — exactly the live, open-position case a cap needs. A new,
   small backward walk was required.

DESIGN.

`src/ait/data/options_chain.py`: new `black_scholes_price(spot, strike, t, r, sigma, flag)
-> float | None`, next to `solve_iv_from_price`, using the SAME `py_vollib` dependency
(not `backtesting/pricing.py`'s separate scipy-based implementation — one pricing library on
the live path, not two, per CLAUDE.md's duplication theme). Never raises; `None` on
`t<=0`/`sigma<=0`/any py_vollib failure.

`src/ait/execution/roll_executor.py`: `poll_leg_quotes`'s bid-acceptance condition (`b >=
0`) becomes `b >= -1`, normalizing a `-1` read to `0.0` — finding 2's fix, mutation-checked.
`PreparedRollCombo` gains `closing_net`/`opening_net` (the two subtotals `mid_net` already
sums internally, exposed separately, purely additive — `mid_net`'s own meaning and every
existing consumer unchanged) so a caller can estimate "cost to close everything right now"
(`closing_net - carried_value`, the SAME formula `roll_booking.book_roll_fill` already uses
for a REAL fill, applied here to a MID estimate) without re-deriving the split.

`src/ait/execution/roll_selector.py`: `RollTarget` gains `iv_is_guessed: bool = False`, set
from the chain `select_roll_target` already fetches — the existing chain-level signal
(`OptionsChain.iv_is_guessed`) threaded through so a future caller can refuse the EV
comparison on a chain with no usable IV data, reusing the SAME signal `iron_condor.py`'s
own entry path already checks, not a new detector.

`src/ait/execution/roll_comparison.py` (new): mirrors `roll_selector.py`/`roll_executor.py`'s
own shape — nothing in `src/` calls into it yet, same "build additively, wire later"
discipline as every prior piece of this arc.
- `close_cost_now(prepared) -> float`: `closing_net - carried_value`.
- `heuristic_should_roll(prepared) -> bool`: the tastytrade-style rule from the scoping
  note ([1]/[3]d), worked down to what's actually left to decide once `prepare_roll_combo`'s
  own gates (`roll_min_credit`/`debit_cap`, same-width target selection) already
  structurally guarantee the roll clears "net credit" and "no larger max-loss": **don't
  roll a position that would already be profitable or breakeven if closed now — only roll
  one that would realize a loss**, where the roll's own (already-guaranteed) credit reduces
  that loss rather than locking it in. `roll only when close_cost_now(prepared) > 0`.
- `ev_should_roll(closing_legs_priced, opening_legs_priced, carried_legs_priced, r) -> bool
  | None`: the same comparison, but each leg priced via `black_scholes_price` at its own
  solved IV (model fair value) instead of raw market mid quotes — catches finding [2] from
  the scoping note: a roll whose raw market credit looks fine but is actually giving away
  more theoretical time value than it collects. Takes explicit, already-resolved per-leg
  inputs rather than reaching for a chain itself, staying pure and directly testable;
  gathering those inputs live (the carried legs' CURRENT IV in particular has no existing
  source yet) is explicitly a W54b wiring detail. Returns `None` — defer to the heuristic —
  if any leg's IV is missing/unsolved, never guesses.

`src/ait/config/settings.py` / `config.yaml`: `AssignmentResponseConfig` gains
`comparison_model: Literal["heuristic","ev"] = "heuristic"` (nested under `policy`, same
gating idiom `policy` and `condor_defense.enabled` already use; the description AND the
`config.yaml` comment both carry the operator's requested backtest warning verbatim: "'ev'
has NOT been backtested ... RECOMMENDED: stay on 'heuristic' ... do not switch this to 'ev'
in a live/paper account before then") and `max_rolls_per_position: int = 2` (applies to ANY
roll regardless of trigger).

`src/ait/bot/state.py`: new `StateManager.count_roll_ancestors(trade_id, max_depth=20) ->
int` — a single recursive-CTE query walking `rolled_from_trade_id` BACKWARD from `trade_id`
to its origin, counting hops. Bounded by `max_depth` (belt-and-suspenders — the field is
written exactly once, at seed time, so a cycle should never exist, but the bound costs
nothing). Explicitly documented as distinct from `fold_roll_chains` (finding 3), so a future
reader doesn't try to unify them.

`src/ait/bot/orchestrator.py`: `_execute_roll` (already exists, W61) gains one new, cheap,
FIRST check — `depth = state.count_roll_ancestors(trade.trade_id); if depth >=
assignment_response.max_rolls_per_position: log + return` — before any chain fetch. The
one piece of W54a touching a function already on a live-reachable path.

PROOF. `tests/test_roll_comparison.py` (new, 16 tests): `black_scholes_price` — deep-ITM
approaches intrinsic, deep-OTM near zero, put-call parity holds within tolerance, `t<=0`/
`sigma<=0` return `None` never raise, and a round-trip through `solve_iv_from_price`
recovers the original sigma (the two py_vollib call sites agree with each other).
`heuristic_should_roll` — a losing position rolls, a winning/breakeven one doesn't, and a
profitable CARRIED vertical can flip a losing rolled vertical's own verdict (proving
`carried_value` is genuinely part of the decision, not just the rolled side).
`ev_should_roll` — missing IV on any leg returns `None`; **a concrete scenario where the
heuristic and EV verdicts genuinely DIFFER**, both sides' real outputs computed and
compared, not asserted a priori — the direct proof EV is a second opinion, not a relabeled
heuristic.

`tests/test_roll_executor.py` (21 → 25, +4): the `-1` bid becomes `0.0` (mutation-checked:
reverting `b >= -1` to `b >= 0` makes the test fail exactly as predicted); a real positive
bid and a real `0.0` bid are both unaffected (the sentinel fix doesn't touch real values);
`closing_net + opening_net == mid_net` exactly, each independently matching a direct
`leg_net_price` computation over just its own legs.

`tests/test_roll_ancestors.py` (new, 5 tests): a never-rolled trade and a missing trade_id
both have depth 0; a one-hop chain has depth 1 at the child, still 0 at the origin; a
3-hop chain has depth 2 at the open leaf (mutation-checked: dropping the CTE's `+1` makes
the 3-hop test fail exactly as predicted); depth is correctly bounded by `max_depth` (5 real
hops capped at 2 when asked, uncapped at 5 when the bound is raised) — the belt-and-
suspenders proven to actually work, not just declared.

`tests/test_roll_wiring.py` (24 → 26, +2): a position at the cap (`max_rolls_per_position=
0`) is refused BEFORE `select_roll_target` is ever awaited (spy/call-count proof, mutation-
checked: disabling the cap condition makes the "not awaited" assertion fail exactly as
predicted); a position below the cap proceeds to call it normally.

## 2026-09-29 - BUILT — W54b: wire rule 3/rule 3e to the close-or-roll comparison, gated by
`policy` + `execute_rolls`

SCOPE. W54a (`e5a3011`) shipped the comparison models but left them fully unreachable. This
wave makes rule 3 (ITM assignment risk) and rule 3e (pre-ex-div assignment risk) in
`portfolio.py` actually consult `assignment_response.policy` and, when it allows rolling,
run the close-or-roll comparison in the orchestrator before deciding to close. Re-reading
the exact current code (unchanged since W54a) resolved the two risks W54a's own research
flagged, and surfaced a third, more subtle one, all confirmed by direct source read before
writing any code:

1. **The arbitration conflict turned out to be nearly free.** `condor_defense`'s block was
   already gated `if not should_exit`. Rule 3/3e's new roll-candidate signal lives in a
   SEPARATE local (`assignment_roll_side`, not `condor_roll_side`) and — the key move —
   rule 3/3e keep setting `should_exit=True` exactly as before even when they ALSO offer a
   roll candidate. That alone means the existing gate already prevents `condor_defense`
   from ever running on a tick rule 3/3e already claimed. No new arbitration logic was
   needed — proven directly (see PROOF), not just argued.
2. **The side-encoding fix** ("put"/"call" → "P"/"C") is a one-line translation at the
   point `assignment_roll_side` is set; `itm_side`'s own string (used in the CLOSE
   exit_reason text) is untouched.
3. **New finding, not in W54a's own list: the PDT veto (rule 5) would have silently
   mis-routed a blocked position.** It already resets `should_exit`/`partial_exit_
   quantity`/`exit_reason` on a veto, but nothing reset a roll-candidate local. A
   PDT-vetoed position would then report `should_exit=False, roll_side=<set>` — EXACTLY the
   shape `_partition_roll_positions` (W61) already treats as a condor_defense-style roll
   ready to place, feeding it straight into `_execute_roll` and bypassing the PDT
   protection entirely. Found while writing the plan, fixed, and mutation-checked (removing
   the fix reproduces the exact bug it prevents).

**Also found while writing the plan, not assumed fixed**: `PortfolioManager` had no
`assignment_response_config` at all — only the orchestrator read `assignment_response`
directly. Added, mirroring `condor_defense_config`'s own exact threading pattern.

DESIGN.

`src/ait/execution/roll_executor.py`: `PreparedRollCombo` gains `quotes: dict[int,
tuple[float | None, float | None]]` — the raw per-conId bid/ask dict `poll_leg_quotes`
already builds, exposed so the EV comparison's per-leg IV gathering can reuse data already
fetched instead of a second broker round-trip.

`src/ait/execution/portfolio.py`: `PortfolioManager.__init__` gains
`assignment_response_config` (the missed-gap fix). New locals `assignment_roll_side`/
`assignment_action_reason`, declared before the take-profit/rule-3 if/elif chain (moving
statements INTO the middle of an existing elif chain is a syntax error — caught immediately
by `py_compile`, fixed by placing them before the chain starts instead). Rule 3, inside `if
itm_side is not None:`, after the existing (unchanged) `should_exit = True`: when `policy !=
"close_only"`, sets `assignment_roll_side = "P" if itm_side == "put" else "C"` and
`assignment_action_reason = f"assignment_risk_{policy}"`. Rule 3e: same pattern, always
`"C"` (calls-only by construction). PDT veto: resets both locals to `None` alongside its
existing resets — finding 3's fix. Return site: `roll_side = condor_roll_side or
assignment_roll_side`; `action = ROLL if roll_side is not None else derive(...)` — the two
locals are provably never both set (finding 1), so `or` is a safe merge.

`src/ait/config/settings.py` / `config.yaml`: `AssignmentResponseConfig` gains
`execute_rolls: bool = False` — mirrors `condor_defense.execute_rolls` exactly, a
placement-level opt-in separate from `policy`, added now because its consumer exists.

`src/ait/bot/orchestrator.py`: `PortfolioManager(...)`'s construction site threads
`assignment_response_config=settings.assignment_response`. `_execute_roll` gains optional
`prepared`/`roll_target` params — when the caller already has them (the comparison must
prepare a combo to run the comparison in the first place), skips a SECOND ~110-209s chain
fetch for the same decision; fully backward compatible, `condor_defense`'s own call site
passes neither. New `_compare_close_or_roll(pos) -> bool`: `execute_rolls=False` → `False`
immediately; fetches trade/target/combo (stopping short of CAS/seed/place); `policy==
"roll_only"` → always roll once prepared; `"close_or_roll"` → `heuristic_should_roll` or,
for `"ev"`, a data-quality fallback (`roll_target.iv_is_guessed`) then a new
`_gather_ev_leg_inputs` (solves each leg's IV from `prepared.quotes` via
`solve_iv_from_price`, `None` on any REQUIRED leg's failure — a carried leg's own failure
just drops it, same as `carried_value`'s own fallback elsewhere) feeding `ev_should_roll`,
itself falling back to the heuristic if it returns `None`. On a roll verdict: `await self.
_execute_roll(pos, prepared=prepared, roll_target=roll_target)`. `_trading_cycle`'s exit
loop: `if pos.roll_side and await self._compare_close_or_roll(pos): continue` before
`_execute_exit` — `pos.roll_side` alone is a safe, sufficient gate per finding 1's dual-
shape argument (a `should_exit=True` position with `roll_side` set can only have come from
rule 3/3e, never `condor_defense`).

PROOF. `tests/test_w54b_assignment_roll_dispatch.py` (new, 17 tests). Part A (real
`_evaluate_position` calls, same `PortfolioManager.__new__` harness `test_w52_multileg_itm_
diagnosis.py` uses): `policy=="close_only"` reports no roll candidate (byte-identical to
before this wave); `roll_only`/`close_or_roll` report the correctly-translated `"P"`/`"C"`
side, `should_exit` UNCHANGED (still `True`); a `getattr`-guarded config-less manager
behaves like `close_only`; rule 3e always reports `"C"`; the PDT-veto fix, both directly
asserted AND mutation-checked (removing the reset reproduces `roll_side='P'` on a
`should_exit=False` position — the exact bug finding 3 names); the arbitration claim,
proven not assumed — `evaluate_condor_defense` monkeypatched to a FORCED ROLL verdict,
asserting it is called ZERO times once rule 3 has already claimed the tick, mutation-checked
by temporarily removing the `not should_exit` gate (the test then fails with `call_count==1`,
confirming the gate is genuinely load-bearing, not incidentally passing).

Part B (`orchestrator._compare_close_or_roll`/`_gather_ev_leg_inputs`, real `StateManager`,
monkeypatched `select_roll_target`/`prepare_roll_combo`/`heuristic_should_roll`/`ev_should_
roll` as spies): `execute_rolls=False` returns `False` with ZERO calls into `select_roll_
target`; `policy=="roll_only"` always rolls with the heuristic never even called;
`comparison_model=="heuristic"` — a losing position rolls, a winning one closes (real
`heuristic_should_roll` outputs, not mocked); `"ev"` with `iv_is_guessed=True` falls back to
heuristic with `ev_should_roll` never called; `"ev"` with every leg's quote missing falls
back to heuristic (via `_gather_ev_leg_inputs` returning `None`); a REAL `ev_should_roll`
call with solvable legs, `select_roll_target`/`prepare_roll_combo` each confirmed called
EXACTLY ONCE — the direct proof of the no-second-broker-round-trip claim, not just "should
be". `_gather_ev_leg_inputs` directly: a missing quote refuses the whole result; a carried
leg's own missing quote just drops it (closing/opening still build); the happy path builds
all three lists with real solved IVs (`> 0`) and the correct lowercase `flag`.

A real phantom-failure incident, caught and correctly diagnosed rather than treated as a
regression: mid-way through this wave's gates, an unrelated `inspect.getsource`-based test
(`test_r16_round2_fixes.py::TestBagQuotePathAlive`) failed in a background fast-lane run
because `orchestrator.py` was edited (a small mypy type-narrowing fix) WHILE that run was
still executing — exactly the "Never edit a source file while the test suite is running"
failure class CLAUDE.md documents. Confirmed by re-running that one test in isolation
immediately afterward (passed cleanly) and then re-running the FULL fast lane with no
concurrent edits, which came back clean. Recorded so a future session recognizes the same
symptom fast — the same discipline as `roll_booking.py`'s own W57-era `git checkout`
