## 2026-10-23 - W95 AS PLANNED: eight hidden policy numbers become configuration variables; the census ignore list narrows (label note: W91 is the other session's table-unification wave, W94 the IB-endpoint wave)

Operator decisions (2026-10-23), taken after W93's measure-only pass: the nine policy numbers that the census's "unit-like" ignore list (60, 252, 100, ...) hid are judged by one rule. A number a study or an operator might sensibly vary is a **configuration variable** (a schema field with bounds and an explanation, a YAML key in `config.yaml`, or in `config_research.yaml` when research-only); a number that is a fixed convention stays a named, documented constant. Eight become configuration variables with defaults equal to today's literals, so **no result moves**: research-only in `config_research.yaml` - `engine_tuning.drawdown_high_lookback_rows` (60, the drawdown gate's rolling high), `engine_tuning.replay_lookback_days` (60 calendar days, the replay history pad), `walkforward_tuning.oos_feature_context_bars` (252, history prepended to each test window), `walkforward_tuning.meta_label_min_window_rows` (60), `walkforward_tuning.min_fetched_rows` (100, "more than"), `walkforward_tuning.min_backtest_rows` (60, the optimizer's `_MIN_BACKTEST_ROWS`, which is used five times including `* 2` and `// 2`); live-shared in the `config.yaml` `regime:` block - `min_history_rows` (60), `iv_rank_min_rows` (60), `iv_rank_window_rows` (252). The ninth, the Sharpe `min(252, trades per year)` cap in `result.py`, stays a fixed constant: named (`SHARPE_ANNUALIZATION_CAP`) and explained in RESEARCH_GUIDE.md, because a study that could change how its own Sharpe is annualized would make reported Sharpes incomparable.

**Facts that shape it (read from the code, not assumed).** (a) The regime detector is live-only (`orchestrator.py` builds it from `settings.regime`; research never imports it). Its "IV rank" is a realized-vol percentile proxy (20-day vol against its last 252 values), NOT `ait.data.iv_rank` and not the feature `vol_regime.iv_rank_lookback`; the guide must say so. Its 60-row IV-rank minimum counts 20-day-vol values, so the proxy stays 0.5 until the history reaches about 80 rows although `analyze` needs only 60; documented, not changed. (b) `walkforward.py` `context_bars = 60` in the meta-labeler path is NOT a context length: the shadow labeller runs on the full training frame with `context_bars=0`, and the number only guards `len(train_df) <= 60`; `train_head` is assigned and never used and its comment ("same 60-bar convention as the OOS run") is stale (the OOS run uses 252). It becomes `meta_label_min_window_rows`; the dead local goes (no behaviour). (c) The other `context_bars` (`min(252, len(train_df))`) is a real feature context; `backtest.context_bars` already exists with a different meaning (engine intraday look-back), so the new name differs. (d) `replay.py` pads the replay window by 60 CALENDAR days (about 42 rows), so the replayed engine's 60-row drawdown gate sees fewer rows (`min(60, len)`): pre-existing, documented, not fixed. (e) The drawdown gate's diagnostic key `pct_from_60d_high` keeps its name (renaming would change run records). 

**Validators.** `oos_feature_context_bars` below the feature spec's longest look-back (`vol_regime.iv_rank_lookback`) is refused when the walk-forward starts (a too-short context silently yields NaN features); the exact minimum is fixed by a perturbation test before the rule is written. `regime.min_history_rows` must cover the trend measure's longest need (default 60 against a need of 55), same pattern as W92's floor <= cap.

**Scan interval, deliberately NOT here (proposed W96).** `backtest.scan_interval_minutes` (default 60) is resolved by the engine and never read (PLAN.md has recorded "resolved but unused" since an earlier audit). With intraday bars the engine makes ONE entry attempt per day at the first bar of the entry window and then tries a limit fill over the next `limit_order_timeout_bars` bars. The operator wants the engine to use the interval as designed, behind a new on/off configuration variable, default Off. That is a feature, not a conversion (it changes what the engine decides intraday), so it gets its own plan; with the flag Off every result stays byte-identical. Open design questions for W96: what is re-evaluated at each scan (strike and credit at the intraday spot? which gates are daily and which intraday?), entries per day, DTE and pricing at a later time of day, the flag name (proposal `backtest.intraday_scanning_enabled`). The study harness constant `STUDY_SCAN_INTERVAL_MINUTES` stays as is until then.

**Last step, with the operator's review before anything is classified.** The census ignore list narrows: 60, 252, 100 leave `TRIVIAL` (12 / 24 / 1000 only if they surface something). About 93 newly visible literals are expected (the W93 pass: `x 100` conversions, `/ 365`, `sqrt(252)`, 31 in `ml/features.py`, two display slices). Nothing is categorized by Claude alone: a review table (file:line, function, number, expression, proposed category and why, grouped by kind, anything that reads as a window / threshold / minimum / limit listed separately) goes to the operator, who confirms each group as a fixed unit conversion or asks for a conversion; only then is the allowlist written and committed. Own commit; scanner and allowlist only.

**Gates (same as W90 / W92 / W93).** Built in a worktree on branch `w95` after plan mode; reference dump, `gate_parity_ab`, `ex_div_gate_ab` and the walk-forward smoke byte-identical to `main`; per-field perturbation tests at the real code path; the W92 regime golden unchanged at defaults; mutation check on all eight read sites with hash-verified restore; node-id reconciliation against a base worktree; fast lane; compileall; `scripts/typecheck.py`; `scripts/smoke_deploy.py`. Every new key is explained in the schema description, in `config.yaml` / `config_research.yaml` (comment plus a pointer), and in RESEARCH_GUIDE.md / RUNBOOK.md.
**Pre-merge rule.** A bot (`ait.main`, pid 11554) and the supervisor (`run_orchestrator.py`, pid 3257) were running when this was planned. Before the fast-forward: check for them and, if running, STOP and ask the operator when to merge. This wave adds three keys to `config.yaml` (the `regime:` block), so the W92 hazard applies: a process on older code that re-reads the file would reject them (the supervisor froze its settings at start). Nothing is pushed; no restart (the operator's call).

## 2026-10-24 - W98 AS PLANNED: every model feature has an on/off switch in `config.yaml` (`ml.features.<group>.use`); a study drops, adds or re-windows features with one line each

Operator request (2026-10-24, plan mode, approved after four revisions): the model's feature list was fixed in code (`config/feature_names.py::_BASE_TEMPLATE`, 75 columns, plus the 26 VLMC intraday names); only the windows were settings (W88d / W97). A research user could not see the whole list in one place, drop a feature for one study, or try one, without editing code the live models also run on. Built in a worktree on branch `w98` (label note: W96 stays parked; W98 is this wave).
**Design (the operator's choices, with the reasons given in plan mode).** (1) The list lives in `config.yaml`, not only the overlay: it is shared with live, like the windows. (2) Each `ml.features` group keeps its windows and gains `use:`, one `true`/`false` switch per feature, so the windows and the switches of a group sit side by side (a window is shared by several features, e.g. `sma_mid` feeds three columns, so it stays a group setting and is not copied onto each feature). (3) Switches, not a list you comment lines out of: a study is laid over `config.yaml` and a list laid over a list REPLACES it (dropping one feature would mean copying ~100 names that silently miss any later addition); mappings merge key by key, so a study writes one line. (4) Switch keys are stable ROLE names (`rsi_long`, not `rsi_14`). (5) Five columns the code computes but no model used (`put_call_proxy`, `vix_term_structure`, `skew_proxy`, `momentum_divergence`, `range_compression`) ship `false`, so they are testable by a study with no new code. (6) A brand-new feature still needs code (compute it, add its name to `CATALOGUE`, a `false` line in `config.yaml`); a test fails until the file lists everything the code produces.
**Scope.** `false` removes a column from the inputs of the direction, range and vol-magnitude models and of the tuner (all four go through `FeatureSpec.feature_names`). The column is still computed (the meta-labeler, the gates and the dashboards read some), so a switch does not shorten the warm-up and the meta-labeler's 20 inputs are not affected.
**The hash rule (why no retrain).** The switches enter the feature-spec hash ONLY when one differs from its default (the W97 pattern); `use` is excluded from the existing window dumps, so at the defaults the canonical string is byte-identical and the hash stays `6e0e3f8f922f6b88`. Flipping a switch in `config.yaml` is a live change (every saved model is refused and retrained) and the operator's call.
**Gates.** The default list (with and without VLMC) and the hash were recorded on the unchanged base BEFORE the code changed (`tests/data/w98_golden.json`); a config.yaml completeness guard; every switch flipped one at a time (name list, hash); training through the real ensemble / range / vol-magnitude path; a study that switches a feature and a window; fast lane; `compileall`; `typecheck`; `smoke_deploy`. RESEARCH_GUIDE.md ("Choosing the model's features (W98)", plus §4, §6, §9, §12 pointers) and RUNBOOK.md ("Feature switches (W98)") explain how to set, include and exclude features.
**Pre-merge rule.** The bot (`ait.main`) and the supervisor are running from the main checkout. Both freeze their settings at start, so the new `use:` keys cannot reach their old schema; as with W95 / W97 the merge is safe with them running, but Claude stops and asks the operator before the fast-forward. Nothing pushed; no restart.

Planned in the W98 AS PLANNED entry above (plan approved before building). Built in a worktree on branch `w98` (commit "W98: every model feature has an on/off switch ..."), **not merged into `main`**; the bot and supervisor run from the main checkout and were not touched. Nothing pushed; no restart.

**AS BUILT.** `config/feature_names.py` holds one ordered `CATALOGUE` (group -> feature roles; 80 daily features, 75 on by default, plus the 26 VLMC names moved here, `FeatureEngine.VLMC_FEATURE_NAMES` re-exports them), `DEFAULT_USE`, `OFF_BY_DEFAULT` (the five computed-but-unused columns) and `use_switches(cfg)`; `_BASE_TEMPLATE` is now derived from the catalogue. Every window group in `config/settings.py` (`_UseGroup`) has `use: dict[str, bool]` (a missing key takes its default; an unknown key is a load error that lists the valid names); `price_action` and `seasonality` are new switch-only groups; switching every daily feature off is refused. `FeatureSpec.feature_names` applies the switches (the direction, range and vol-magnitude models and the tuner all read it). `_hash` excludes `use` from the existing dumps and adds `w98: {group: {feature: switch}}` only for switches that differ from their default. `config.yaml` lists all 13 groups with their windows (identical to before) and `use:` blocks (220 lines, the column in a comment); `studies/_template.yaml` has the example; the run record stores `feature_list` next to `feature_spec_hash`. RESEARCH_GUIDE "Choosing the model's features (W98)" (drop, try, re-window, add a brand-new feature, why switches and not a list) with pointers in sections 4, 6, 9 and 12; RUNBOOK "Feature switches (W98)".
**VERIFIED.** The default list (75 / 101 names) and hash `6e0e3f8f922f6b88` were recorded on the unchanged base BEFORE the code changed (`tests/data/w98_golden.json`) and are reproduced; `compute()` frames are `assert_frame_equal` with every switch off. `tests/test_w98_feature_switches.py` (143 tests, none removed anywhere): config.yaml lists every catalogue feature in order; each of the 80 daily features flipped alone adds or removes exactly its column and no two flips share a hash; each VLMC switch; role keys follow a window change (`rsi_long: false` with `rsi_long: 21` drops `rsi_21`); validation errors; the real ensemble / range / vol-magnitude training stores the switched list and a model trained under other switches is refused; a study switches a feature and a window in one run, a typo in a study is refused, and the origin view, run record and parity manifest show it. Fast lane **7092 passed / 56 skipped / 153 deselected** (first run: 3 failed, all fixed: the W70 "every config field has a reader" scan skips `settings.py`, so `use_switches` lives in `feature_names.py` with an explicit read per group; the W88 test takes the first `yaml` block that starts `name:` in RESEARCH_GUIDE, so the new example starts with a comment; the W97 schema test compares windows only). Existing tests edited: two assertions in `tests/test_w97_feature_windows.py` now ignore the `use` key. `compileall` and `scripts/typecheck.py` clean. `scripts/smoke_deploy.py` **SMOKE PASS (13 checks)** against the real `data/` through a temporary symlink (read-only; its own no-writes check passed; the symlink was removed afterwards).
**FALLS SHORT / CAVEATS.** (a) No mutation check and no reference-dump / `gate_parity_ab` A/B this time (the golden tests and the one-by-one flips stand in for them). (b) No full research walk-forward was run with a study that switches a feature; the study path is tested through settings loading, the spec and the real model training. (c) A switch only removes a column from the model inputs: it is still computed, so the warm-up does not shorten and the meta-labeler's 20 inputs do not change (documented). (d) The intraday switches matter only when a model is trained with an intraday store. (e) Adding a brand-new feature needs code (documented as four steps); a new feature that is on by default or adds NaN rows changes live and needs the operator. (f) The running bot and supervisor still run the code they started with.
**NEXT.** (1) Merge `w98` into `main` (fast-forward) only on the operator's word; both processes freeze their settings at start, so the merge is safe with them running (as W95 / W97), and with no switch changed no model retrains. (2) Optional follow-ups the operator can order: a first study that switches `skew_proxy` on (and `hurst_psd_divergence` off) as a B1-style test; a mutation pass over the switch read sites. (3) W96 stays parked; W91 unchanged.

## 2026-10-24 - W99 FOLLOW-UP: `--paper` is no longer hardcoded in the supervisor; paper or live is one decision (`config/launch_mode.py`) that also refuses a paper bot on a live endpoint

The W99 AS BUILT entry above records "`--paper` stays hardcoded in `master.py`" as the operator's decision, justified as "paper stays structural, a safety". **That justification was wrong.** `--paper` only sets `settings.trading.mode`; which account trades is decided by the IB endpoint (`IBKR_PORT`) and login. With `--paper` hardcoded and a live-account port in `.env`, the supervised bot would have traded real money while labelled paper. The operator also prefers no hardcoded value where the setting can be read.

**AS BUILT.** `src/ait/config/launch_mode.py::decide` (pure, stdlib plus `ait.data.ib_ports`), used by `BotManager.start` (the supervisor) and by `ait.main.run_bot`. **Live needs all of:** `config.yaml` `trading.mode: live` AND `.env` `TRADING_MODE=live` (either one saying otherwise gives a paper start), the environment interlock `AIT_ALLOW_LIVE=1` (environment-only, like `AIT_ALLOW_UNDEFINED_RISK`), a live-account IB endpoint (4001 / 7496) and, when `IBKR_ACCOUNT` is set, a non-paper id (paper ids start with `D`). **Paper is refused** on a live-account endpoint or with a live account id. A refusal starts nothing, alerts once per 30 minutes (`REFUSING to start ...`), and is retried on the next health cycle; `--paper` still forces the paper label but the endpoint check still applies. `.env.example`, the `trading.mode` description and comment, RUNBOOK (go-live checklist and alert row), GETTING_STARTED, GUIDE and TECHNICAL_GUIDE were updated; the other W99 ledgers were updated for the changed lines.

**VERIFIED.** `tests/test_launch_mode.py` (34 tests: the decision table, the real `BotManager.start` with a stubbed `Popen`, and the real `run_bot` refusal path); a mutation check (reintroducing the hardcoded flag fails `test_fully_enabled_live_starts_without_the_paper_flag`). Also in this follow-up: `config.yaml` `sentiment.enabled` set to false with a comment (the retired section is read by nothing); claim ledgers written for every maintained document under `reports/docs_review_20261024/`.

**FALLS SHORT / CAVEATS.** (a) A change to the supervisor needs a full supervisor restart; the operator had stopped the bot and the supervisor, and nothing was restarted. (b) Three environment values now gate live (`config.yaml`, `TRADING_MODE`, `AIT_ALLOW_LIVE`); the operator chose "both must say live" plus the interlock, so there is deliberate redundancy. (c) `ait.main` run by hand with a live config and no env votes now starts as paper (or is refused on a live port), which is stricter than before. (d) The IBC `config.ini` still decides paper or live for the supervisor's own Gateway restart; this wave does not touch it. (e) The account-id check relies on IB paper ids starting with `D`.

## 2026-10-25 - CORRECTION to the entry above (EXIT LADDER paragraph) and W101a read-only audit result: the intrinsic floor explains only part of the unfilled exits

**What the entry above overstated.** It said the last limits (2.23-2.48) "were below the short 707 put's intrinsic (>= 2.76) and could not fill". Two errors: 2.76 is the short put alone, the spread's intrinsic is `max(0, 707-S) - max(0, 704-S)` (2.39-2.70 at the last bars); and the claim was made for all 185 orders, while the logs held for this check cover 10-23 only.
**Audit (read-only; scratchpad script on `logs/ait.log*` + `data/historical.db` 5-minute QQQ bars, opened `mode=ro`).** 63 leg-priced / anchor-priced exit placements on 10-23 (`combo_exit_limit_from_legs`, `combo_exit_no_quote_pricing_from_anchor`; every one logged "BAG never ticked", i.e. no combo quote at all). **26 of 63 had a limit below the spread's intrinsic at the matching 5-minute bar**, all from about 15:20 ET onward (e.g. 19:51Z limit 2.46 vs 2.70; 19:58Z limit 2.48 vs 2.61). The other 37 (earlier in the day) were ABOVE intrinsic and above the synthesized cost from the delayed leg quotes, and still did not fill. At 19:58Z the delayed leg quotes were short 707P 2.82/2.87 and long 704P 0.50/0.52 (synthesized buy-back 2.38; limit 2.48): marketable against those quotes, but the market data is delayed (IB error 10091 on the leg subscriptions) and the long put's 0.50 is not credible for a put 0.4 out of the money minutes before the close.
**So two causes are open, not one:** (1) near expiry the delayed leg quotes understate the spread and the limit ends below intrinsic (26 of 63; the W101b intrinsic floor fixes exactly this); (2) the 37 earlier placements priced above intrinsic did not fill either, so a combo order with no combo quote ("BAG never ticked") may simply not match on this paper account with delayed data, or the delayed quotes were stale by more than the limit's margin. This is unproven. W101a must settle it before W101b is designed: order statuses and `whyHeld`/error codes per `order_id`, whether any BAG order ever filled on this account since delayed data (entries: `trades.entry_time` fills on 09-28/09-29), and the 10-22 placements (rotated out of the logs checked here).
**Plan consequence.** The W101 sequence stands, with the audit first and the fix's scope decided after it: the intrinsic floor stays (it is correct near expiry whatever else is wrong), but escalation alone will not fix cause (2) if combos do not match without a combo quote; if so the options are leg-out closes near expiry or waiting for live data (OPRA), to be decided with the operator.

## 2026-10-26 - W101-P AS BUILT (script and tests only; the probe RUN is a separate step with the operator present): `scripts/probe_w101_combo_close.py`, a paper-account probe of "does a condor close fill, at what concession, how fast"

**Why.** W101-B/C changed the pricing and the expiry booking; whether a closing combo priced from the legs actually fills on this delayed-data paper account, and if the shipped escalation is enough, is still unmeasured (the 2026-10-22/23 closes were below the real market for part of the time and nothing was recorded). EVIDENCE that reframed the question (read from `reports/w53_probe/2026-09-29/roll.jsonl`): the W53 4-leg roll with NO BAG quote (`bid None / ask None`), priced from the legs, filled at 0.08 against a 0.09 limit in ~95 s, while the two trials where the BAG DID quote did not fill even at natural. So "a combo needs a combo quote" is not the likely cause; the likely cause is a limit below the simulator's real market while delayed quotes understate it. The probe therefore measures marketability against what the market did ~15 minutes later (the "truth tail"), not only fill / no fill.

**AS BUILT** (no `src/ait` change, so no section-3 diff). `scripts/probe_w101_combo_close.py` (commands `preflight` (default, places nothing), `open --trial T --kind far|pin`, `close --trial T`, `flatten --trial T [--legout-only]`, `cancel`, `status`, `report` (never connects)); `tests/test_w101_probe_script.py` (180 tests); catalogue entry + `docs/reference/SCRIPTS.md`.
- Identity and guards: client id **96** (98 belongs to `validate_w55_synthetic_delta.py`; any other id is refused because a fallback id cannot cancel orders placed under 96); paper `D` account; SPY, one lot, four legs, wings <= 3; every orderRef `W101PROBE-<trial>-<step>-r<k>-<epoch>` (the reconciler only ever adopts an order whose orderRef equals a trade id); the bot-stopped guard is a non-blocking `flock` of `data/orchestrator.lock` (the supervisor flocks it; the pid in the file is informational) plus `data/bot_heartbeat` age < 900 s in market hours; no SPY option position the probe does not own and no foreign working SPY order (`get_positions_fresh`, `None` = refuse); NetLiquidation >= $25k and ExcessLiquidity >= 3x the what-if margin; HALT_UNTRACKED / open-DB-leg collision; per-command windows (open 30 min after the open to 45 before the close, close to 30 before, flatten and cancel 5 / 5, so a 0DTE emergency close is never blocked; a 0DTE `pin` trial must be opened by 14:30 and its close started by 15:15 ET).
- The experiment (`close`): the bot's exact leg-priced rule (`bot_rung_limit`: `(N + cross) + n*max(pct*(N + cross), step)`, N = the legs' natural with BUY legs at ask, SELL legs at bid, a -1 bid = 0), then rungs 4-6 at 25% / 50% / 100% of the remaining gap to the wing width; floored by the bot's intrinsic floor; clamped to the width (a hard check inside the ladder as well); `cap_binds` recorded when natural > width. One NEW order per rung, same trial tag, resting 120 s, then **cancel-and-confirm**: wait up to 30 s for a terminal status, then ALWAYS check executions (ib_insync marks an order Cancelled locally on some errors, e.g. 10148 / 161, that do not prove it did not fill). One probe order live at a time. State is written ahead of every `placeOrder`. A `QuoteSampler` streams the four legs, SPY and the BAG (with `marketDataType`) for the ladder and a 15-minute truth tail; an `ErrorRecorder` keeps every code (including those `IBKRClient` ignores).
- `flatten`: the same combo ladder, then **leg-out**: shorts first (riskier side first), each confirmed flat from fresh positions before anything else; a long is sold only when both shorts are flat; reduce-only checks; nothing is sold and "SHORT STILL OPEN" is raised if a short will not come back. Positions come from the broker, never the state. A Ctrl-C or an error cancels the probe's working orders and exits (130 / 1); it NEVER auto-flattens.
- `report` (pure; refuses `schema != 1`): per run, BAG ticked, legs priceable, filled rung, concessions (vs first natural, vs natural at the fill, vs first mid), time to fill, truth-tail marketability per rung; classes A (filled by rung 3: the shipped escalation is enough), B (rung 4-6: deeper ladder), C (never filled although the BAG never ticked, the legs priced, the width was reached and a limit was truly marketable), C' (never marketable: stale delayed quotes), D (unreadable); overall verdicts BOT_LADDER_SUFFICIENT / NEEDS_DEEPER_LADDER / NO_MATCH_WITHOUT_COMBO_QUOTE (needs >= 2 runs) / LIMITS_NEVER_MARKETABLE (only when no run looks like C) / INCONCLUSIVE, flagged `mixed` when runs disagree; leg-out outcome LEG_OUT_VIABLE / NOTHING_FILLS_ON_DELAYED.
- DEVIATIONS from the plan: the `far` kind picks shorts ~1.5% out of the money by strike (no delta targeting: delayed data makes greeks unreliable, and it avoids `OptionsChainService`); a lone C beside a C' is INCONCLUSIVE, not C'; the redundant `max(lim, prev)` was removed (a rung that does not rise is skipped).

**VERIFIED.** 180 tests with the broker faked at the network edge only and a virtual clock (guards incl. a real second-fd `flock`; the maths; **parity with the bot's real `TradingOrchestrator._close_multi_leg`**: rungs 0-3 and the floor equal the bot's for the incident quotes; the ladder: fills at rung 0 / 2, never fills = 7 rungs ending at the width with each cancel confirmed before the next order and never two live, cancel races a fill, local Cancelled then an execution, pending-cancel-forever, Inactive, reject with its code, ticking BAG, BUY leg without an ask places nothing, write-ahead state, hard cap; open / close / flatten / cancel / status / preflight; leg-out ordering and the "short never fills -> no long is sold" case; the report's classes and verdict rules; `main` Ctrl-C / error / guard refusal; the script runs standalone with `-I`). Mutation pass: 26 mutants over the width clamp, the hard cap, shorts-before-longs, the post-cancel executions check, the flock guard, `cap_binds`, the verdict rules, reduce-only both ways, the floor, Inactive handling, cancel confirmation, client id, write-ahead, cancel-after-rest, the bot formula, the -1 bid, the delay band, `reached_width`, the pin short-put rule, the flatten window, wing caps, foreign-order guard, tag-only cancel, heartbeat, state schema: all killed except one equivalent (removed). A first fast-lane run failed one guard test (`test_w69`: a real paper account id used as a fake value in the new test file); replaced by a dummy id.

**FALLS SHORT / FOR THE OPERATOR.** (1) Nothing here has touched a real IB session: the fakes cannot prove IB's behaviour, so `preflight` (no orders) is the first live call. (2) The probe is the operator's to run: Gateway up, supervisor AND bot stopped, market hours, the operator present; trial plan: day 1 `preflight` ~10:05, F1 open 10:15 / close 10:25, F2 open 12:00 / close 12:10, P1 (0DTE pin) open by 14:30 / close by 15:15; each close <= 7 x 120 s + a 15-minute truth tail (~30 min); paper cost a few tens of dollars (<= $300 worst case per trial). ## 2026-10-26 - W101-P RESULTS AND CORRECTIONS: a closing combo that contains a leg nobody bids for does not fill, whatever the limit; leaving that leg out lets it fill (cause found by an intervention, not by reading the logs)

**What was run (paper, one lot, client id 96, TWS 7497, 2026-10-26, market hours).** F1 (SPY far condor), P1 (SPY 0DTE pin, delay emulated 900 s), N1 and N2 (SPY 0DTE "nobid": short put in the money, long call wing 3 above a short call, the long wing offered at 0.01 with NO bid). Evidence: `reports/w101_probe/2026-10-26/events.jsonl`; `report` states the verdict.

| trial | closing combo | result |
|---|---|---|
| F1: every leg bid | 4 legs | filled at rung 0 in 12 s at exactly the legs' natural (0.86) |
| P1: every leg bid, 0DTE, short put ITM, quotes emulated 15 min late | 4 legs | filled at rung 0 in 6 s at 0.91 (live natural 0.90); the stale limit was above the market |
| **N1**: long 777C wing unbid, KEPT in the combo | 4 legs | **no fill in 7 rungs / 14 min; limits 2.29 -> 3.00 (the full wing width) against a live natural of 0.84-1.12; IB accepted every limit without a price check** |
| **N2**: long 778C wing unbid, LEFT OUT of the combo | 3 legs | first rung rejected by IB's price band ("not at or more aggressive than 1.165", the floor had pushed it to 2.36); the band-clamped second rung (1.16) filled in 6 s at 0.86 (live natural 0.84-0.85) |
N1 and N2 were minutes apart on the same account. N1's leg-out (shorts first) filled every sellable leg; the unbid wing could not be sold and was left to expire.

**CONCLUSION (supported by the contrast).** IB gives a combo a market, and so a price band and a match, only if every leg can trade. A combo that includes a leg to SELL with no bid has no market: it is accepted at any limit and never fills. Every one of the 176 exits for the QQQ condor on 10-22/23 included the 772C long wing, quoted `-1/0.01` (no bid) in all of them; none filled and none drew a price-band reject, as N1 did. Leaving a worthless unbid long wing out of the closing combo (it expires on its own) is the fix N2 demonstrates.

**CORRECTIONS to earlier statements (made in this session).**
- "The 10-22/23 quotes were delayed": WRONG. OPRA was active; fitting the logged 707P quote against QQQ (no-future bar alignment, time-decay trend) is best at lag 0 and clearly worse at 15 min on both days (RMSE 0.33 / 0.36 at lag 0, 0.56 / 0.54 at 15 min). The 5-minute bars cannot separate 0 from about 5 min, but 15 min is excluded.
- "The endpoint (TWS vs Gateway) decides the data type": WRONG, retracted. Same login, same entitlements; the bot was on TWS 7497 on 10-22 and on Gateway 4002 on 10-23 and failed on both.
- "A combo needs every leg two-sided to tick": unsupported (F1's combo stayed silent with all legs two-sided and still filled). The bot's short BAG-poll window (2.5 s) is a separate, minor observation.
- The W101-P entry above says the likely cause was "a limit below the simulator's real market while delayed quotes understate it": superseded by the conclusion here. The delay emulation (`--emulate-delay`) stays as a tool.
- The `exit_intrinsic_delayed_band_pct` allowance (W101-B) assumed delayed quotes; the SPOT is what is delayed or missing (OPRA gives real-time options, not the stock), so the allowance still has a reason, but its effect is real: near expiry it lifts limits well above IB's price band (N2: floor 2.36 vs band 1.165, one wasted cycle). The existing exit-band handling re-places under the band.

**What else the trials showed.** The stock feed is the weak one (no real-time equity subscription: errors 10089 / 10091 / 10167, and 10197 while another session competed); the probe estimates the underlying from a call/put pair (`probe_spot_from_options`). The operator confirmed: OPRA active before 10-22; "share real-time data with paper" on; no competing sessions possible on one login. Quote age was 0-1 s on the options in this session. The bot's touch stop and floor read the delayed or missing stock price: a candidate change (derive the underlying from the options) is registered, not built.

**BUILT in the probe since the entry above** (script and tests only): `--symbol SPY|QQQ`; kind `nobid` with `--short-call`; `--require-nobid`; `--exclude-unbid` (refused if the unbid leg has value, > 0.05); a clamp under IB's price band after a reject; `--emulate-delay`; spot from options when the stock is silent; `quotes` (read-only); the report's `unbid_leg` finding and `headline`; the position guard now refuses only collisions on the contracts the trial would trade (the operator's own QQQ 10-30 legs are left alone), working foreign orders on SPY/QQQ still refuse; the what-if "unset" sentinel; verdict C no longer requires a silent combo. 265 tests, mutation checks on every new rule (all killed).

**LEFT OPEN / PROPOSED (not built, needs the operator).** (1) A BOT change in `_close_multi_leg` (section 3): when a leg the close must SELL has no bid and is worthless (ask <= 0.05), build the closing combo without it; keep it out only if every short is in the combo; log it; test with the W33/W101 rig. (2) The same condition on ENTRY is impossible (a far wing is bought at its ask). (3) The delay allowance and the price band (above). (4) Underlying-from-options for the touch stop and floor. (5) Control not run: a QQQ all-bids trial (the incident's instrument); N1/N2 are SPY. (6) Residual positions: one worthless long call wing each from N1 (777C) and N2 (778C), both expiring 2026-10-26 16:00 ET; `status` reports not ready to restart until they expire. (7) `report`'s overall verdict is `BOT_LADDER_SUFFICIENT` with `mixed: true`; the `headline` and `unbid_leg` finding are the reading.

## 2026-10-26 - W101-D AS BUILT: a worthless unbid long wing is left out of the closing combo

**Why.** The paper probe (entries above) showed that a closing BAG holding a leg to SELL with no bid (IB bid `-1`) has no market: IB accepts it at any limit and it never fills, and the same combo without that wing fills in seconds (N2; control Q1 with every leg bid also fills). The QQQ 772C wing was `-1/0.01` on all 176 closes of 2026-10-22/23. The operator confirmed the fix: leave the wing out, it expires.

**AS BUILT (section 3: orchestrator.py, reconciler.py; approved plan).**
- `_close_multi_leg`: for credit structures, `_unbid_wings_to_leave_out` polls the legs the close would SELL (`roll_executor.poll_leg_quotes`) and leaves out a wing with bid 0 (IB `-1` or 0) and ask <= `exit.exit_unbid_wing_max_ask` (0.05). A short (a BUY-back leg) is never left out; a missing or NaN quote keeps the leg in; nothing is left out if fewer than two legs, or no buy-back leg, would remain; a settings stub without the key leaves everything as it was (`is True`). The BAG and `_synthesize_combo_cost` take the reduced list; `_defined_risk_width` and `_exit_intrinsic_floor` keep the FULL list (a three-leg condor has no width, which would have switched off the cap, the floor and the no-quote path). Logged `exit_unbid_wing_left_out`.
- Written after the CAS to CLOSING and before `place_order`, on every attempt: `exit_excluded_legs_<trade>` (how many; "0" overwrites an earlier three-leg attempt) and `residual_leg_<key>` (`{trade_id, qty, expiry}`), so the record exists before the order can fill and survives a restart.
- Reconciler: in the untracked-option branch, before the sighting debounce, exactly that key at exactly that signed quantity (expiry no more than one day past) logs `expected_residual_leg_seen` and is skipped: no sighting, no discrepancy, no `HALT_UNTRACKED`. Records are purged when the leg is gone or past the grace, only when the book is confirmed (same authority as the declared-position cleanup). Chosen over reusing `manual_positions` declarations (they add a risk row that takes a position slot, message at expiry and mislabel the leg) and over keeping closed trades' legs in `local_map` (trips the PARTIAL-legs branch and the stale-booking CAS).
- Commission true-up: `_expected_commission_rows` expects `2 * legs_n - exit_excluded_legs` rows (7, not 8, for a three-leg close; the expiry-booking branch is unchanged); the count is forgotten with the commission estimate and swept post-market. The remembered estimate over-states by one leg fill until the true-up replaces it.
- Settings `exit.exit_leave_out_unbid_wings` (true) and `exit.exit_unbid_wing_max_ask` (0.05); RUNBOOK row for the two log events.
- One bug the end-to-end test caught before merge: a trade's legs JSON carries strike `772`, the broker key is `772.0`; `residual_leg_key` normalises with `float()`.

**Tests.** `tests/test_w101d_unbid_wing.py` (40): the incident closes three legs (both shorts in, limit 2.48 as before, floor/width at 3.00 near expiry with the wing out); every keep-in case; the placement record and its order before `place_order`; the lost-CAS case writes nothing; the reconciler on a real StateManager (negative control freezes; a record stops the freeze; the orchestrator's own record read back by the reconciler; another quantity, a short, an expired record freeze; the day after expiry is covered; purge when gone, kept when the book is unconfirmed); the commission count; parity with the probe's rule. Mutation pass over 21 mutants, all killed after one test was strengthened.

**Not built / registered.** (1) Rolls still put every leg in the combo (`prepare_roll_combo`, `_validate_roll_legs` needs exactly 2 closing legs; both roll paths are off in config). (2) `shadow_referee.pnl_vs_broker` compares booked P&L with the broker's realized P&L over the three closed legs, so it differs by the wing's cost until the wing expires (at most 0.05 x 100). (3) A new entry on a contract recorded as a residual is not refused (an opposite-direction position nets to zero at the broker). (4) If the wing ever gains value before expiry it is not sold; an in-the-money expiry is exercised by IB and the stock freeze applies. (5) Underlying-from-options for the touch stop and floor; the floor-versus-IB-band extra cycle (both above). (6) The bot restart (W102) remains the operator's call; the probe residuals N1 777C and N2 778C expire 2026-10-26 16:00 ET.

## 2026-10-26 - W103 AS BUILT: a bot stop finishes inside the supervisor's wait

**Why.** Every bot stop since July ended in SIGKILL (W21/W28). In the last four stops (10-23, 10-24) `shutdown_signal_received` was the bot's last line and `orchestrator_shutting_down`, `graceful_shutdown_timed_out_cancelling` and `ait_shutdown_complete` appear zero times in any retained log. Nothing hangs: (1) the supervisor killed at 30 s while the bot's own 30 s grace (started only after its handler ran) was still running, with the shutdown step and the connection cleanup still to come; (2) `wait_for_phase` slept up to an hour without looking at the stop flag, and every observed stop was inside it; (3) the shutdown step ran only when the loop ended by itself, so the caller's cancel skipped the shutdown page and the marks snapshot; (4) the signal handler's `event.set()` may not wake an idle loop (not observed, now removed as a possibility); (5) no reap after `kill()`, so `start()` read `bot_already_running` and the bot stayed down about 2 minutes after every planned restart.

**AS BUILT (section 3 treatment: orchestrator.py, scheduler.py, main.py, master.py).**
- `MarketScheduler.wait_for_phase(target, stop_event=None)` returns the moment the event is set; the orchestrator creates `_stop_event` in `run()`, `stop()` sets it, and the three phase waits, the 30 s scan tick and the 60 s error back-off use it (`_sleep_unless_stopped`). An in-flight scan stays uninterruptible; the grace window and its cancel cover it. No scan starts after a stop.
- `run()` is now a wrapper: `_run_main()` in a `try/finally` that awaits `_shutdown_once()` (once, bounded by `BOT_SHUTDOWN_STEP_SECONDS`, errors logged not raised), so the cancel path also sends the shutdown page and takes the marks snapshot.
- `main._install_shutdown_signals`: the handler calls `loop.call_soon_threadsafe(event.set)` (wakes the selector); `signal.signal` kept for Windows. The cleanup after the loop (poller, background tasks, `ibkr.disconnect()`) is bounded by `BOT_CLEANUP_SECONDS`; `ait_shutdown_complete` now says whether it timed out.
- `BotManager.stop()` waits `SUPERVISOR_STOP_WAIT_SECONDS` (75 s), logs `bot_stop_escalated_to_kill` before any `kill()`, reaps with a 5 s wait, and `bot_stopped` carries `pid`, `exit_code` and `escalated`.
- The five numbers live in `ait/utils/cadence.py` (the existing home of timing constants that must agree; stdlib-only, so the supervisor can import it); a test requires the supervisor's wait to exceed the bot's three budgets and both sides to read the same objects. (The plan named `config/invariants.py`; that registry also drives the GUIDE table, the `config.yaml` pointer block and the W70 parity test, a larger footprint for no gain here.)
- RUNBOOK: what a clean stop looks like and which log lines mean it was not.

**Tests.** `tests/test_w103_graceful_shutdown.py` (18): a real child process with a real SIGTERM/SIGINT on an idle one-hour wait ends in under 5 s; the real `wait_for_phase` on a long wait returns when the event is set, returns at once when already set, and sleeps as before without one; the real `run()` on the smoke rig ends at once on `stop()` from the off-hours wait, the pre-market wait, the post-market wait and the error back-off, runs the shutdown step exactly once on a normal stop and on a cancel, cuts a hung step at its budget and survives a failing one; the scan tick ends on a stop with no scan after it; `BotManager.stop()` over a fake process (exits: no kill, `escalated=false`; ignores SIGTERM: logged, killed, reaped, not "already running" afterwards); the budget test. Mutation pass over 18 mutants (every wait site, the signal wake-up, the `finally`, the once-flag, the step budget, the supervisor wait, the reap, the escalation log, the `escalated` field, the shared constant), all killed after three tests were added or strengthened.

**Not done / registered.** (1) Windows (Prithvi's box): `Popen.terminate()` is `TerminateProcess`, so no Python handler runs there and there is still no graceful stop; the fix is `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` plus `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` and a `SIGBREAK` handler, which cannot be tested on this Mac. The supervisor now logs `bot_stop_escalated_to_kill`, so the box will show it. (2) `to_thread` workers wrapped in `wait_for` keep running after their timeout and `asyncio.run` waits for the default executor on exit; not seen as a cause. (3) The proof is the next planned restart: `shutdown_signal_received`, `orchestrator_shutting_down`, `ait_shutdown_complete` within seconds, the "Bot shutting down" page, and `bot_stopped escalated=false` in the supervisor log. The supervisor change (master.py) needs a SUPERVISOR restart; the bot changes need a bot restart; both are the operator's call.

## 2026-10-26 - W104 AS BUILT: silent failures on money paths become named, visible ones; the alert channel can no longer die quietly

**Why.** Two audits against HEAD `47eb0f0` re-verified the registered fail-open and alerting list. TECHNICAL_GUIDE section 2: fail closed, say so, keep managing positions, never block an exit. The book trades only iron condors, so several sites cannot reach an order today (multi-leg partial exits are refused), but each was a place where the system lacked information and said nothing; and a revoked Telegram token showed up only as an identical `alert_send_failed` warning (the operator rotates the token soon).

**AS BUILT (section 3 treatment: orchestrator, portfolio, executor, circuit_breaker, state; plus watchdog, telegram, ops_health, status, master).**
- **Watchdog.** A recovery callback that returns `False` is a failed recovery (`ensure_connected` returns False on a failed reconnect and used to be marked HEALTHY, never paged); the page failure and the caller's failure are logged (`watchdog_alert_failed`, `watchdog_check_failed`); the per-component hour is keyed on the component (the first token was always `ALERT:`, so it had been one global hour).
- **Breaker store.** `CircuitBreaker.retry_persist()`; `_check_breaker_store()` runs at the top of every trading cycle (before the tripped early-return): retry once, then `circuit_breaker_store_unhealthy` (critical) and a page at most every 30 min, `circuit_breaker_store_recovered` when it heals. W42 had built the flag and nothing read it.
- **Alert channel.** `TelegramNotifier.send` classifies failures (`auth` 401/403, `rate` 429, `transient`, `no_creds`) in `last_error_kind`; a 401/403 is not retried, writes `data/TELEGRAM_DEAD` with the reason (absolute path now; it was cwd-relative) and logs `telegram_unauthorized`. New stdlib-only `notifications/channel_state.py` keeps `data/alert_channel.json` while the channel fails (first failure time, kind, count, source); both processes write it, a successful send deletes it, `status.get_status()` / `python status.py` / the status page show "ALERTS NOT DELIVERED since ...". The supervisor `_alert` records the same, drops its cached credentials on a 401/403 (the next alert re-reads `.env`, so a rotated token works without restarting the supervisor) and raises a local macOS notification once the channel has clearly stopped delivering (auth at once, transient from the third failure, at most hourly). `_alert_gate_release` gives the throttle back when the BOT HUNG page fails to send. The file is a no-op under pytest unless a test patches its path.
- **Liveness probe.** `ops_health._default_market_open` judges a calendar fault on the host clock (`assume_market_open_on_clock`, moved to stdlib-only `utils/tz.py`; master keeps its name and its own clock) and the verdict says `calendar_fault`; `bot_liveness` used to answer `not_rth` / ok in the middle of a session.
- **Silent passes.** `assignment_risk_diag_failed` (the exit still fires); `macro_flatten_check_failed` every pass plus one page per process (stays fail-open by the W44/W51 precedent); `PartialExitsCorruptError` for an unreadable `partial_exits` (it read as `[]`, so a taken level fired again, and `null`/`{}` aborted the whole pass's exit evaluation): the check takes no partial exit, `record_partial_exit` archives the raw text to `bot_state`; an unparseable `exit_time` is booked as today's session with an error log and a page (it was retired unbooked, so the P&L never reached stats, breaker, PDT or Thompson) and `pending_exit_bookings` also selects date-less values; the "fill landed on a terminal row" flag write failure is critical and kept in memory for the drain, which now pages BEFORE deleting the flag; `losing_days_count_failed`; the MARKS MISSING and PDT BLOCKED EXIT pages latch only after a send that did not raise (MARKS MISSING also retries on every tick past the threshold, not only at the single threshold tick).

**Tests.** `tests/test_w104_failopen_and_alerting.py` (69). Mutation pass over 44 mutants (every rule above), all killed after one status test was added. The W20 harness is reused for the hang-page gate release.

**Not built / registered.** (1) Double-fire when P&L crosses two partial levels in one pass (`pnl_level` records the highest level crossed; multi-leg partials are refused, so dormant). (2) The supervisor skips its hang check when `data/bot_heartbeat` is missing during market hours. (3) `AIT_SIMULATED_CAPITAL` malformed values silently disable the governor (`runtime_env.py`, `broker/account.py`). (4) The partial-exit `cancelOrder` failure is swallowed (single-leg only). (5) Windows has no local fallback notification (Prithvi). (6) Other supervisor pages still record their throttle before the send. (7) The bot reads the Telegram token only at start; after a rotation it needs a restart. The supervisor change (master.py) needs a supervisor restart and the bot changes a bot restart, both the operator's call.

## 2026-10-27 - W105 AS BUILT: the executions ledger tells the truth; one default IB port; the digest marker uses the ET date

**Why, and what the audit corrected.** A read-only audit of `data/ait_state.db` (36 executions, newest 09-29) and the logs corrected two registered premises. (1) `exec_time` is wrong for only 5 rows (the bot's one real fill, 2026-09-28: stored 15:54:15Z, true 17:54:15Z): ib_insync converts the gateway's zone-less time with the HOST's zone, so a live fill is off by minus the host's UTC offset (2 h on the CEST box) and replayed fills are right; `record_execution` never updates `exec_time`, so the first write wins. (2) The 31 `trade_id=''` rows are not bot trades: 23 are the W53 probe (clientId 97, `W53PROBE-*` refs) and 8 are the operator's own TWS orders (clientId 0, order id 0). Also found: 11 manual fills (09-28, 09-30) never reached the table because the sweep iterated `ib.trades()` and a replayed fill with no Trade object was skipped. The operator manages by hand only what was opened by hand, so a manual fill never belongs to a bot trade.

**AS BUILT (section 3 treatment: executor, state, master; plus the read-only shadow referee).**
- **Fill time.** `_sweep_executions` stores `Fill.time` (aware UTC: arrival time for a live fill, the execution time for a replayed one), falling back to `Execution.time`.
- **Every account fill is recorded.** The ledger is written from `ib.fills()`; the `ib.trades()` loop stays for what only a Trade knows (the order's ids, its symbol, whether it was a combo), with the old precedence (the Trade's ids first) pinned by a test.
- **Who placed it.** `executions` gains `client_id`, `order_ref`, `origin` (additive ALTERs). `origin` is `bot` (attributed, or a bot order we could not attribute: the real orphan), `manual` (clientId 0), `other` (a reference that matches no trade: probes, other tools); NULL on older rows. `bot` is never downgraded; a manual/other row becomes `bot` if a later pass attributes it.
- **Attribution that survives a restart.** `_ledger_context` falls back to `orderRef` when the in-memory maps (empty after a restart) know nothing: a reference that IS a known trade attributes the fill; a roll reference books to the closing trade, as the in-memory path does. Manual, probe and unknown references match nothing.
- **Readers.** `shadow_referee.py` `orphan_fills` ignores `manual`/`other` rows (it broke on every manual and probe fill; it still breaks on a `bot` orphan and on a legacy row). The weekly scorecard's executions line splits `$X commissions (bot) + $Y manual/other` (it summed everything: $20.18 where $2.50 was the bot's). `go_live.py` and `fill_vs_model_report.py` are unchanged (they already treat a trade-less row as outside the gate sample).
- **Backfill.** `scripts/restate_w105_executions.py` (dry run read-only; `--apply` snapshots to `data/backups/`, adds the columns if missing, tags the 31 rows and fixes the 5 times; refuses unless the database matches the audit; never deletes or attributes). Its dry run against the live database listed exactly those 36 changes. NOT applied: the operator runs it with the bot stopped.
- **IB port.** `master._configured_ib_port` defaults to the bot's own `IBKREnvConfig.ibkr_port` (7497), read lazily, instead of a second literal (4002). With `.env` loaded (the normal launch) nothing changes; with no `IBKR_PORT` the supervisor and the bot no longer watch different endpoints.
- **Digest marker.** `digest_sent_*` and the digest's trade-count date use `now_et()`, as the catch-up check does (the host date from 19:00 ET would have stamped tomorrow).
- **Housekeeping.** `test_w28_et_date_authority::test_today_et_never_returns_the_bare_host_date_in_the_window` assumed a 6 h Berlin/ET gap; between the EU and US clock changes (10-25 to 11-01) it is 5 h and the test failed on any full lane run 23:00-00:00 CET (18:00-19:00 ET). It now skips until the host date has rolled over. Not a code bug.

**Tests.** `tests/test_w105_ledger_and_defaults.py` (41); the r16/r19 sweep rigs now provide `ib.fills()`; two r16_ops tests follow the new defaults. Mutation pass over 26 mutants: all killed after two tests were added; one (`origin` upgrade clause) is equivalent (the next WHEN gives the same result).

**Not built / registered.** (1) An empty `IBKR_PORT=` makes the bot's pydantic parse fail (not run; a `.env`/launch change). (2) The 11 old manual fills are not inserted from the logs. (3) No end-of-day re-stamp of `trades.commission` (the W48 deferred true-up covers late reports). (4) `T-20260928-195224-adfe01` is still `filled` in the database past its expiry; W101-C books it at the next start. (5) The other 4002 literals (IBC `OverrideTwsApiPort`, the backfill scripts' `--port`, docs) are Gateway-specific or the operator's. The bot changes need a bot restart, `master.py` a supervisor restart, both the operator's call; run the restatement script after the deploy, with the bot stopped.

## 2026-10-27 - W108 AS PLANNED: one lot-sizing rule for live and research; per-trade risk back to 5% of capital (W100's 20% reversed); branch `w108-lot-sizing-parity`

**Why.** A read-only investigation of how the condor builder fixes a trade's structure (operator question, 2026-10-26/27) found: (1) the wing is `min(free width, budget/90)`, snapped to the nearest listed strike (`iron_condor.py` `_vol_scaled_width`); the free width is `wing_k x price x IV x sqrt(DTE/365)`, about $21-$59 on SPY/QQQ/IWM at the shipped `wing_k` 1.6, so the budget ceiling decided every condor built so far (`adfe01`: $300 budget, 3-wide) and decides every condor at a $1,000 budget (11-wide, max loss about $750-$900). W100's "wing_k is no longer inert" holds only for `wing_k` below about 0.3 (QQQ) to 0.85 (IWM); the optimizer's drop rule tests only k=0.30. (2) The 20% of W100 rested on a misunderstanding of what the budget does (it is a ceiling that fills itself through the wing width, not a loss the structure may reach): the operator reverses it to 5%. (3) Live and research size lots with different code. Live: `PositionSizer` (scalers x 0.4 condor factor, `max(1, ...)`, an `account_scale_cap = max(1, int(NLV/10_000))` literal that never binds) and then `min(request.contracts, sizer)` where every builder requests 1 lot, so live can never place more than 1 lot whatever `max_contracts_per_trade` says. Research: `int(capital x pct / risk)` inline in each builder, a "1 lot if it costs <= 25% of capital" fallback, and the pool re-sizing; no scalers, no scale cap. Raising `max_contracts_per_trade` would therefore give multi-lot results in research that live cannot reproduce. (4) `PositionSizer.max_contracts_for_budget` is dead code.

**Operator decisions (2026-10-27).**
- D1: lot rule = budget only. Option A: the UNSCALED budget decides viability (one lot's max loss above `risk.max_position_risk_pct x NLV` is refused; zero lots = rejected), scalers only throttle the count above 1 lot (`max(1, floor(budget x scaler / risk))`). Option B (the scaled budget handed to the builder) is rejected: at 5-10% it builds nothing (W64: $66/$150 budgets build nothing). Scalers stay OFF for every strategy: new `position_sizing.scaled_strategies: []`; a strategy named in the list gets the existing confidence / vol / IV-rank / drawdown / VIX curves, others are budget-only.
- D2: retire `positions.max_position_pct` and `backtest.position_size_pct`; `risk.max_position_risk_pct` is the one budget number.
- D3: zero lots = rejected (no floor to 1, no 25% fallback).
- D4: the research pool also models gate 6c (per-symbol concentration), the per-expiry cap and the correlation cluster cap.
- Per-trade risk 5% ($250 at the $5k account: a 3-wide condor, max loss about $200-$210); `risk.max_daily_loss_pct` back to about 0.045; `max_contracts_per_trade` stays 1; `positions.max_portfolio_risk_pct` and `risk.max_symbol_concentration_pct` stay 0.20.

**AS PLANNED (phase 1; no live behaviour change at 1 lot).** (a) A pure lot function shared by `PositionSizer`, every research builder and the pool; delete `account_scale_cap` and `max_contracts_for_budget`. (b) Retire the three settings above (and `backtest.spread_tuning.max_cost_fraction_of_capital`, whose only use is the 25% fallback) with their validators, tests, generated docs and the literal-census entries. (c) Pool: gate 6c, per-expiry and cluster cap from the live helpers and config. (d) `gate_parity.py` rows for the new pool rejections and for what still differs. (e) `tests/test_lot_sizing_parity.py`: the same trades through the live path, the engine builders and the pool for the condor, both debit spreads and both credit spreads; mutation pass over the shared function and the pool gates. (f) The W100-pinned tests return to 5%. Section 3: `risk/position_sizer.py` (operator confirmed the diff may be made); `risk/manager.py` only if its call changes.

**Not in phase 1 (registered).** Phase 2, live multi-lot: builders request the lot count (today's `min(request, sizer)` caps it at 1), skip multi-leg profit scale-out (`_execute_partial_exit` refuses it and `_check_partial_exit` re-fires every cycle with more than 1 lot), multi-lot cases for the W101-B exit pricing and the W101-C expiry booking (neither has one), and a staged paper ramp (2 then 3 lots: full fill, partial fill, exit, expiry); nothing live has ever traded more than 1 lot (22 of 22 trades). Phase 3, scalers: condor confidence in research derived from `backtest.gates_mode` (observe: `ml.observe_mode_neutral_confidence` 0.60, which live applies at `orchestrator.py` 2720-2731 and the engine never reads; enforce: the range probability after the fractal delta); a research "recent losing days" input; directional scalers only after the multi-timeframe analyzer is ported into the engine (intraday coverage to be checked first). Phase 4: budget-fitted widths for spreads; live builders for `put_credit_spread` / `call_credit_spread` (research-only today); no calendar-spread builder exists in live (retired) or research. Separate: a carried-equity walk-forward path (each window restarts at `account.capital`; `total_return` compounds while `max_drawdown` / `equity_curve` add dollars). Narrow-wing and multi-lot studies need `wing_k` below the optimizer's 0.30 floor (the schema minimum is 0.1; 2-wide credits measured at W64 sit under the $0.70 floor).

Design agreed in principle: keep the per-window reset as the basis for parameter selection, add an opt-in carried path reported as an estimate (the parameters were tuned at the fresh budget), make the reported figures use one method, windows' OOS replay becomes sequential. (S2) The narrow-wing study: widen the optimizer's `wing_k` lower bound below 0.30 (schema minimum 0.1) and tighten `_maybe_drop_inert_params`, which drops `wing_k` only when the cap binds at `k_min` (at the shipped values `wing_k` above about 0.3 on QQQ gives identical structures); budget-only arm first. Real 2-wide credits measured at W64 ($0.62-0.68) sit under the $0.70 floor, so 3-wide is the realistic narrowest.

**Open decisions for the operator.** The per-trade percentage once phase 2 is in view (5% gives 1 lot; 10% gives a 6-wide at about $400 per lot); whether the condor's 0.4 strategy factor should stay if scalers are ever turned on; whether research should keep `gates_mode: enforce` for the parity studies.

## 2026-10-28 - W109 AS PLANNED (pre-registration, written BEFORE the script exists or any run): the narrow-wing and multi-lot study; branch `w109-narrow-wing-study`

**Question (operator, 2026-10-27).** At the $5k account, does a NARROWER condor wing and/or MORE THAN ONE LOT beat the shipped configuration (5% per trade, `wing_k` 1.6 -> a 3-wide via the budget ceiling, 1 lot)? The answer decides whether Phase 2 (live multi-lot: builders requesting lots, multi-leg scale-out skip, multi-lot cases for W101-B / W101-C, a staged paper ramp, section-3 files) is worth building. At 5% a 3-wide risks about $200 against a $250 budget, so live is 1 lot whatever the rules say; multi-lot appears only at a higher per-trade percentage with narrow wings.
**Harness (fixed).** `scripts/narrow_wing_study.py`, modelled on `scripts/wing_budget_study.py`; reuses `SYMBOLS`, `load_data`, `lower_priority`, `metrics` from `scripts/post_event_study.py`. SPY / QQQ / IWM, iron_condor only, `train_window_models=False`, walk-forward train 126 / test 63 / step 63 / gap 5, stored-IBKR-IV store (`data/historical.db`, 1052 rows per symbol 2022-08-01..2026-10-08), `initial_capital` = `account.capital` ($5,000, one shared pool, the W108 pool gates on), `entry_dte` 18 (the live median) and 25 (robustness). `use_research_config()` first (calibrated `friction_model: per_leg_usd`, IV-rank gate, `condor_any_direction false`), then `gates_mode="observe"` explicitly (live runs observe; the overlay's `enforce` with no trained models would reject every entry): the one deliberate deviation. `position_size_pct`, `wing_k`, `max_contracts_per_trade` are set per variant. Scalers are not a variable (off, the shared rule `lots_for_budget`).
**Variants (budget %, wing_k, max lots).** `base` 5, 1.6, 1 = BASELINE (the shipped config); `sanity_default` = `base` with `wing_k=None` (config default) and must reproduce `base` exactly (n, net, PF, max DD) else the study is VOID. 5%: `b5_k015_1`, `b5_k010_1`, `b5_k010_3`. 10%: `b10_k160_1`, `b10_k030_1`, `b10_k015_1`, `b10_k010_1`, `b10_k015_3`, `b10_k010_3`. Reference only, never a candidate: `ref20_k160_1` (the W100 regime, an 11-wide). 12 variants x 2 DTE.
**Wiring checks (any failure = VOID, never a quiet result).** The per-leg friction model is actually fitted (engine `_friction_stats`); `b5_k010_*` mean wing < `base` mean wing; `b10_k160_1` mean wing > `base`; every 3-lot variant takes more than 1 lot in at least one trade (else flagged "multi-lot never triggered"); pairs of variants with identical results are flagged as unwired knobs.
**Decision rule (fixed; not edited after any result).** Per DTE, against `base`, a candidate is WORTH PURSUING only if at BOTH DTE levels: (1) n >= 30 and n >= 0.85 x base n; (2) PF >= base PF + 0.10 and net per position-day >= base; (3) max drawdown <= 8% of the pool (the go-live gate) and <= 1.25 x base's; (4) in >= 60% of the walk-forward windows that traded, its window net >= base's, AND the point estimate of the net difference from a block bootstrap (windows resampled, 80% interval reported) is positive; (5) friction share (entry + exit costs / gross credit) <= base + 10 points; (6) a survivor repeats at `friction_stress_multiplier` 2.0 (a second run, survivors only) and still passes (1)-(3). A multi-lot candidate is WORTH PHASE 2 only if it passes the above AND beats its own 1-lot twin (same budget, same `wing_k`) on net with max DD <= 1.25 x the twin's AND takes more than 1 lot in >= 25% of its trades. Verdicts: PHASE 2 JUSTIFIED / NARROW-ONLY (a narrower `wing_k` or a higher budget at 1 lot beats `base`; no Phase 2) / NOTHING BEATS BASELINE (keep 5%, 1.6, 1 lot) / VOID.
**Limits stated in advance.** About 55-70 trades per variant over four years and about 14 windows: only large effects are visible, and "no difference" is the likely outcome (it is a valid answer, not a failure). Prices are Black-Scholes plus skew from stored daily IV (half the days carry stored IV), not real quotes. W64 measured real 2-wide credits of $0.62-$0.68, under the $0.70 floor, while the model gives $0.72-$0.77, so 2-wide arms are biased favourably (the stress repeat bounds it). The absolute level is not trusted (an earlier harness run put the shipped ruleset at PF 0.18 under the legacy cost model against the live book's 2.2); read relative effects only. A result licenses a Phase 2 plan-mode pass or a config proposal to the operator, never a live change.

## 2026-10-28 - W109 RESULTS: verdict VOID (a pre-registered wiring check failed); exploratory reading attached; branch `w109-narrow-wing-study`, not committed

**Run.** `scripts/narrow_wing_study.py` (sha256 `d379c8c4...7839`, unchanged between the pre-registration entry, the smoke run and the full run; 44 unit tests, 13-mutant pass over the rule all killed), both entry DTEs (18, 25), 12 variants each, SPY / QQQ / IWM, 1051 daily rows each (2022-08..2026-10), per-leg friction fitted for all three symbols (`calibrated_on` 2026-10-09), `gates_mode` observe, $5,000 pool, the W108 pool gates on. Output: `reports/narrow_wing_study/results.{json,md}` (git-ignored). `sanity_default` reproduced `base` exactly at both DTE.
**Pre-registered verdict: VOID.** Wiring check "a `b5_k010_*` variant is narrower than `base`" failed at both DTE: mean wing 3.0 = base 3.0. The knob IS wired (`b5_k010_1` took 13 trades against `base` 104 at DTE 18, 28 against 88 at DTE 25), but the expectation written into the rule was wrong: at 5% the ceiling is $2.78 so `base` already builds a 3-wide, and at `wing_k` 0.10 the free width is below the $2 floor on most entries; a 2-wide cannot clear the $0.70 credit floor (W64 measured $0.62-$0.68), so those entries are REFUSED and only the days on which a 3-wide fits remain. Narrower than 3-wide is not buildable at this credit floor, in the model as on the real chains. Per the rule the verdict stays VOID; no criterion of the rule was evaluated for a candidate and the stress repeat did not run (no survivors). Flags raised as designed: `b5_k010_3` never took a second lot (max 1) and equals `b5_k010_1` exactly at both DTE; at 5% a 3-wide risks about $215 of a $250 budget, so multi-lot cannot trigger.
**Exploratory reading (post-hoc, NOT the verdict; labelled so because the rule was never run on it).** DTE 18 / DTE 25, n, PF, net $, max DD % of the pool:
- `base` (5%, 3-wide): 104 / 88 trades, PF 0.41 / 0.34, net -1,485 / -1,508, DD 33.6 / 32.6%.
- `b10_k160_1` (10%, 6-wide): PF 0.73 / 0.69, net -848 / -939. `ref20_k160_1` (20%, 11-wide, the W100 regime): 61 / 51 trades, PF 1.61 / 1.11, net +1,186 / +222, DD 11.7 / 13.8%. The ordering by budget is monotone in the model: the wider ceiling-built condor did better. Friction share (entry crossing + commissions over gross credit) falls from 14-15% at 3-wide to 5% at 11-wide.
- Narrower k at 10% (`b10_k015_1`, `b10_k010_1`): PF 0.68 / 0.59 and 0.61 / 0.89 on 66 / 65 and 13 / 28 trades; no variant with fewer trades is comparable on pace (the rule's n >= 0.85 x base criterion would have failed all of them).
- Multi-lot against its own 1-lot twin, same budget and `wing_k` (the Phase 2 question), worse in every pair at both DTE: `b10_k015_3` net -961 / -1,359 against `b10_k015_1` -418 / -664 and DD 28.5 / 35.5% against 15.0 / 20.1%; `b10_k010_3` -193 / -106 against -122 / -55. Lots multiply the loss on the touch stops (about 36% of exits) and the 20% aggregate cap then blocks concurrent entries.
**What this licenses.** Nothing for Phase 2: there is no evidence that multi-lot or narrower-than-3-wide condors help, and the descriptive twin comparison points the other way; at the shipped 5% / $5k multi-lot cannot trigger at all. It does NOT license a config change. It does surface a question the pre-registration did not ask: in this model the 5% / 3-wide configuration is the WORST of the budgets tried (PF 0.34-0.41, a 33% drawdown of the pool) and the 20% / 11-wide regime the best. W108's return to 5% rested on a risk argument (an 11-wide risks $750-$900 of $5k), not on return evidence. The level is not trusted (Black-Scholes + skew from stored daily IV, half the days; the same harness under the legacy cost model put the ruleset at PF 0.18, the live book's 22 closes are PF 2.2), and 50-100 trades per variant leave only large effects visible, so this is a reason to ask the question properly, not an answer.
**For the operator.** Options: (A) accept VOID and stop (no Phase 2; per-trade percentage unchanged); (B) a new pre-registered study W109b on the question the data raises: the per-trade budget ladder (5% / 7.5% / 10% / 15% / 20% at `wing_k` 1.6, 1 lot, both DTE, a stressed-friction repeat, a corrected wiring expectation: "a budget variant's mean wing is wider than `base`'s" and "n differs from `base`" for the credit-floor case), fixed in PLAN.md before it runs. Option B is about 30 minutes of compute. Any live change is the operator's call and a new sample epoch.

**CORRECTION to the W109 RESULTS entry above (same day).** (1) The mutation pass listed 13 mutants of which one was a no-op pattern: 12 real mutants, all killed (two survivors on the first pass, "stress rows absent counts as a pass" and "a tie with the one-lot twin is a win", each now has a test). (2) The sentence "the 20% aggregate cap then blocks concurrent entries" is NOT supported: every multi-lot variant took exactly as many trades as its one-lot twin (`b10_k015_3` 66 = `b10_k015_1` 66, `b10_k010_3` 13 = 13 at DTE 18; 65 = 65 and 28 = 28 at DTE 25), so no entry was blocked. The small trade count of `k` 0.10 (13 / 28) is the $0.70 credit floor refusing the 2-wide entries, in the one-lot variant too. The multi-lot loss is the same entries taken at 1.6-1.9 lots on average; why it loses more per trade than the one-lot twin was not examined beyond the touch-stop share (37 of 104 exits in `base`).

## 2026-10-28 - W109b AS PLANNED (pre-registration, written BEFORE the script exists or any run): the per-trade budget ladder; branch `w109b-budget-ladder` (off `w109-narrow-wing-study`, `0bca1b6`)

**Question.** W109 came back VOID (its wiring expectation was wrong: a 2-wide cannot clear the $0.70 credit floor, so `wing_k` 0.10 cannot build narrower than the 3-wide `base`), but its exploratory reading raised the question the choice of the per-trade percentage hinges on: in the model the shipped 5% / 3-wide setup was the worst budget tried and the 20% / 11-wide regime the best. The ladder table is then the deliverable: it shows what the cap costs and gives the operator the evidence to revisit the cap deliberately. A "no" is a valid verdict.
**Harness (fixed; identical to W109).** `scripts/budget_ladder_study.py`, importing `Variant`, `trade_stats`, `window_nets`, `paired_window_stats`, `dd_pct`, `build_config`, `friction_preflight`, `STRESS_MULTIPLIER` from the committed `scripts/narrow_wing_study.py` (not edited). Variants (budget, `wing_k`, lots 1): `base` 5%, 1.6 (BASELINE); `sanity_default` (`wing_k=None`, must reproduce `base`); candidates `b075` 7.5%, `b10` 10%; above the cap, reported only: `b15` 15%, `b20` 20%; reference only: `ref20_k055` (20%, `wing_k` 0.55, a 7-8-wide, to separate a higher budget from a wider wing). 7 variants x 2 DTE.
**Decision rule (fixed; not edited after any result).** Candidates are `b075` and `b10`. Per DTE, against `base`, a candidate is SUPPORTED only if at BOTH DTE: (1) n >= 30 and n >= 0.85 x base n; (2) PF >= base PF + 0.10 and net per position-day >= base; (3) max drawdown <= 15% of the pool and <= 1.25 x base's, and the largest single-trade structural loss <= 10% of the pool; (4) >= 60% of traded windows with window net >= base's AND a positive point estimate of the block-bootstrapped net difference (80% interval reported); (5) friction share <= base + 10 points (entry crossing + round-trip commissions over gross credit; the exit crossing is not separable); (6) ABSOLUTE: net > 0 and PF >= 1.0 (a configuration that loses money in the model is never supported, even if it beats a worse base); (7) a survivor repeats at `friction_stress_multiplier` 2.0 (`base` rerun at 2.0 too) and still passes 1-3 and 6. Dose-response label over the whole ladder 5% -> 20%: PF non-decreasing in >= 3 of the 4 adjacent pairs at each DTE; a candidate passing 1-7 while the ladder is not monotone is SINGLE-POINT (exploratory), not supported. Verdicts: BUDGET RAISE SUPPORTED to `<level>` (the supported candidate with the highest net per position-day; ties to the lower budget) / SINGLE-POINT / NO BUDGET WITHIN THE CAP BEATS 5% (keep 5%) / VOID. Above-cap and reference rows are printed in the same table, marked "outside the operator's cap: informational".
**Wiring checks (corrected from W109).** VOID if: the per-leg friction model is missing for a symbol; `sanity_default` differs from `base`; mean wing is not non-decreasing along the ladder with `b20` strictly wider than `base`; mean max loss is not non-decreasing along the ladder. FLAGGED (reported, not void): identical results between two rungs (inert), runs that errored.
**Limits (as W109).** Black-Scholes + skew from stored daily IV (half the days), not quotes; about 50-100 trades per variant and 14-22 windows, so only large effects are visible; the absolute level is not trusted (an earlier run of the harness under the legacy cost model put the shipped rules at PF 0.18, the live book's 22 closes are PF 2.2); read relative effects only. A result licenses a config PROPOSAL to the operator (and a new sample epoch if accepted), never a live change.

## 2026-10-28 - W109b RESULTS: NO BUDGET WITHIN THE CAP BEATS 5% (as pre-registered); the ladder is monotone and only the rungs above the 10% cap are profitable in the model; branch `w109b-budget-ladder`, not committed

**Run.** `scripts/budget_ladder_study.py` (sha256 `ab5bbabf...a255`, unchanged from the smoke run through the full run; 42 unit tests; 20-mutant pass over the rule, all applicable mutants killed after two gaps were closed), both entry DTEs (18, 25), 7 variants each, the W109 harness (SPY / QQQ / IWM, stored-IV store, per-leg friction fitted, $5,000 pool, W108 pool gates, `gates_mode` observe, 1 lot). `sanity_default` reproduced `base` exactly at both DTE; every wiring check passed (mean wing 3.0 -> 4.0 -> 5.8 -> 8.1 -> 11.1 along the ladder, mean max loss rising with it). No candidate survived criteria 1-6, so the stressed repeat did not run. Output: `reports/narrow_wing_study`'s sibling `reports/budget_ladder_study/results.{json,md}` (git-ignored).
**Verdict (rule applied as written).** `b075` (7.5%) fails criteria 2, 3, 4 and 6; `b10` (10%) passes 1, 2, 4 and 5 but fails 3 (drawdown 31.7% / 30.6% of the pool against the 15% ceiling) and 6 (it loses money: net -$848 / -$939, PF 0.73 / 0.69). Dose-response: PF is non-decreasing in 4 of 4 adjacent pairs at both DTE.
**The ladder (DTE 18 / DTE 25), PF, net $, drawdown % of the pool, trades, largest single-trade structural loss.**
- 5% `base` (3-wide): 0.41 / 0.34, -1,485 / -1,508, 33.6 / 32.6%, 104 / 88, $230 / $233.
- 7.5% (4-wide): 0.49 / 0.49, -1,435 / -1,312, 34.8 / 31.4%, 104 / 89.
- 10% (5.8-wide): 0.73 / 0.69, -848 / -939, 31.7 / 30.6%, 104 / 89, $483 / $480. (last rung inside the operator's cap)
- 15% (8-wide, above the cap): 1.30 / 0.84, +521 / -294, 10.4 / 15.2%, 61 / 51, $680 / $716.
- 20% (11-wide, above the cap): 1.61 / 1.11, +1,186 / +222, 11.7 / 13.8%, 61 / 51, $946 / $932.
- reference 20% at `wing_k` 0.55 (about 8-wide): 1.10 / 1.01, +216 / +27, 17.3 / 14.7%, 74 / 55, $900 / $897.
Friction share (entry crossing + round-trip commissions over gross credit) falls from 14.4% / 15.3% at 3-wide to 5.1% / 5.0% at 11-wide; mean credit rises from $0.86 to $2.43.
**What this shows, and what it does not.** In this model, with a $5,000 pool, a 3-wide condor's fixed per-lot costs are a large share of its credit and the touch stops take a large share of the rest: the shipped 5% setup and everything up to 10% lose money, and the profit appears only at 15-20% (profitable at both DTE only at 20%, and then marginally at DTE 25). The width, not only the budget, carries the effect: at the same 20% budget an 8-wide (reference) is much worse than the 11-wide (PF 1.10 / 1.01 against 1.61 / 1.11). The operator's 10% per-trade cap therefore excludes every profitable configuration of this ladder; the rule's verdict follows from that cap and is not a finding that 5% is good. It does NOT show that 20% is safe or profitable live: 51-61 trades per rung, modelled prices (Black-Scholes + skew from stored daily IV, half the days), an absolute level the harness does not support (the same harness under the legacy cost model put the shipped ruleset at PF 0.18; the live book's 22 closes are PF 2.2), and a 20% rung that risks up to $946 (19% of the pool) in one trade.
**For the operator.** (A) Keep 5% / 10% cap: nothing in the model is profitable inside it. (B) Check the model before deciding anything: `scripts/parity_replay.py` (W72) compares modelled entry credit and exit value with the real fills (the manual trades and the bot's own); if the model overstates 3-wide credits or friction the whole table moves. (C) Revisit the cap deliberately, with this table: a new pre-registered study (W109c) at a cap you choose (15% or 20%), with the dose-response and stress criteria unchanged. (D) Treat the account size as the binding constraint: at $5k the fixed costs of a narrow condor are the problem; the ladder is the cost of that. Any live change is the operator's call and a new sample epoch.

**CORRECTION to the W109b RESULTS entry above (same day).** The mutation pass listed 20 mutants of which one pattern did not match the code: 19 real mutants, all killed (two survivors on the first pass, "the stressed repeat has no rows and still counts as a pass" and "profit factor >= 1.0 dropped from criterion 6", each now has a test).
