## 2026-10-28 - W110 AS PLANNED (pre-registration, written BEFORE the paper restart): the paper checkpoint that tests the W109 / W109b model against real fills; plus one omitted limit of those studies

**Omitted limit (CORRECTION to the W109 and W109b limits).** 20-25% of the model's trades in every variant (`backtest_end`: 22.1% / 25.0% in `base` at DTE 18 / 25, 19.6-24.7% across the ladder) are positions force-closed at the end of a walk-forward test window, at the model's mark with exit friction; live has no such exit. The share is nearly the same in every variant, so it does not explain the ladder's trend, but it does bear on the absolute levels (PF 0.34-0.41 for `base`) that the studies already declare untrusted. Comparisons with live below therefore use the non-forced exits.
**Why this checkpoint.** W109b found nothing profitable inside the operator's 10% per-trade cap in the model; whether that holds in reality is unobserved (the one real 3-wide condor, `adfe01`, expired unresolved; the earlier parity replay had 2 structures in the 15-45 DTE band). The paper account is the test, at no financial risk. The operator starts the bot on 2026-10-29 before the open. This entry fixes what will be compared, and the decision classes, before any paper result exists.
**Epoch.** Starts at the bot's first scan after that restart with the shipped W108 configuration (`risk.max_position_risk_pct` 0.05 = $250, breaker 0.045, 1 lot, scalers off, SPY / QQQ / IWM, `options.dte_range` [14, 30], ML gates in observe). A config change inside the epoch starts a new epoch (house rule) except a recorded safety fix. Counted: iron_condor trades entered at or after the epoch start whose close is a real close by `ait.reporting.go_live` (`is_real_close` / `real_close_count`, rolled chains folded as the scorecard does), read from `data/ait_state.db` opened read-only. `adfe01` (entered 2026-09-28) is outside the epoch.
**Model figures to compare with** (W109b `base`, DTE 18 / DTE 25; the studies' limits apply): win rate 39.4% / 37.5%; PF 0.41 / 0.34; mean credit $0.855 / $0.838 on a mean 3.0 wing (credit / width 0.28); mean max loss $215; mean hold 8.5 / 11.2 days; friction share (entry crossing + round-trip commissions over gross credit) 14.4% / 15.3%; among the NON-forced exits: touch stop 45.7% / 51.5%, take profit 49.4% / 43.9%, expiry approach 4.9% / 4.5%. The mapping of live `exit_reason_detailed` values to touch stop / take profit / expiry is fixed when the comparison script is written, before the first checkpoint, and recorded in the script's docstring.
**Checkpoints.** C1, a data-capture audit with NO decision, at 10 real closes or 12 weeks from the epoch start, whichever comes first: every field the comparison needs is recorded, the metrics are reported descriptively. C2, the decision, at 25 real closes or 26 weeks (2027-04-29), whichever comes first; if fewer than 15 real closes exist then, it is extended until 15 closes or 52 weeks; if still fewer than 15 the result is PACE-LIMITED (reported with the fill statistics; the cause, not the model, is then the question). At every checkpoint also report entries placed / filled / cancelled, closes per week against the go-live pace target (3-4 per week; the model itself produced about 2.4 trades a month, and September's live record was 1 filled entry of 12), the median entry slip against the credit (go-live gate 8%), and an 80% bootstrap interval of the PF over the closes.
**Decision classes at C2 (n >= 15 real closes).** (a) MODEL TOO PESSIMISTIC AT 3-WIDE: real net > 0 and real PF >= 1.0 -> the model is rejected for this regime, 5% stays, the W109b table is not a basis for raising the cap. (b) MODEL CONSISTENT: real net < 0 and real PF <= 0.6 (the model's 0.34-0.41 plus slack for a PF measured on about 25 trades) -> the 3-wide setup does not pay at $5k in reality either; the operator chooses between a new pre-registered study at a per-trade cap he sets (W109c) and treating the account size as the binding constraint; paper trading may continue, it costs nothing. (c) INDETERMINATE: otherwise (or n < 15) -> continue to 50 closes, the go-live preliminary read. PF 1.0 is break-even; 0.6 is a judgement, stated as such.
**What this does not change.** None of the go-live gates (50 preliminary / 100 before funding closes, PF >= 1.3, drawdown <= 8% of deployed risk, entry slip <= 8%, the pace line) is relaxed or replaced; this is a model-validation read on the same data. The comparison is a read-only script `scripts/paper_checkpoint.py` to be written, tested (its model figures equal this entry's, as the W109 / W109b tests do) and pre-registered-as-built before C1; nothing in `src/` changes.

**CORRECTION to the W110 entry above (same day).** The forced window-end share across the ladder rows runs 19.6% to 25.0% (the maximum is `base` at DTE 25), not 19.6-24.7%.

**AS BUILT.** `scripts/paper_checkpoint.py [--checkpoint C1|C2] [--epoch-start 2026-10-29] [--now ISO] [--db] [--out]`: opens `data/ait_state.db` with `file:...?mode=ro`; population = iron_condor closes under `ait.reporting.go_live` (`not_real_close_sql`, `fold_roll_chains`) whose origin was entered at or after the epoch start; reports pace and fills first (entries placed / filled / cancelled / rejected / pending, fill rate, the pre-epoch record for context, closes per week against the 3-4 target, median entry slip against the 8% gate), then real against model (win rate, net, PF with an 80% bootstrap interval, avg win / loss, credit, wing, credit / width, capital at risk, hold, friction share, touch / take-profit / expiry shares of the exits), then the C1 data-capture audit (missing fields and unmapped exit reasons, listed verbatim) or the C2 decision class. Exit mapping: `short_strike_touch*` -> touch stop, `take_profit*` -> take profit, `expiry_approaching*` -> expiry approach, anything containing `expired` -> expiry settled, everything else -> other. Schedule and decision classes exactly as the W110 entry (C1 at 10 closes or 12 weeks, i.e. by 2027-01-21; C2 at 25 closes or 26 weeks, i.e. 2027-04-29, extended to 15 closes or 52 weeks, PACE-LIMITED below 15; net > 0 and PF >= 1.0 / net < 0 and PF <= 0.6 / otherwise INDETERMINATE). Report goes to stdout and `reports/paper_checkpoint/<date>_<C1|C2>.md`. Catalogue entry added; docs regenerated; stamp retaken.
**DEVIATION from the plan.** The script does not print the weekly scorecard's lines: `compute_go_live_verdict` opens the database with a plain `sqlite3.connect` (read-write), which would break the script's read-only guarantee; the scorecard remains the whole-DB reference and the script uses the same population functions.
**VERIFIED.** `tests/test_paper_checkpoint.py` (50 tests, a tmp database built with the real `StateManager` schema): column contract, read-only connection (a write is refused; a full run leaves the file byte-identical), epoch filter (`adfe01` excluded), non-real closes and other strategies excluded, rolled chains folded, population equal to `real_close_count`, the live exit-reason strings, metrics on fixed numbers, bootstrap reproducible, fill / slip / pace, every schedule and decision boundary, the model figures equal to the W110 text of this file. Mutation pass, 17 mutants, all killed (one gap closed first: the strategy filter in `epoch_closes`). Real runs against the current database, read-only: `--epoch-start 2026-10-29` -> 0 epoch closes, "C1: NOT DUE", pre-epoch record placed 16 / filled 5 / cancelled 11; `--epoch-start 2026-04-01` -> the 4 April closes, 16 entries placed, fill rate 31.2%, median slip 9.2% over 1 fill, and the C1 audit flags exactly what is missing on those legacy rows (capital at risk, exit reason, entry live mid), which is what the audit is for. No `src/` change; `gen_docs.py --check` clean.
**A defect in my mutation harness, found here and re-checked.** The harness rewrote a file with a mutant, ran the tests and restored the file; Python caches bytecode keyed by the source's modification second and size, and the mutant `mode=rw` has the same size as `mode=ro`, so a restored file could run the mutant's stale bytecode (it made one test fail spuriously, and it could in principle make a later mutant look killed by an earlier one). Fixed (`python -B` and the bytecode of the mutated module deleted around every run). All earlier passes were re-run with the fix and give the same results: W108 14 applicable mutants all killed, W109 12, W109b 19 (the 'killed' claims in those entries stand).
**Not done.** Not merged to `main` (the operator's say-so). The bot restart and the epoch are the operator's.

## 2026-10-28 - W111 AS PLANNED (Phase 2a): the live lot-request path, built so that `positions.max_contracts_per_trade: 1` keeps live behaviour identical; branch `w111-lot-request` in a separate worktree (`trade_v2_dev`), merged only on the operator's say-so

**Operator decisions (2026-10-28).** Proceed with Phases 2, 3 and 4 in the order 2a -> 2b -> 3 -> 4; the W109 / W109b studies do not gate them (their results depend on configuration values someone chose, e.g. the $0.70 credit floor; the research mode exists so the operator can study those); live stays at one lot through `positions.max_contracts_per_trade: 1`; each phase has its own plan-mode pass, branch and entries. The paper bot may be running during this work, so every edit is made in the worktree and never in the checkout the bot runs from.
**Gap closed by 2a ("condition 3").** Live can never place more than one lot: the builder emits `quantity=1`, `TradeRequest.contracts` is that 1 and `validate_trade` returns `min(request.contracts, sizer)` (`risk/manager.py`). The W108 rule and the sizer already return counts above 1 when the cap allows; nothing asks for them. A larger count must not simply flow through: the dollar gates (buying power, 6b per-trade, 6b-2 aggregate, 6c per-symbol) compare `request.max_loss` for the REQUESTED count and run before sizing, so they must see the TOTAL risk of the lots actually placed.
**Design.** (1) `TradeRequest.scale_to_budget: bool = False` (default = today's semantics for every caller); when True, `max_loss` is per lot and `contracts` is the minimum. (2) `RiskManager.validate_trade`: steps 6 / 6b / 6b-2 / 6c move into one helper `_dollar_gates(...)` with the same arithmetic and rejection texts; a non-scaling request calls it once exactly as today; a scaling request gets the sizer's lot count first (the same `calculate` call, hoisted), the correlation haircut, then a FIT: the largest N from the target down to 1 whose dollar gates all pass, rejecting with the N = 1 gate's own text if none does; `position_size` = N, `max_risk` = N x per-lot. (3) `orchestrator._try_execute` builds the request with `scale_to_budget=True` and re-validates for the learning multiplier only when `adjusted_size > validation.position_size` (was `> request.contracts`: its real intent is "the multiplier inflated the approved size"). (4) No new setting; builders and `Signal` are untouched (a signal stays a one-lot description, `max_loss` per contract). Section 3: `risk/manager.py` (the operator confirms the diff before any merge).
**Tests fixed in advance.** A GOLDEN table generated from the CURRENT code before any edit (`tests/data/lot_request_golden.json`: condor / debit spread / no `max_loss`; NLV 5k / 25k / 200k; empty book / aggregate near the cap / same-symbol exposure / correlated cluster open / duplicate; VIX 16 / 27; confidence low / high): after the change it must reproduce with `scale_to_budget` False and with True at a cap of 1. Scaling cases at a cap of 3 (the rule's count; the aggregate cap trims 3 -> 2 -> 1; per-symbol cap; buying power; the N = 1 reject text equals the old one; haircut applies to N; no `max_loss` / undefined risk never scales; debit scales on the debit; `max_risk` = N x per-lot); orchestrator cases on the existing smoke rig (executor receives N; `trade_maxloss_*` and `capital_at_risk` are N x per-lot; no second validation at multiplier 1.0; the multiplier tests keep their shape); a mutation pass run with bytecode caching off (the W110 lesson).
**Out of scope here, in order.** 2b (before the cap is raised): `_check_partial_exit` skips multi-leg trades, multi-lot cases for the W101-B exit pricing and the W101-C expiry booking and the reconciler quantity checks, the staged paper ramp as an IB-paper probe run with the operator present. 3: the sizer receives `iv_rank` (the manager does not pass it today), research condor confidence from `gates_mode`, a research losing-days input, the multi-timeframe port spike; inert in live while the cap is 1. 4: budget-fitted widths for the spreads, live builders for the credit spreads; calendar has no builder anywhere.

## 2026-10-28 - W111 AS BUILT (Phase 2a): the live lot-request path; branch `w111-lot-request` (worktree `trade_v2_dev`), not merged; `positions.max_contracts_per_trade` stays 1, so live behaviour is unchanged

## 2026-10-28 - W112 AS PLANNED (Phase 2b): every post-entry path made correct at N lots, before `positions.max_contracts_per_trade` is ever raised; branch `w112-multi-lot-lifecycle` in the worktree `trade_v2_dev`, merged only on the operator's say-so

**Why.** W111 (merged) lets the risk manager approve N > 1 lots; the cap stays 1, so nothing below changes live behaviour today. An exploration of the entry, reconciliation, exit and booking paths found that entry order size, every full close (BAG size from `trade.quantity`), realized P&L, exit partial fills, the reconciler's quantity checks, expiry intrinsic booking and capital-at-risk restatement already scale with the quantity, and that the following gaps exist ONLY at N >= 2.
**Gaps and fixes (as designed).** (1) `portfolio._check_partial_exit` fires for any multi-leg position with quantity > 1, `orchestrator._execute_partial_exit` refuses multi-leg without recording the level, so the refusal repeats every cycle and the position drops out of the roll dispatch and thesis re-check (debit verticals reach it; condors almost never): the check will run for single-leg positions only, multi-leg positions are managed whole (as the research engine models them). (2) The commission true-up counts execution ROWS (`>= 2 x legs`), which entry rows alone can satisfy when a leg fills in several executions: completeness will be counted in contracts per leg. (3) Expiry booking from the broker's per-leg realizedPNL after earlier exit slices can count the slices twice: with slices, book the remaining quantity at intrinsic. (4) A fill recovered only from the executions ledger reports `units: 0.0` and so books the REQUESTED count: units will be computed from the ledger rows. (5) The placement-time `trade_maxloss_<id>` write can overwrite the fill-time restatement: write it only if the restatement has not landed. (6) A partially filled entry that is still working has no open-position row until the entry timeout (240 s): documented, not changed. (7) Leg ratios are ignored by the reconciler and the ledger units: documented as a 1:1 invariant.
**Tests fixed in advance.** `tests/test_multi_lot_lifecycle.py`: pins at N = 2 and 3 for the paths that are already right (entry and close BAG `totalQuantity`, P&L x N, expiry intrinsic x N, partial-fill booking, exit-slice fold, reconciler adoption and liveness, capital at risk x N); one failing-before / passing-after test per gap; the existing suites for these paths and the W111 golden table unchanged; a mutation pass over each fix (`python -B`, bytecode cleared).
**The IB-paper ramp.** `scripts/probe_multi_lot.py` (the W101 probe's guards and evidence pattern; quantity 2 or 3; SPY 3-wide condor; open N, close 1, close the rest; the bot stopped; writes nothing to `data/`) with its own script tests. Running it is the operator's scheduled step (it interrupts the paper bot for about 30 minutes) and its result is appended here; partial entry fills, stops, take-profits and expiry cannot be forced on paper and are covered by the unit tests.
**Section 3 files touched.** `execution/portfolio.py`, `execution/executor.py`, `execution/reconciler.py`: the diffs are shown to the operator before any merge.
**Not in scope.** Phase 3 (scalers) and Phase 4 (other structures, width choice that can target more than one lot).

## 2026-10-28 - W112 AS BUILT (Phase 2b): every post-entry path correct at N lots; branch `w112-multi-lot-lifecycle` (worktree `trade_v2_dev`), not merged; `positions.max_contracts_per_trade` stays 1

**AS BUILT, as planned.** (1) `execution/portfolio.py`: the partial-exit check runs only for single-leg positions (`contract_type` call / put); multi-leg positions are managed whole. (2) `bot/orchestrator.py` + `bot/state.py`: the commission true-up's completeness is counted in contracts per leg (`StateManager.sum_commissioned_shares`, an unsized row counts as one contract; expected = expected rows x lots traded, where lots traded = quantity on the row + quantity of exit slices, `_lots_traded`), used by both the booking-time true-up and the post-market settle through one helper, `_commission_ledger_complete`; the row test stays as a necessary condition. (3) `execution/reconciler.py`: an EXPIRED trade that carries exit slices is valued on the remaining quantity at the settlement value instead of the broker's per-leg realizedPNL sum (which covers the slices too; `close_trade` adds the slices). (4) `execution/executor.py`: a fill known only from the executions ledger reports its combo units (`_ledger_units`: the BAG rows, else the smallest leg total with every leg present, else 0.0 = unknown as before; `StateManager.executed_shares_by_con`). (5) `bot/orchestrator.py`: the placement-time `trade_maxloss_<id>` / `capital_at_risk` stamp is skipped when the fill's restatement already wrote `trades.capital_at_risk`. (6) Documented, not changed: a partially filled entry that is still working has no open-position row until the entry timeout; legs are 1:1 by invariant (GUIDE).

## 2026-10-28 - W115 AS PLANNED (Phase 3): the multi-timeframe analyzer ported into the research engine, so research confidence is "direction model + multi-timeframe boost - fractal penalty" as live; branch `w115-mtf-port` in the worktree `trade_v2_dev`, merged only on the operator's say-so; written BEFORE the first edit

**Merge status of the entries above.** W113 AS BUILT: merged as c85a105 (reaches the bot at its next restart). W114 AS BUILT: merged as 3b14607 (the shared scaler function; scalers off, one lot).
**Why.** The analyzer (`ait/data/multi_timeframe.py`, weekly + daily + 5-minute alignment) adds -0.10 to +0.15 to live's directional confidence (`orchestrator.py` ~2275, after the model, before the fractal penalty); only its `confidence_boost` is consumed. Research has no counterpart, so research directional confidence is lower in variance and differs from what live gates and sizes on; directional strategies stay off in research (`settings.py` ~303) until it is reproduced. The 5-minute bars cover the research windows (2023-10-12 to 2026-10-23; windows start 2024-01-01; W113 stops anything deleting them). Operator decision 2026-10-28: a FULL port in this phase.
**Design.** (1) In `engine.run`, right after `_get_direction(hist_dec)` and BEFORE the fractal penalty: `confidence = clamp01(confidence + boost)` for every strategy, as live does; it reaches the directional min-confidence / bearish gates, the meta-labeler's primary confidence, `entry_confidence` and the directional leg of the sizing confidence. (2) As-of rule: daily = the `hist_dec` tail (`MTF_DAILY_TAIL_ROWS = 100`, a fixed limit; a test proves the tail gives the same answer as the full frame); intraday = the 5-minute bars strictly BEFORE the scan time of day D (finished bars), from the last two sessions (day D alone has about 12 bars at 10:30, under the analyzer's 20-row minimum; live's 730-day frame includes the previous session). Scan time = the first bar in the entry window. Bars are loaded once per Backtester (`load_intraday_range(first - 7 days, last)`) and grouped by date. (3) Missing coverage: `analyze(daily, None)` (weekly + daily only), counted in a separate `mtf_coverage` counter on the result (the funnel's conservation invariant is untouched) and logged per window. (4) Switch `backtest.mtf_confidence_boost` (reader in `settings.py`, `gen_docs` row, `gate_parity` row): true in `config_research.yaml` (parity), false as the model default so config.yaml-driven tests keep their numbers. (5) Remaining live-vs-research confidence differences are recorded in `gate_parity.py`, not ported now: the regime direction override (live only), the neutral-only raw-confidence gate, the Friday 0.90 gate (after 14:30, short_strangle only; research decides at 10:30), the first-hour 0.85 gate, live's daily frame possibly including today's partial bar.
**Read first (open items).** Whether live's incremental intraday fetch (`market_data.get_intraday_since`) includes the bar still in progress (decides strict `<` vs `<=` at the cut-off); whether the first-hour gate's boundary includes 10:30; how `hist` is built in the live scan (does it include today's partial bar).
**Tests fixed in advance.** `tests/test_mtf_parity.py`: for many stored-bar dates and scan times, the engine's boost equals `MultiTimeframeAnalyzer.analyze(live inputs)` on every field (mutations: `<=` instead of `<`, day-D-only bars, boost applied after the fractal penalty must each fail); the engine imports the analyzer (no copy); fingerprints: switch off -> trades byte-identical to the end of W114; switch on with the gates in observe and no meta-labeler -> condor trades identical apart from `entry_confidence`; a timing check (under 5% of engine runtime on the fixture). Results that legitimately change with the switch on: runs with a trained meta-labeler, recorded `entry_confidence`, directional fixtures; each is listed in AS BUILT.
**Verification.** Targeted suites, mutation pass over the port, full fast lane (~35 min), `gen_docs --check`, `typecheck.py`; `smoke_deploy.py` in the live checkout after the merge. No file on the TECHNICAL_GUIDE section 3 list is expected to change (`engine.py`, `settings.py`, config and docs only).

## 2026-10-29 - W108 phase 3c AS PLANNED (pre-registration, written BEFORE the script exists or any run): do the sizing scalers help a multi-lot condor book? Branch `prithvi/w106-w108`; the RUN is on the Mac (the data)

**What the code already settles (`tests/test_w108_scalers_inert_for_condors.py`, the real engine builder, scalers ON, a scaler of 0.02).** Viability never changes. At the $5,000 simulated account every budget up to 20% builds one lot with or without scalers (the ceiling sets the wing; one lot risks most of the budget), so at the shipped `max_contracts_per_trade: 1` and at $5k the 3c question has no domain. On a large account the free width binds below the ceiling and the scaler DOES cut the count (3 and 7 lots -> 1 at $100k / 10% and 20%). The question is therefore only live for a large account with the lot cap raised: the Windows box ($198.7k, 3%, free width $21-59 below its ~$65 ceiling) if multi-lot is ever switched on.
**Question.** On a free-width-bound account with a lot cap above 1, does turning the condor's scalers on (`position_sizing.scaled_strategies: [iron_condor]`) improve risk-adjusted results against the unscaled budget-only count?
**Harness.** As `scripts/budget_ladder_study.py` (W109b): SPY / QQQ / IWM, iron_condor only, train 126 / test 63 / step 63 / gap 5, `train_window_models=False`, stored-IBKR-IV store, `use_research_config()` then `gates_mode="observe"`, per-leg friction fitted, entry DTE 18 and 25, `wing_k` config. Pool $200,000, budget 3% (the Windows box's live values). Script `scripts/scaler_arms_study.py`.
**Arms.** `unscaled_3` (lot cap 3, scalers off) = BASELINE; `scaled_3` (lot cap 3, scalers on) = CANDIDATE; `one_lot` (lot cap 1, scalers off) = reference; `scaled_1` (lot cap 1, scalers on) = SANITY.
**Wiring checks (VOID if any fails).** Friction model present for all three symbols; `scaled_1` identical to `one_lot` (n, net, PF, max DD); `unscaled_3` mean lots > 1.0 (the configuration exercises multi-lot); `scaled_3` mean lots < `unscaled_3` mean lots (the scaler throttles); `scaled_3` and `unscaled_3` have the same number of trades (scalers never change viability).
**Decision rule (fixed; not edited after any result).** `scaled_3` is SUPPORTED only if at BOTH DTE: (1) n >= 30; (2) max drawdown $ <= `unscaled_3`'s; (3) if `unscaled_3` net > 0: net / max DD $ >= 1.10 x `unscaled_3`'s; if `unscaled_3` net <= 0: `scaled_3` net > `unscaled_3` net; (4) `scaled_3` net > 0; (5) a repeat at `friction_stress_multiplier` 2.0 (both arms) still passes 2-4. Verdicts: SCALERS SUPPORTED FOR MULTI-LOT / NOT SUPPORTED (keep `scaled_strategies: []`) / VOID. `one_lot` is printed for context (W109 found multi-lot worse than its one-lot twin in every pair at $5k).
**Limits.** Black-Scholes + skew from stored daily IV, not quotes; 50-100 trades per arm; the absolute level is not trusted, read RELATIVE effects. A result licenses a config PROPOSAL (with the lot cap decision), never a live change; with `max_contracts_per_trade: 1` the scalers are inert in live whatever this says.
